cues.zh: 我认为，专有 AI 系统导致的权力集中，其危险远大于其他一切。
cues.en: I see the danger of this concentration of power through proprietary AI systems as a much bigger danger than everything else.

cues.zh: 对此持反对意见的人认为，出于安全考虑，我们应当把 AI 系统牢牢锁住，因为把它交到所有人手里太危险了。
cues.en: What works against this is people who think that for reasons of security, we should keep AI systems under lock and key because it’s too dangerous to put it in the hands of everybody.

cues.zh: 那会带来一个非常糟糕的未来：我们所有的信息摄取都被少数几家拥有专有系统的公司控制。
cues.en: That would lead to a very bad future in which all of our information diet is controlled by a small number of companies who proprietary systems.

cues.zh: 我相信人性本善，所以如果 AI，尤其是开源 AI 能让人变得更聪明，那只会激发人性中的善。
cues.en: I believe that people are fundamentally good, and so if AI, especially open source AI can make them smarter, it just empowers the goodness in humans.

cues.zh: 我也有同感。
cues.en: So I share that feeling.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 我认为人性本善，事实上，很多末日论者之所以是末日论者，正是因为他们不认为人性本善。
cues.en: I think people are fundamentally good and in fact, a lot of doomers are doomers because they don’t think that people are fundamentally good.

cues.zh: 这是与 Yann LeCun 的对话，他第三次做客本播客。
cues.en: The following is a conversation with Yann LeCun, his third time on this podcast.

cues.zh: 他是 Meta 的首席 AI 科学家、纽约大学教授、图灵奖得主，也是人工智能历史上的奠基性人物之一。
cues.en: He is the chief AI scientist at Meta, professor at NYU, Turing Award winner and one of the seminal figures in the history of artificial intelligence.

cues.zh: 他和 Meta AI 一直是开源和 AI 开发的大力支持者，并且言行一致，开源了他们许多最大的模型，包括 Llama 2，以及最终的 Llama 3。
cues.en: He and Meta AI have been big proponents of open sourcing, AI development and have been walking the walk by open sourcing many of their biggest models, including Llama 2 and eventually Llama 3.

cues.zh: 此外，Yann 一直直言不讳地批评 AI 社区中那些警告 AGI 即将带来危险和生存威胁的人。
cues.en: Also, Yann has been an outspoken critic of those people in the AI community who warn about the looming danger and existential threat of AGI.

cues.zh: 他相信 AGI 终有一天会被创造出来，但它会是好的。
cues.en: He believes the AGI will be created one day, but it will be good.

cues.zh: 它不会逃脱人类的控制，也不会主宰并杀死所有人类。
cues.en: It will not escape human control, nor will it dominate and kill all humans.

cues.zh: 在AI飞速发展的当下，这个立场其实颇具争议，所以看到Yann在网上参与了许多激烈而精彩的讨论，就像我们这次对话一样，挺有意思的。
cues.en: At this moment of rapid AI development, this happens to be somewhat a controversial position, and so it’s been fun seeing Yann get into a lot of intense and fascinating discussions online as we do in this very conversation.

cues.zh: 这是Lex Fridman播客。
cues.en: This is the Lex Fridman podcast.

cues.zh: 想支持的话，请看看简介里的赞助商。
cues.en: To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

cues.zh: 现在，亲爱的朋友们，有请Yann LeCun。
cues.en: And now, dear friends, here’s Yann LeCun.

cues.zh: 你整个职业生涯中对人工智能的未来发表过一些有力的、技术性的论断，最近你也说过，自回归LLM不是我们通往超人类智能的进步之路。
cues.en: You’ve had some strong statements, technical statements about the future of artificial intelligence throughout your career actually, but recently as well, you’ve said that autoregressive LLMs are not the way we’re going to make progress towards superhuman intelligence.

cues.zh: 这些就是像GPT-4、即将推出的Llama 2和3等等这样的大语言模型。
cues.en: These are the large language models like GPT-4, like Llama 2 and 3 soon and so on.

cues.zh: 它们如何运作，又为何无法带我们走到终点？
cues.en: How do they work and why are they not going to take us all the way?

cues.zh: 原因有很多。
cues.en: For a number of reasons.

cues.zh: 首先是智能行为有若干特征。
cues.en: The first is that there is a number of characteristics of intelligent behavior.

cues.zh: 比如理解世界的能力，理解物理世界，记忆和检索信息的能力，持久记忆，推理能力，以及规划能力。
cues.en: For example, the capacity to understand the world, understand the physical world, the ability to remember and retrieve things, persistent memory, the ability to reason, and the ability to plan.

cues.zh: 这是智能系统或实体——人类、动物——的四个基本特征。
cues.en: Those are four essential characteristics of intelligent systems or entities, humans, animals.

cues.zh: LLM 这些一个都做不到，或者只能以非常原始的方式做到，而且它们并不真正理解物理世界。
cues.en: LLMs can do none of those or they can only do them in a very primitive way and they don’t really understand the physical world.

cues.zh: 它们没有真正的持久记忆。
cues.en: They don’t really have persistent memory.

cues.zh: 它们无法真正推理，更谈不上规划。
cues.en: They can’t really reason and they certainly can’t plan.

cues.zh: 所以，如果你指望系统在不具备这些能力的情况下变得智能，那就错了。
cues.en: And so if you expect the system to become intelligent just without having the possibility of doing those things, you’re making a mistake.

cues.zh: 这并不是说自回归LLM没有用。
cues.en: That is not to say that autoregressive LLMs are not useful.

cues.zh: 它们当然有用，但并不是说它们有趣，也不是说我们无法围绕它们构建完整的应用生态。
cues.en: They’re certainly useful, that they’re not interesting, that we can’t build a whole ecosystem of applications around them.

cues.zh: 我们当然可以，但作为通往人类级智能的一步，它们缺少关键组件。
cues.en: Of course we can, but as a pass towards human-level intelligence, they’re missing essential components.

cues.zh: 然后还有一个我觉得非常有意思的小事实。
cues.en: And then there is another tidbit or fact that I think is very interesting.

cues.zh: 这些LLM是在海量文本上训练的，基本上就是互联网上所有公开可用文本的全部，对吧？
cues.en: Those LLMs are trained on enormous amounts of texts, basically, the entirety of all publicly available texts on the internet, right?

cues.zh: 这通常是10的13次方个token的量级。
cues.en: That’s typically on the order of 10 to the 13 tokens.

cues.zh: 每个token通常是两个字节，所以训练数据就是2乘以10的13次方个字节。
cues.en: Each token is typically two bytes, so that’s two 10 to the 13 bytes as training data.

cues.zh: 如果每天读八小时，你我要读完这些数据得花17万年。
cues.en: It would take you or me 170,000 years to just read through this at eight hours a day.

cues.zh: 所以这些系统似乎能积累海量知识，但随后你会发现数据其实没那么多。
cues.en: So it seems like an enormous amount of knowledge that those systems can accumulate, but then you realize it’s really not that much data.

cues.zh: 如果你和发育心理学家聊聊，他们会告诉你，一个四岁孩子醒着的时间累计有16000小时，而四年里到达这个孩子视觉皮层的信息量大约只有10到15字节。
cues.en: If you talk to developmental psychologists and they tell you a four-year-old has been awake for 16,000 hours in his or her life, and the amount of information that has reached the visual cortex of that child in four years is about 10 to 15 bytes.

cues.zh: 你可以这样算：视神经每秒大约传输20兆字节，所以四岁孩子是10的15次方字节，而17万年阅读量是2乘以10的13次方字节。
cues.en: And you can compute this by estimating that the optical nerve carry about 20 megabytes per second roughly, and so 10 to the 15 bytes for a four-year-old versus two times 10 to the 13 bytes for 170,000 years worth of reading.

cues.zh: 这说明，通过感官输入，我们看到的信息远比通过语言获得的多；而且尽管直觉相反，我们学到的大部分东西和大部分知识，都来自对真实世界的观察和互动，而不是语言。
cues.en: What that tells you is that through sensory input, we see a lot more information than we do through language, and that despite our intuition, most of what we learn and most of our knowledge is through our observation and interaction with the real world, not through language.

cues.zh: 我们在生命最初几年学到的一切，当然还有动物学到的一切，都和语言无关。
cues.en: Everything that we learn in the first few years of life, and certainly everything that animals learn has nothing to do with language.

cues.zh: 所以也许可以质疑一下你刚才说法背后的一些直觉。
cues.en: So it would be good to maybe push against some of the intuition behind what you’re saying.

cues.zh: 确实，进入人类大脑的数据量要多出好几个数量级，速度也快得多，而人类大脑能从中非常快地学习，非常快地过滤数据。
cues.en: So it is true there’s several orders of magnitude more data coming into the human mind much faster, and the human mind is able to learn very quickly from that, filter the data very quickly.

cues.zh: 有人可能会反驳你把感官数据和语言做的对比，说语言本身已经高度压缩了。
cues.en: Somebody might argue your comparison between sensory data versus language, that language is already very compressed.

cues.zh: 和视觉数据相比，语言所包含的信息量远远超过存储它所需的字节数。
cues.en: It already contains a lot more information than the bytes it takes to store them if you compare it to visual data.

cues.zh: 所以语言里蕴含着大量智慧。
cues.en: So there’s a lot of wisdom and language.

cues.zh: 有词语，还有我们把它们拼接起来的方式，本身就已经包含了很多信息。
cues.en: There’s words, and the way we stitch them together, it already contains a lot of information.

cues.zh: 那么，有没有可能语言本身已经蕴含了足够的智慧和知识，能够从中构建出一个世界模型和对世界的理解，一种对你所说的LLM所缺乏的物理世界的理解？
cues.en: So is it possible that language alone already has enough wisdom and knowledge in there to be able to, from that language, construct a world model and understanding of the world, an understanding of the physical world that you’re saying LLMs lack?

cues.zh: 所以哲学家和认知科学家之间有很大争论，比如智能是否需要扎根于现实。
cues.en: So it’s a big debate among philosophers and also cognitive scientists, like whether intelligence needs to be grounded in reality.

cues.zh: 我显然属于认为是的阵营：智能不可能在没有某种现实根基的情况下出现。
cues.en: I’m clearly in the camp that yes, intelligence cannot appear without some grounding in some reality.

cues.zh: 它不需要是物理现实。
cues.en: It doesn’t need to be physical reality.

cues.zh: 它可以是模拟的，但环境远比你能用语言表达的要丰富得多。
cues.en: It could be simulated, but the environment is just much richer than what you can express in language.

cues.zh: 语言是对感知和/或心智模型的一种非常近似的表征。
cues.en: Language is a very approximate representation or percepts and/or mental models.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，我们完成的很多任务都是在操作当前情境的心智模型，而这与语言毫无关系。
cues.en: I mean, there’s a lot of tasks that we accomplish where we manipulate a mental model of the situation at hand, and that has nothing to do with language.

cues.zh: 任何物理的、机械的东西，当我们建造某样东西、完成一项任务、比如抓取某物的模型任务等等，我们会规划动作序列，而我们做这件事本质上是通过想象一系列可能动作的结果，这需要与语言关系不大的心智模型，我认为我们的大部分知识都源自与物理世界的这种互动。
cues.en: Everything that’s physical, mechanical, whatever, when we build something, when we accomplish a task, model task of grabbing something, et cetera, we plan or action sequences, and we do this by essentially imagining the result of the outcome of a sequence of actions that we might imagine and that requires mental models that don’t have much to do with language, and I would argue most of our knowledge is derived from that interaction with the physical world.

cues.zh: 所以我很多对计算机视觉之类更感兴趣的同事，确实属于那个阵营，认为AI本质上需要具身化。
cues.en: So a lot of my colleagues who are more interested in things like computer vision are really on that camp that AI needs to be embodied essentially.

cues.zh: 而另一些来自NLP方向或出于其他动机的人则不一定同意这一点，哲学家们也有分歧，世界的复杂性很难想象。
cues.en: And then other people coming from the NLP side or maybe some other motivation don’t necessarily agree with that, and philosophers are split as well, and the complexity of the world is hard to imagine.

cues.zh: 现实世界中有很多我们习以为常的复杂事物，我们甚至不觉得它们需要智能，这些复杂性很难被表示出来，对吧？
cues.en: It’s hard to represent all the complexities that we take completely for granted in the real world that we don’t even imagine require intelligence, right?

cues.zh: 这就是机器人学先驱莫拉维克提出的经典莫拉维克悖论：为什么用计算机做下棋、解积分这类高层次复杂任务似乎很容易，而我们每天习以为常的事情，比如学开车或抓取物体，计算机却做不到？我们有能通过律师资格考试的大语言模型，所以它们一定很聪明，但它们却不能像任何17岁的人那样在20小时内学会开车，也不能像任何10岁孩子那样一次就学会收拾餐桌、把碗碟放进洗碗机。
cues.en: This is the old Moravec paradox, from the pioneer of robotics, hence Moravec, who said, how is it that with computers, it seems to be easy to do high-level complex tasks like playing chess and solving integrals and doing things like that, whereas the thing we take for granted that we do every day, like, I don’t know, learning to drive a car or grabbing an object, we can’t do with computers, and we have LLMs that can pass the bar exam, so they must be smart, but then they can’t learn to drive in 20 hours like any 17-year old, they can’t learn to clear out the dinner table and fill up the dishwasher like any 10-year old can learn in one shot.

cues.zh: 为什么会这样？
cues.en: Why is that?

cues.zh: 我们缺了什么？
cues.en: What are we missing?

cues.zh: 我们缺少哪种学习或推理架构之类的东西，正是它让我们无法在汽车和家用机器人上实现第五级自动驾驶？
cues.en: What type of learning or reasoning architecture or whatever are we missing that basically prevent us from having level five sort of in cars and domestic robots?

cues.zh: 大语言模型能否构建一个世界模型，它知道如何开车、知道如何装洗碗机，但只是目前还不知道如何处理视觉数据，从而能在概念空间中运作？
cues.en: Can a large language model construct a world model that does know how to drive and does know how to fill a dishwasher, but just doesn’t know how to deal with visual data at this time, so it can operate in a space of concepts?

cues.zh: 所以没错，这正是很多人在研究的方向。
cues.en: So yeah, that’s what a lot of people are working on.

cues.zh: 所以简短的回答是不行，而更复杂的回答是，你可以用各种技巧让大语言模型基本上消化图像、视频乃至音频的视觉表征。
cues.en: So the short answer is no, and the more complex answer is you can use all kinds of tricks to get an LLM to basically digest visual representations of images or video or audio for that matter.

cues.zh: 一种经典做法是以某种方式训练视觉系统，我们有多种训练视觉系统的方法——监督、半监督、自监督，各种不同的方式——能把任何图像转换成高层表征。
cues.en: And a classical way of doing this is you train a vision system in some way, and we have a number of ways to train vision systems either supervised, semi-supervised, self-supervised, all kinds of different ways, that will turn any image into a high-level representation.

cues.zh: 基本上就是一串与典型LLM输入非常相似的token列表。
cues.en: Basically a list of tokens that are really similar to the kind of tokens that typical LLM takes as an input.

cues.zh: 然后你把这些和文本一起喂给LLM，期望LLM在训练中能利用这些表示来帮助做决策。
cues.en: And then you just feed that to the LLM in addition to the text, and you just expect the LLM, during training, to be able to use those representations to help make decisions.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，沿着这个方向的研究已经持续很长时间了，现在你看到了那些系统。
cues.en: I mean, there’s been work along those lines for quite a long time and now, you see those systems.

cues.zh: 我是说有些LLM带有一些视觉扩展，但它们基本上是权宜之计，因为这些系统并没有被训练去真正理解世界。
cues.en: I mean there are LLMs that have some vision extension, but they’re basically hacks in the sense that those things are not trained to really understand the world.

cues.zh: 比如，它们没有用视频训练过。
cues.en: They’re not trained with video, for example.

cues.zh: 它们并不真正理解直觉物理，至少目前还不理解。
cues.en: They don’t really understand intuitive physics, at least not at the moment.

cues.zh: 所以你不认为直觉物理、对物理空间的常识推理、对物理现实的常识推理有什么特别之处。
cues.en: So you don’t think there’s something special to you about intuitive physics, about sort of common sense reasoning about the physical space, about physical reality.

cues.zh: 这对你来说是一个巨大的飞跃，而LLM就是做不到吗？
cues.en: That to you is a giant leap that LLMs are just not able to do?

cues.zh: 用我们今天正在使用的这类LLM，我们是做不到这一点的，原因有很多，但主要原因是LLM的训练方式：你取一段文本，去掉其中一些词，把它们遮住，用空白标记替换，然后训练一个神经网络来预测缺失的词。
cues.en: We’re not going to be able to do this with the type of LLMs that we are working with today, and there’s a number of reasons for this, but the main reason is the way LLMs are trained is that you take a piece of text, you remove some of the words in that text, you mask them, you replace them by blank markers, and you train a genetic neural net to predict the words that are missing.

cues.zh: 如果你以特定方式构建这个神经网络，使它只能看左边的词或它试图预测的那个词，那么你得到的就是一个基本上在尝试预测文本中下一个词的系统。
cues.en: And if you build this neural net in a particular way so that it can only look at words that are to the left or the one it’s trying to predict, then what you have is a system that basically is trying to predict the next word in a text.

cues.zh: 于是你可以喂给它一段文本、一个提示，然后让它预测下一个词。
cues.en: So then you can feed it a text, a prompt, and you can ask it to predict the next word.

cues.zh: 它永远无法精确预测下一个词。
cues.en: It can never predict the next word exactly.

cues.zh: 所以它的做法是，对词典中所有可能的词生成一个概率分布。
cues.en: So what it’s going to do is produce a probability distribution of all the possible words in a dictionary.

cues.zh: 事实上，它预测的不是词。
cues.en: In fact, it doesn’t predict words.

cues.zh: 它预测的是 token，也就是某种子词单元，因此处理预测中的不确定性很容易，因为词典中可能的词数量有限，你只需在它们之上计算一个分布。
cues.en: It predicts tokens that are kind of subword units, and so it’s easy to handle the uncertainty in the prediction there because there is only a finite number of possible words in the dictionary, and you can just compute a distribution over them.

cues.zh: 然后系统的做法是，从这个分布中挑选一个词。
cues.en: Then what the system does is that it picks a word from that distribution.

cues.zh: 当然，在分布中概率更高的词被选中的机会更大。
cues.en: Of course, there’s a higher chance of picking words that have a higher probability within that distribution.

cues.zh: 所以你从这个分布中采样，真正生成一个词，然后把这个词移入输入，这样系统就能预测第二个词，一旦这样做，你再把它移入输入，以此类推。
cues.en: So you sample from that distribution to actually produce a word, and then you shift that word into the input, and so that allows the system not to predict the second word, and once you do this, you shift it into the input, et cetera.

cues.zh: 这叫自回归预测，所以那些大语言模型应该叫自回归大语言模型，但我们通常就叫它们大语言模型。这种过程和另一种过程有区别——在生成一个词之前……你和我说话时，你和我都是双语者，我们会思考要说什么，而这跟我们打算用哪种语言说相对无关。
cues.en: That’s called autoregressive prediction, which is why those LLMs should be called autoregressive LLMs, but we just call them LLMs, and there is a difference between this kind of process and a process by which before producing a word… When you and I talk, you and I are bilingual, we think about what we’re going to say, and it’s relatively independent of the language in which we’re going to say.

cues.zh: 当我们谈论，比如说，一个数学概念之类的，我们所进行的那种思考、我们计划给出的答案，并不取决于我们是用法语、俄语还是英语来表达它。
cues.en: When we talk about, I don’t know, let’s say a mathematical concept or something, the kind of thinking that we’re doing and the answer that we’re planning to produce is not linked to whether we’re going to see it in French or Russian or English.

cues.zh: Chomsky 翻了个白眼，但我理解，所以你是说在语言之前有一个更大的抽象，然后映射到语言上？
cues.en: Chomsky just rolled his eyes, but I understand, so you’re saying that there’s a bigger abstraction that goes before language and maps onto language?

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 我们做的很多思考确实如此。
cues.en: It’s certainly true for a lot of thinking that we do.

cues.zh: 这很明显吗，我们不……你是说你的思考在法语和英语里是一样的？
cues.en: Is that obvious that we don’t… You’re saying your thinking is same in French as it is in English?

cues.zh: 是的，差不多。
cues.en: Yeah, pretty much.

cues.zh: 差不多，还是说如果存在概率分布，你的灵活性有多大？
cues.en: Pretty much or how flexible are you if there’s a probability distribution?

cues.zh: 嗯，这取决于哪种思考，对吧？
cues.en: Well, it depends what kind of thinking, right?

cues.zh: 如果是造双关语，我在法语上比英语好得多，或者差得多。
cues.en: If it’s producing puns, I get much better in French than English about that, or much worse.

cues.zh: 双关语有抽象表征吗？
cues.en: Is there an abstract representation of puns?

cues.zh: 你的幽默是抽象的……当你发推文，你的推文有时有点辛辣，在映射到英语之前，你大脑里推文有抽象表征吗？
cues.en: Is your humor an abstract… When you tweet and your tweets are sometimes a little bit spicy, is there an abstract representation in your brain of a tweet before it maps onto English?

cues.zh: 有一种抽象表征，就是想象读者对那段文字的反应。
cues.en: There is an abstract representation of imagining the reaction of a reader to that text.

cues.zh: 还是你先笑，然后再想办法让它发生？
cues.en: Or you start with laughter and then figure out how to make that happen?

cues.zh: 或者想清楚你想引发什么反应，再琢磨怎么说才能引发那种反应。
cues.en: Or figure out like a reaction you want to cause and then figure out how to say it so that it causes that reaction.

cues.zh: 但这其实已经很接近语言了。
cues.en: But that’s really close to language.

cues.zh: 但想想一个数学概念，或者想象用木头做某个东西之类的。
cues.en: But think about a mathematical concept or imagining something you want to build out of wood or something like this.

cues.zh: 你进行的这种思考，其实和语言毫无关系。
cues.en: The kind of thinking you’re doing has absolutely nothing to do with language really.

cues.zh: 并不是说你一定在用某种特定语言进行内心独白。
cues.en: It’s not like you have necessarily an internal monologue in any particular language.

cues.zh: 你是在想象这件事的心理模型。
cues.en: You are imagining mental models of the thing.

cues.zh: 我是说，如果我让你想象这个水瓶旋转90度后是什么样子，那和语言毫无关系。
cues.en: I mean, if I ask you to imagine what this water bottle will look like if I rotate it 90 degrees, that has nothing to do with language.

cues.zh: 所以很明显，存在一个更抽象的表示层次，我们的大部分思考都在这个层次进行；如果输出是说出来的话，而不是肌肉动作，我们会先计划好要说什么，在产出答案之前先规划好。
cues.en: And so clearly, there is a more abstract level of representation in which we do most of our thinking, and we plan what we’re going to say if the output is uttered words as opposed to an output being muscle actions, we plan our answer before we produce it.

cues.zh: LLM 不是这样做的。
cues.en: LLMs don’t do that.

cues.zh: 它们只是一个词接一个词地本能输出，如果你愿意这么说的话。
cues.en: They just produce one word after the other instinctively if you want.

cues.zh: 这有点像潜意识行为——你分心了，你在做某件事，完全专注，有人过来问你一个问题，你就随口回答了。
cues.en: It’s a bit like the subconscious actions where you’re distracted, you’re doing something, you’re completely concentrated, and someone comes to you and asks you a question and you kind of answer the question.

cues.zh: 你没时间思考答案，但答案很简单。
cues.en: You don’t have time to think about the answer, but the answer is easy.

cues.zh: 所以你不需要特别注意。
cues.en: So you don’t need to pay attention.

cues.zh: 你有点像是自动回应。
cues.en: You sort of respond automatically.

cues.zh: LLM 差不多就是这样。
cues.en: That’s kind of what an LLM does.

cues.zh: 它并不会真正思考自己的答案。
cues.en: It doesn’t think about its answer really.

cues.zh: 它是检索出来的，因为它积累了大量知识。
cues.en: It retrieves it because it’s accumulated a lot of knowledge.

cues.zh: 所以它能检索出一些东西，但它就是一个 token 接一个 token 地吐出来，并不规划答案。
cues.en: So it can retrieve some things, but it’s going to just spit out one token after the other without planning the answer.

cues.zh: 但你把它说得好像只是一个 token 接一个 token 而已。
cues.en: But you’re making it sound just one token after the other.

cues.zh: 一次生成一个 token 必然很简单，但如果世界模型足够复杂，那么一次一个 token、它最可能生成的 token 序列，就会是一件极其深刻的东西。
cues.en: One token at a time generation is bound to be simplistic, but if the world model is sufficiently sophisticated that one token at a time, the most likely thing it generates is a sequence of tokens is going to be a deeply profound thing.

cues.zh: 但这假设了那些系统真的拥有一个永恒的世界模型。
cues.en: But then that assumes that those systems actually possess an eternal world model.

cues.zh: 所以这真的归结到……我认为根本问题是，你能否构建一个真正完整的世界模型，不是完整，而是对世界有深刻理解的那种？
cues.en: So really goes to the… I think the fundamental question is can you build a really complete world model, not complete, but one that has a deep understanding of the world?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 那么，首先你能通过预测来构建它吗？答案很可能是肯定的。
cues.en: So can you build this first of all by prediction, and the answer is probably yes.

cues.zh: 你能通过预测词语来构建它吗？
cues.en: Can you build it by predicting words?

cues.zh: 答案很可能是不能，因为语言的信息量非常贫乏，可以说是低带宽，那里根本没有足够的信息。
cues.en: And the answer is most probably no, because language is very poor in terms of weak or low bandwidth if you want, there’s just not enough information there.

cues.zh: 所以构建世界模型意味着观察世界，理解世界为何如此演化，而世界模型额外的一个组成部分，是能够预测世界将如何因你可能采取的行动而演化。
cues.en: So building world models means observing the world and understanding why the world is evolving the way it is, and then the extra component of a world model is something that can predict how the world is going to evolve as a consequence of an action you might take.

cues.zh: 所以一个模型其实就是：这是我在时刻T对世界状态的判断，这是我也许会采取的行动。
cues.en: So one model really is here is my idea of the state of the world at time, T, here is an action I might take.

cues.zh: 在时刻T+1，世界被预测的状态是什么？
cues.en: What is the predicted state of the world at time, T+1?

cues.zh: 这个世界的状态不需要表示世界的一切，只需要表示与行动规划相关的足够信息，但不一定需要所有细节。
cues.en: Now that state of the world does not need to represent everything about the world, it just needs to represent enough that’s relevant for this planning of the action, but not necessarily all the details.

cues.zh: 现在，问题来了。
cues.en: Now, here is the problem.

cues.zh: 你没法用生成模型做到这一点。
cues.en: You’re not going to be able to do this with generative models.

cues.zh: 所以生成模型已经在视频上训练过了，我们尝试做这件事已经十年了，你拿一段视频，给系统看一段视频，然后让它预测视频剩下的部分，基本上就是预测接下来会发生什么。
cues.en: So a generative model has trained on video, and we’ve tried to do this for 10 years, you take a video, show a system, a piece of video, and then ask you to predict the reminder of the video, basically predict what’s going to happen.

cues.zh: 一次一帧，做和自回归LLM一样的事，只不过换成视频。
cues.en: One frame at a time, do the same thing as the autoregressive LLMs do, but for video.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 要么一次一帧——
cues.en: Either one frame at a time-

cues.zh: LVM。
cues.en: LVMs.

cues.zh: ……要么一次一组帧。
cues.en: … or a group of frames at a time.

cues.zh: 不过也可以说，就是大型视频模型。
cues.en: But yeah, a large video model if you want.

cues.zh: 做这件事的想法已经流传很久了，在FAIR，我和一些同事尝试做这个大约有十年了，但你没法真的照搬LLM那套做法，因为LLM，就像我说的，你没法准确预测一个词序列后面具体会跟哪个词，但你可以预测词的分布。
cues.en: The idea of doing this has been floating around for a long time and at FAIR, some of our colleagues and I have been trying to do this for about 10 years, and you can’t really do the same trick as with LLMs because LLMs, as I said, you can’t predict exactly which word is going to follow a sequence of words, but you can predict the distribution of words.

cues.zh: 现在，如果转向视频，你需要做的是预测视频中所有可能帧的分布，而我们其实并不知道如何妥善地做到这一点。
cues.en: Now, if you go to video, what you would have to do is predict the distribution of all possible frames in a video, and we don’t really know how to do that properly.

cues.zh: 我们不知道如何以有用的方式来表示高维连续空间上的分布。
cues.en: We do not know how to represent distributions over high-dimensional, continuous spaces in ways that are useful.

cues.zh: 主要问题就在这里，而我们之所以能做到这一点，是因为世界在信息层面比文本要复杂和丰富得多。
cues.en: And there lies the main issue, and the reason we can do this is because the world is incredibly more complicated and richer in terms of information than text.

cues.zh: 文本是离散的，视频是高维且连续的。
cues.en: Text is discrete, video is high-dimensional and continuous.

cues.zh: 这里面有很多细节。
cues.en: A lot of details in this.

cues.zh: 所以如果我拍一段这个房间的视频，镜头在四周平移，我不可能预测出镜头平移时房间里会出现的一切。
cues.en: So if I take a video of this room and the video is a camera panning around, there is no way I can predict everything that’s going to be in the room as I pan around.

cues.zh: 系统无法预测镜头平移时房间里会出现什么。
cues.en: The system cannot predict what’s going to be in the room as the camera is panning.

cues.zh: 也许它能预测出这是个有灯、有墙的房间之类的。
cues.en: Maybe it’s going to predict this is a room where there’s a light and there is a wall and things like that.

cues.zh: 但它没法预测墙上的画长什么样，或者沙发的质感是什么样的。
cues.en: It can’t predict what the painting of the wall looks like or what the texture of the couch looks like.

cues.zh: 更别说地毯的质感了。
cues.en: Certainly not the texture of the carpet.

cues.zh: 所以我没办法预测所有这些细节。
cues.en: So there’s no way I can predict all those details.

cues.zh: 所以一种可能处理这个问题的方法，也是我们长期在做的，就是用一个带有所谓隐变量的模型。
cues.en: So one way to possibly handle this, which we’ve been working for a long time, is to have a model that has what’s called a latent variable.

cues.zh: 隐变量被输入到神经网络中，它应该表示所有你尚未感知到的、关于这个世界的信息，你需要用它来增强系统，让预测能更好地预测像素，包括地毯、沙发和墙上画作的精细质感。
cues.en: And the latent variable is fed to a neural net, and it’s supposed to represent all the information about the world that you don’t perceive yet, and that you need to augment the system for the prediction to do a good job at predicting pixels, including the fine texture of the carpet and the couch and the painting on the wall.

cues.zh: 这基本上彻底失败了。
cues.en: That has been a complete failure essentially.

cues.zh: 我们试过很多方法。
cues.en: And we’ve tried lots of things.

cues.zh: 我们试过纯神经网络，试过 GAN，试过 VAE，还有各种正则化自编码器。
cues.en: We tried just straight neural nets, we tried GANs, we tried VAEs, all kinds of regularized auto encoders.

cues.zh: 我们试了很多。
cues.en: We tried many things.

cues.zh: 我们还试过用这类方法学习图像或视频的良好表征，以便之后作为输入，用于图像分类系统等。
cues.en: We also tried those kinds of methods to learn good representations of images or video that could then be used as input to, for example, an image classification system.

cues.zh: 这也基本失败了。
cues.en: That also has basically failed.

cues.zh: 所有试图从损坏版本的图像或视频中预测缺失部分的系统，基本上都是这样：拿一张图像或一段视频，以某种方式损坏或变换它，然后尝试从损坏版本重建完整的视频或图像，并希望系统内部能发展出良好的图像表征，可用于物体识别、分割等等。
cues.en: All the systems that attempt to predict missing parts of an image or video from a corrupted version of it, basically, so take an image or a video, corrupt it or transform it in some way, and then try to reconstruct the complete video or image from the corrupted version, and then hope that internally, the system will develop good representations of images that you can use for object recognition, segmentation, whatever it is.

cues.zh: 这基本上是完全失败了，但对文本却非常有效。
cues.en: That has been essentially a complete failure and it works really well for text.

cues.zh: 这就是LLM采用的原理，对吧？
cues.en: That’s the principle that is used for LLMs, right?

cues.zh: 那失败到底在哪里？
cues.en: So where’s the failure exactly?

cues.zh: 是不是很难形成图像的好的表示，比如把图像中所有重要信息做好的嵌入？
cues.en: Is it that it’s very difficult to form a good representation of an image, like a good embedding of all the important information in the image?

cues.zh: 是不是在图像与图像之间的一致性上，也就是构成视频的那种图像与图像之间的一致性？
cues.en: Is it in terms of the consistency of image to image, to image to image that forms the video?

cues.zh: 如果我们做一个集锦，把你失败的所有方式都放进去，那会是什么样？
cues.en: If we do a highlight reel of all the ways you failed, what’s that look like?

cues.zh: 好，所以这行不通的原因是，首先我得告诉你到底是什么行不通，因为还有别的东西是行得通的。
cues.en: Okay, so the reason this doesn’t work is first of all, I have to tell you exactly what doesn’t work because there is something else that does work.

cues.zh: 所以行不通的是，通过训练系统从损坏版本的图像中重建出好的图像，来学习图像的表示，明白吗？
cues.en: So the thing that does not work is training the system to learn representations of images by training it to reconstruct a good image from a corrupted version of it, okay?

cues.zh: 这就是行不通的地方。
cues.en: That’s what doesn’t work.

cues.zh: 为此我们有一整套技术，都是去噪自编码器的变体，其中一种叫 MAE，是我在 FAIR 的同事开发的，即掩码自编码器。
cues.en: And we have a whole slew of techniques for this that are variant of denoising autoencoders, something called MAE developed by some of my colleagues at FAIR, masked autoencoder.

cues.zh: 所以基本上就像 LLM 之类的做法，你通过破坏文本来训练系统，只不过这里破坏的是图像，从中移除一些图块，然后训练一个巨大的神经网络来重建。
cues.en: So it’s basically like the LLMs or things like this where you train the system by corrupting texts except you corrupt images, you remove patches from it, and you train a gigantic neural network reconstruct.

cues.zh: 你得到的特征并不好，而且你知道它们不好，因为如果你现在训练同样的架构，但用标注数据、图像的文本描述等来做监督训练，你确实能得到好的表征，识别任务上的表现也比做这种自监督再训练要好得多。
cues.en: The features you get are not good, and you know they’re not good because if you now train the same architecture, but you train it to supervise with label data, with textual descriptions of images, et cetera, you do get good representations and the performance on recognition tasks is much better than if you do this self-supervised retraining.

cues.zh: 这个架构好吗？
cues.en: The architecture is good?

cues.zh: 这个架构不错，编码器的架构很好，但你训练系统去重建图像，这并不会让它产生长期、良好的图像通用特征。
cues.en: The architecture is good, the architecture of the encoder is good, but the fact that you train the system to reconstruct images does not lead it to produce to long, good generic features of images.

cues.zh: 当你用自监督的方式训练时呢？
cues.en: When you train in a self-supervised way?

cues.zh: 通过重建进行自监督。
cues.en: Self-supervised by reconstruction.

cues.zh: 对，通过重建。
cues.en: Yeah, by reconstruction.

cues.zh: 好，那替代方案是什么？
cues.en: Okay, so what’s the alternative?

cues.zh: 替代方案是联合嵌入。
cues.en: The alternative is joint embedding.

cues.zh: 什么是联合嵌入？
cues.en: What is joint embedding?

cues.zh: 你如此兴奋的这些架构是什么？
cues.en: What are these architectures that you’re so excited about?

cues.zh: 好，现在不再是训练系统编码图像，然后训练它从损坏版本重建完整图像，而是取完整图像，取损坏或变换后的版本，把两者都通过编码器，这些编码器通常相同，但不一定。
cues.en: Okay, so now instead of training a system to encode the image and then training it to reconstruct the full image from a corrupted version, you take the full image, you take the corrupted or transformed version, you run them both through encoders, which in general, are identical, but not necessarily.

cues.zh: 然后你在这些编码器之上训练一个预测器，从损坏版本的表示来预测完整输入的表示。
cues.en: And then you train a predictor on top of those encoders to predict the representation of the full input from the representation of the corrupted one.

cues.zh: 所以叫联合嵌入，因为你把完整输入和损坏或变换后的版本都送进编码器，得到一个联合嵌入，然后你问：我能不能从损坏版本的表示预测出完整版本的表示？
cues.en: So joint embedding, because you’re taking the full input and the corrupted version or transformed version, run them both through encoders, you get a joint embedding, and then you’re saying, can I predict the representation of the full one from the representation of the corrupted one?

cues.zh: 我把这个叫做 JEPA，也就是联合嵌入预测架构，因为这里有联合嵌入，还有一个预测器，从“坏家伙”的表示预测“好家伙”的表示。
cues.en: And I call this a JEPA, so that means joint embedding predictive architecture because this joint embedding and there is this predictor that predicts the representation of the good guy from the bad guy.

cues.zh: 最大的问题是，怎么训练这样的东西？
cues.en: And the big question is how do you train something like this?

cues.zh: 直到五六年前，我们对如何训练这类东西都没有特别好的答案，除了一个叫对比学习的方法。对比学习的思路是，你取一对图像——同样是一张图像和它某种损坏、退化或变换后的版本——然后训练预测出的表示与它保持一致。
cues.en: And until five years ago or six years ago, we didn’t have particularly good answers for how you train those things except for one, called contrastive learning, where the idea of contrastive learning is you take a pair of images that are, again, an image and a corrupted version or degraded version somehow or transformed version of the original one, and you train the predicted representation to be the same as that.

cues.zh: 如果你只做到这一步，这个系统就会崩溃。
cues.en: If you only do this, this system collapses.

cues.zh: 它基本上完全忽略输入，生成恒定不变的表示。
cues.en: It basically completely ignores the input and produces representations that are constant.

cues.zh: 对比方法避免了这个问题，这类方法早在90年代初就出现了，我在1993年就有一篇相关论文，就是你也展示已知不同的图像对，然后把它们的表示互相推开。
cues.en: So the contrastive methods avoid this, and those things have been around since the early ’90s, I had a paper on this in 1993, is you also show pairs of images that you know are different, and then you push away the representations from each other.

cues.zh: 也就是说，不仅已知相同事物的表示应该相同或相似，而且已知不同事物的表示也应该不同。
cues.en: So you say, not only do representations of things that we know are the same should be the same or should be similar, but representation of things that we know are different should be different.

cues.zh: 这能防止崩溃，但有一些局限。
cues.en: And that prevents the collapse, but it has some limitation.

cues.zh: 过去六七年里出现了一大堆技术，能让这类方法重新焕发生机，有些来自FAIR，有些来自Google和其他地方，但这些对比方法都有局限。
cues.en: And there’s a whole bunch of techniques that have appeared over the last six, seven years that can revive this type of method, some of them from FAIR, some of them from Google and other places, but there are limitations to those contrastive methods.

cues.zh: 过去三四年发生的变化是，我们现在有了非对比式的方法。
cues.en: What has changed in the last three, four years is now we have methods that are non-contrastive.

cues.zh: 所以它们不需要那些我们知道不同的负对比图像样本。
cues.en: So they don’t require those negative contrastive samples of images that we know are different.

cues.zh: 你把同一事物的不同版本或不同视角的图像输入进去，然后依靠一些其他技巧来防止系统崩溃。
cues.en: You turn them on you with images that are different versions or different views of the same thing, and you rely on some other tricks to prevent the system from collapsing.

cues.zh: 我们现在有六种不同的方法可以做到这一点。
cues.en: And we have half a dozen different methods for this now.

cues.zh: 那么，联合嵌入架构和LLM之间的根本区别是什么？
cues.en: So what is the fundamental difference between joint embedding architectures and LLMs?

cues.zh: JEPA能带我们走向AGI吗？
cues.en: Can JEPA take us to AGI?

cues.zh: 我们是否应该说你不喜欢AGI这个词，而且我们大概会争论——我想每次和你交谈，我们都争论过AGI里的G。
cues.en: Whether we should say that you don’t like the term AGI, and we’ll probably argue I think every single time I’ve talked to you, we’ve argued about the G in AGI.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 我明白。
cues.en: I get it.

cues.zh: 我明白。
cues.en: I get it.

cues.zh: 嗯，我们可能还会继续争论这个问题。
cues.en: Well, we’ll probably continue to argue about it.

cues.zh: 这很棒。
cues.en: It’s great.

cues.zh: 你喜欢 AMI，是因为你喜欢法语，而 ami 在法语里是朋友的意思，而 AMI 代表高级机器智能。
cues.en: You like AMI because you like French and ami is friend in French, and AMI stands for advanced machine intelligence.

cues.zh: 但不管怎样，JEPA 能带我们走向那个高级机器智能吗？
cues.en: But either way, can JEPA take us to that towards that advanced machine intelligence?

cues.zh: 嗯，所以这是第一步。
cues.en: Well, so it’s a first step.

cues.zh: 好，那么首先，它和 LLMs 这类生成式架构有什么区别？
cues.en: Okay, so first of all, what’s the difference with generative architectures like LLMs?

cues.zh: LLMs 或通过重建训练的视觉系统会生成输入。
cues.en: So LLMs or vision systems that are trained by reconstruction generate the inputs.

cues.zh: 它们生成原始输入，也就是未损坏、未变换的输入，所以你必须预测所有像素，系统要花费大量资源来实际预测所有这些像素和所有细节。
cues.en: They generate the original input that is non-corrupted, non-transformed, so you have to predict all the pixels, and there is a huge amount of resources spent in the system to actually predict all those pixels, all the details.

cues.zh: 在 JEPA 中，你并不试图预测所有像素，你只试图预测输入的抽象表示。
cues.en: In a JEPA, you’re not trying to predict all the pixels, you’re only trying to predict an abstract representation of the inputs.

cues.zh: 这在很多方面要容易得多。
cues.en: And that’s much easier in many ways.

cues.zh: 所以JEPA系统在训练时，试图做的是从输入中提取尽可能多的信息，但只提取那些相对容易预测的信息。
cues.en: So what the JEPA system, when it’s being trained, is trying to do is extract as much information as possible from the input, but yet only extract information that is relatively easily predictable.

cues.zh: 世界上有很多事情是我们无法预测的。
cues.en: So there’s a lot of things in the world that we cannot predict.

cues.zh: 比如，如果你有一辆自动驾驶汽车在街道或公路上行驶，路周围可能有树木，而且可能是个大风天。
cues.en: For example, if you have a self-driving car driving down the street or road, there may be trees around the road and it could be a windy day.

cues.zh: 所以树上的叶子会以某种半混沌、随机的方式移动，你无法预测，也不在乎，你不想去预测。
cues.en: So the leaves on the tree are kind moving in kind semi-chaotic, random ways that you can’t predict and you don’t care, you don’t want to predict.

cues.zh: 所以你希望你的编码器基本上消除所有这些细节。
cues.en: So what you want is your encoder to basically eliminate all those details.

cues.zh: 它会告诉你叶子在动，但不会给出具体发生了什么细节。
cues.en: It’ll tell you there’s moving leaves, but it’s not going to give the details of exactly what’s going on.

cues.zh: 所以当你在表征空间里做预测时，就不必预测每片叶子的每一个像素。
cues.en: And so when you do the prediction in representation space, you’re not going to have to predict every single pixel of every leaf.

cues.zh: 这不仅简单得多，还让系统本质上能学到世界的抽象表征：可建模、可预测的部分被保留，其余部分被视为噪声，由编码器剔除。
cues.en: And that not only is a lot simpler, but also, it allows the system to essentially learn an abstract representation of the world where what can be modeled and predicted is preserved and the rest is viewed as noise and eliminated by the encoder.

cues.zh: 所以它提升了表征的抽象层次。
cues.en: So it lifts the level of abstraction of the representation.

cues.zh: 想想看，这是我们一直在做的事。
cues.en: If you think about this, this is something we do absolutely all the time.

cues.zh: 每当我们描述一个现象，都是在某个特定的抽象层次上描述它。
cues.en: Whenever we describe a phenomenon, we describe it at a particular level of abstraction.

cues.zh: 我们不会总用量子场论去描述每一个自然现象。
cues.en: We don’t always describe every natural phenomenon in terms of quantum field theory.

cues.zh: 那是不可能的。
cues.en: That would be impossible.

cues.zh: 所以我们有多个抽象层次来描述世界上发生的事，从量子场论，到原子理论和分子、化学、材料，一直到现实世界中的具体物体等等。
cues.en: So we have multiple levels of abstraction to describe what happens in the world, starting from quantum field theory, to atomic theory and molecules and chemistry, materials and all the way up to concrete objects in the real world and things like that.

cues.zh: 所以我们不能只在最低层级上对所有事物建模。
cues.en: So we can’t just only model everything at the lowest level.

cues.zh: 这就是 JEPA 理念的核心所在：以自监督方式学习抽象表征，而且还可以分层来做。
cues.en: And that’s what the idea of JEPA is really about, learn abstract representation in a self-supervised manner, and you can do it hierarchically as well.

cues.zh: 所以我认为，这是智能系统的一个关键组成部分。
cues.en: So that, I think, is an essential component of an intelligent system.

cues.zh: 而在语言领域，我们可以绕开这一步，因为语言本身已经具有一定程度的抽象，并且已经剔除了大量不可预测的信息。
cues.en: And in language, we can get away without doing this because language is already to some level abstract and already has eliminated a lot of information that is not predictable.

cues.zh: 因此我们可以不做联合嵌入，不提升抽象层级，直接预测词语就行。
cues.en: And so we can get away without doing the joint embedding, without lifting the abstraction level and by directly predicting words.

cues.zh: 所以联合嵌入仍然是生成式的，只不过是在这个抽象表征空间里生成？
cues.en: So joint embedding, it’s still generative, but it’s generative in this abstract representation space?

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 而你的意思是，在语言上我们其实偷了懒，因为抽象表征是白送的，现在我们必须把视野拉远，真正去思考通用智能系统。
cues.en: And you’re saying language, we were lazy with language because we already got the abstract representation for free, and now we have to zoom out, actually think about generally intelligent systems.

cues.zh: 我们得应对纷繁复杂的物理现实，也就是现实本身。
cues.en: We have to deal with a full mess of physical reality, of reality.

cues.zh: 你确实得完成这一步：从完整、丰富、详尽的现实，跳跃到基于你后续能推理的内容等所构建的现实的抽象表示。
cues.en: And you do have to do this step of jumping from the full, rich, detailed reality to a abstract representation of that reality based on what you can then reason and all that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 关键在于，那些通过预测来学习的自监督算法，即便在表示空间中，如果你喂给它们的输入数据冗余度更高，它们就能学到更多概念。
cues.en: And the thing is those self-supervised algorithm that learn by prediction, even in representation space, they learn more concept if the input data you feed them is more redundant.

cues.zh: 数据中的冗余越多，它们就越能捕捉到其中的某些内部结构。
cues.en: The more redundancy there is in the data, the more they’re able to capture some internal structure of it.

cues.zh: 因此，感知输入（如视觉这类感官输入）的结构中冗余远多于文本，而文本的冗余度则低得多。
cues.en: And so there is way more redundancy in the structure in perceptual inputs, sensory input like vision than there is in text, which is not nearly as redundant.

cues.zh: 这又回到了你几分钟前问的问题。
cues.en: This is back to the question you were asking a few minutes ago.

cues.zh: 语言可能承载更多信息，因为它已经被压缩过了。
cues.en: Language might represent more information really, because it’s already compressed.

cues.zh: 你说得对，但这也意味着它的冗余更少，所以自监督的效果不会那么好。
cues.en: You’re right about that, but that means it’s also less redundant, and so self-supervision, you will not work as well.

cues.zh: 有没有可能把视觉数据的自监督训练和语言数据的自监督训练结合起来？
cues.en: Is it possible to join the self-supervised training on visual data and self-supervised training on language data?

cues.zh: 那里有海量的知识，尽管你贬低那10的13次方个token。
cues.en: There is a huge amount of knowledge, even though you talk down about those 10 to the 13 tokens.

cues.zh: 那10的13次方个token代表了全部——
cues.en: Those 10 to the 13 tokens represent the entirety-

cues.zh: 那10的13次方个token代表了全部，代表了人类已经弄明白的很大一部分内容，既有Reddit上的胡扯，也有所有书籍、文章的内容，以及人类智力创造的全谱系。
cues.en: Those 10 to the 13 tokens represent the entirety, a large fraction of what us humans have figured out, both the shit-talk on Reddit and the contents of all the books and the articles and the full spectrum of human intellectual creation.

cues.zh: 那么有没有可能把这两者结合起来？
cues.en: So is it possible to join those two together?

cues.zh: 嗯，最终会的。
cues.en: Well, eventually, yes.

cues.zh: 但我觉得如果做得太早，就有作弊的风险。
cues.en: But I think if we do this too early, we run the risk of being tempted to cheat.

cues.zh: 事实上，现在人们在视觉语言模型上就是这么做的。
cues.en: And in fact, that’s what people are doing at the moment with vision-language model.

cues.zh: 我们基本上是在作弊。
cues.en: We’re basically cheating.

cues.zh: 我们在用语言当拐杖，弥补视觉系统的不足，帮它从图像和视频中学到好的表征。
cues.en: We’re using language as a crutch to help the deficiencies of our vision systems to learn good representations from images and video.

cues.zh: 问题在于，给语言模型喂图像也许能改进它，但我们达不到猫或狗那种对世界的智能和理解水平，而它们并没有语言。
cues.en: And the problem with this is that we might improve our language models by feeding them images, but we’re not going to get to the level of even the intelligence or level of understanding of the world of a cat or a dog, which doesn’t have language.

cues.zh: 它们没有语言，却比任何 LLM 都更懂这个世界。
cues.en: They don’t have language and they understand the world much better than any LLM.

cues.zh: 它们能规划非常复杂的动作，还能想象一系列动作的结果。
cues.en: They can plan really complex actions and imagine the result of a bunch of actions.

cues.zh: 我们如何让机器先学会这些，再与语言结合？
cues.en: How do we get machines to learn that before we combine that with language?

cues.zh: 显然，如果把这与语言结合起来，这将会是赢家，但在此之前，我们必须关注如何让系统学会世界是如何运作的？
cues.en: Obviously if we combine this with language, this is going to be a winner, but before that, we have to focus on how do we get systems to learn how the world works?

cues.zh: 所以这个联合嵌入预测架构，对你来说，将能够学习类似常识的东西，比如猫用来预测如何通过打翻东西来最优化地捣乱主人的那种能力。
cues.en: So this joint-embedding predictive architecture, for you, that’s going to be able to learn something like common sense, something like what a cat uses to predict how to mess with its owner most optimally by knocking over a thing.

cues.zh: 这就是希望所在。
cues.en: That’s the hope.

cues.zh: 事实上，我们使用的技术是非对比式的。
cues.en: In fact, the techniques we’re using are non-contrastive.

cues.zh: 所以不仅架构是非生成式的，我们使用的学习程序也是非对比式的。
cues.en: So not only is the architecture non-generative, the learning procedures we are using are non-contrastive.

cues.zh: 我们有两套技术。
cues.en: We have two sets of techniques.

cues.zh: 一套基于蒸馏，有许多方法使用这一原理，其中一个由DeepMind提出，叫BYOL，FAIR有几个，一个叫vcREG，另一个叫I-JEPA。
cues.en: One set is based on distillation, and there’s a number of methods that use this principle, one by DeepMind called BYOL, a couple by FAIR, one called vcREG and another one called I-JEPA.

cues.zh: 我得说，vcREG其实不是一种蒸馏方法，但I-JEPA和BYOL确实是。
cues.en: And vcREG, I should say, is not a distillation method actually, but I-JEPA and BYOL certainly are.

cues.zh: 还有一个叫DINO，也是FAIR产出的。
cues.en: And there’s another one also called DINO or DINO also produced from at FAIR.

cues.zh: 这些方法的核心思路是：你拿完整输入，比如一张图像，通过编码器生成一个表示，然后破坏或变换这个输入，再让它通过基本相同的编码器（有些细微差别），然后训练一个预测器。
cues.en: And the idea of those things is that you take the full input, let’s say an image, you run it through an encoder, produces a representation, and then you corrupt that input or transform it, run it through essentially what amounts to the same encoder with some minor differences and then train a predictor.

cues.zh: 有时预测器非常简单，有时甚至不存在，但训练一个预测器，从被破坏的输入预测第一个未破坏输入的表示。
cues.en: Sometimes a predictor is very simple, sometimes it doesn’t exist, but train a predictor to predict a representation of the first uncorrupted input from the corrupted input.

cues.zh: 但你只训练第二个分支。
cues.en: But you only train the second branch.

cues.zh: 你只训练网络中接收被破坏输入的那部分。
cues.en: You only train the part of the network that is fed with the corrupted input.

cues.zh: 另一个网络，你不训练它。
cues.en: The other network, you don’t train.

cues.zh: 但既然它们共享同一套权重，你修改第一个时，第二个也会跟着变。
cues.en: But since they share the same weight, when you modify the first one, it also modifies the second one.

cues.zh: 通过各种技巧，你可以防止系统崩溃，避免我之前解释的那种崩溃类型，也就是系统基本忽略输入的情况。
cues.en: And with various tricks, you can prevent the system from collapsing with the collapse of the type I was explaining before, where the system basically ignores the input.

cues.zh: 所以效果非常好。
cues.en: So that works very well.

cues.zh: 我们在 FAIR 开发的两种技术，DINO 和 I-JEPA，在这方面效果很好。
cues.en: The two techniques we developed at FAIR, DINO and I-JEPA work really well for that.

cues.zh: 那么这里说的是什么样的数据？
cues.en: So what kind of data are we talking about here?

cues.zh: 有几种场景，一种是你拿一张图像，通过改变裁剪来破坏它，比如稍微改变尺寸，也许改变方向，模糊它，改变颜色，对它做各种糟糕的处理。
cues.en: So there’s several scenario, one scenario is you take an image, you corrupt it by changing the cropping, for example, changing the size a little bit, maybe changing the orientation, blurring it, changing the colors, doing all kinds of horrible things to it.

cues.zh: 但那些糟糕的基础操作呢？
cues.en: But basic horrible things?

cues.zh: 那些糟糕的基础操作会稍微降低质量，改变构图，裁剪图像。
cues.en: Basic horrible things that sort of degrade the quality a little bit and change the framing, crop the image.

cues.zh: 在某些情况下，比如 I-JEPA，你根本不需要做这些，只需遮住其中一部分。
cues.en: And in some cases, in the case of I-JEPA, you don’t need to do any of this, you just mask some parts of it.

cues.zh: 基本上就是去掉一些区域，比如一大块，然后通过编码器运行，训练整个系统——编码器和预测器——从损坏版本的表示预测完好版本的表示。
cues.en: You just basically remove some regions, like a big block essentially, and then run through the encoders and train the entire system, encoder and predictor, to predict the representation of the good one from the representation of the corrupted one.

cues.zh: 这就是 I-JEPA。
cues.en: So that’s the I-JEPA.

cues.zh: 它不需要知道这是图像，比如，因为它唯一需要知道的就是如何做这种遮罩。
cues.en: It doesn’t need to know that it’s an image for example, because the only thing it needs to know is how to do this masking.

cues.zh: 而用 DINO 时，你需要知道这是图像，因为你要做几何变换、模糊之类的操作，这些都是图像特有的。
cues.en: Whereas with DINO, you need to know it’s an image because you need to do things like geometry transformation and blurring and things like that, that are really image specific.

cues.zh: 我们有一个更新的版本，叫 V-JEPA。
cues.en: A more recent version of this that we have is called V-JEPA.

cues.zh: 基本思路和 I-JEPA 一样，只是应用到了视频上。
cues.en: So it’s basically the same idea as I-JEPA except it’s applied to video.

cues.zh: 现在你拿一整段视频，把其中一大块遮住。
cues.en: So now you take a whole video and you mask a whole chunk of it.

cues.zh: 我们遮住的其实是一个时间上的管状区域，也就是视频每一帧中同一块区域，贯穿整段视频。
cues.en: And what we mask is actually kind of a temporal tube, so a whole segment of each frame in the video over the entire video.

cues.zh: 这个管状区域在各帧中位置固定，就是字面意义上的一个直管。
cues.en: And that tube was statically positioned throughout the frames, just literally it’s a straight tube.

cues.zh: 这个管状区域通常覆盖 16 帧左右，我们在整段 16 帧里遮住同一块区域。
cues.en: The tube, yeah, typically is 16 frames or something, and we mask the same region over the entire 16 frames.

cues.zh: 当然，每个视频遮的位置都不一样。
cues.en: It’s a different one for every video obviously.

cues.zh: 然后同样地，训练这个系统，让它从部分被遮住的视频预测完整视频的表示。
cues.en: And then again, train that system so as to predict the representation of the full video from the partially masked video.

cues.zh: 效果非常好。
cues.en: And that works really well.

cues.zh: 这是我们第一个能学习视频良好表示的系统，把这些表示输入给监督分类器头部，它就能相当准确地告诉你视频里正在发生什么动作。
cues.en: It’s the first system that we have that learns good representations of video so that when you feed those representations to a supervised classifier head, it can tell you what action is taking place in the video with pretty good accuracy.

cues.zh: 这是我们第一次得到这种质量的结果。
cues.en: So that’s the first time we get something of that quality.

cues.zh: 这是一个很好的检验，说明形成了良好的表示。
cues.en: That’s a good test that a good representation is formed.

cues.zh: 这意味着这东西确实有门道。
cues.en: That means there’s something to this.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我们还有初步结果似乎表明，这种表示能让我们的系统判断视频在物理上是可能的还是完全不可能的，比如某个物体消失了，或者物体突然从一个位置跳到另一个位置，或者改变了形状之类的。
cues.en: We also preliminary result that seem to indicate that the representation allow our system to tell whether the video is physically possible or completely impossible, because some object disappeared or an object suddenly jumped from one location to another or changed shape or something.

cues.zh: 所以它能捕捉到一些关于视频所呈现现实的物理约束，关于物体的出现和消失。
cues.en: So it’s able to capture some physics based constraints about the reality represented in the video, about the appearance and the disappearance of objects.

cues.zh: 是的，这确实是全新的。
cues.en: Yeah, that’s really new.

cues.zh: 好吧，但这真能让我们得到那种足够理解世界、可以开车的世界模型吗？
cues.en: Okay, but can this actually get us to this kind of world model that understands enough about the world to be able to drive a car?

cues.zh: 有可能，但要达到那一步还需要一段时间。
cues.en: Possibly, this is going to take a while before we get to that point.

cues.zh: 而且已经有系统了，基于这个理念的机器人系统。
cues.en: And there are systems already robotic systems, that are based on this idea.

cues.zh: 为此你需要的是这个的一个稍作修改的版本，想象你有一段完整的视频，你对这段视频做的是要么在时间上把它向未来平移。
cues.en: And what you need for this is a slightly modified version of this, where imagine that you have a complete video and what you’re doing to this video is that you are either translating it in time towards the future.

cues.zh: 所以你只看到视频的开头，但看不到原视频中后面的部分，或者比如你只遮住视频的后半段。
cues.en: So you only see the beginning of the video, but you don’t see the latter part of it that is in the original one, or you just mask the second half of the video, for example.

cues.zh: 然后你训练一个JEPA系统，或者我描述的那种类型，从平移后的版本预测完整视频的表示。
cues.en: And then you train a JEPA system or the type I described, to predict the representation of the full video from the shifted one.

cues.zh: 但你还会给预测器输入一个动作。
cues.en: But you also feed the predictor with an action.

cues.zh: 比如方向盘向右打了10度之类的，对吧？
cues.en: For example, the wheel is turned 10 degrees to the right or something, right?

cues.zh: 所以如果是车里的行车记录仪，而且你知道方向盘的角度，你应该能在一定程度上预测你看到的画面接下来会发生什么。
cues.en: So if it’s a dash cam in a car and you know the angle of the wheel, you should be able to predict to some extent what’s going to happen to what you see.

cues.zh: 你显然无法预测视野中出现物体的所有细节，但在抽象表征层面上，你大概能预测会发生什么。
cues.en: You’re not going to be able to predict all the details of objects that appear in the view obviously, but at a abstract representation level, you can probably predict what’s going to happen.

cues.zh: 所以现在你得到的是一个内部模型，它说：“这是我对时刻T世界状态的判断。
cues.en: So now what you have is a internal model that says, “Here is my idea of the state of the world at time T.

cues.zh: 这是我正在采取的动作。
cues.en: Here is an action I’m taking.

cues.zh: 这是对时刻T加一、T加delta T、T加两秒之后世界状态的预测，”不管具体是什么。
cues.en: Here is a prediction of the state of the world at time T plus one, T plus delta T, T plus two seconds,” whatever it is.

cues.zh: 如果你有这种类型的模型，就可以用它来做规划。
cues.en: If you have a model of this type, you can use it for planning.

cues.zh: 现在你能做 LMS 做不到的事，也就是规划你接下来要做什么。
cues.en: So now you can do what LMS cannot do, which is planning what you’re going to do.

cues.zh: 从而达成某个结果，或满足某个特定目标。
cues.en: So as you arrive at a particular outcome or satisfy a particular objective.

cues.zh: 所以你可以有多个目标。
cues.en: So you can have a number of objectives.

cues.zh: 我能预测，如果我有这样一个物体，然后张开手，它就会掉下去。
cues.en: I can predict that if I have an object like this and I open my hand, it’s going to fall.

cues.zh: 如果我在桌上用特定的力推它，它就会移动。
cues.en: And if I push it with a particular force on the table, it’s going to move.

cues.zh: 如果我推桌子本身，它大概不会以同样的力移动。
cues.en: If I push the table itself, it’s probably not going to move with the same force.

cues.zh: 所以我们脑中有一个关于世界的内部模型，让我们能规划一系列动作来达成特定目标。
cues.en: So we have this internal model of the world in our mind, which allows us to plan sequences of actions to arrive at a particular goal.

cues.zh: 那么现在，如果你有这个世界模型，我们就可以想象一系列动作，预测这串动作会带来什么结果，衡量最终状态在多大程度上满足某个特定目标，比如把瓶子移到桌子左边，然后在运行时规划出一串能最小化这个目标的动作。
cues.en: And so now if you have this world model, we can imagine a sequence of actions, predict what the outcome of the sequence of action is going to be, measure to what extent the final state satisfies a particular objective, like moving the bottle to the left of the table and then plan a sequence of actions that will minimize this objective, at runtime.

cues.zh: 我们说的不是学习，而是推理阶段，所以这其实是规划。
cues.en: We’re not talking about learning, we’re talking about inference time, so this is planning, really.

cues.zh: 在最优控制里，这是非常经典的东西。
cues.en: And in optimal control, this is a very classical thing.

cues.zh: 它叫模型预测控制。
cues.en: It’s called model predictive control.

cues.zh: 你有一个待控制系统的模型，能根据指令序列预测对应的状态序列。
cues.en: You have a model of the system you want to control that can predict the sequence of states corresponding to a sequence of commands.

cues.zh: 你规划一串指令，使得按你的模型，系统的最终状态能满足你设定的目标。
cues.en: And you’re planning a sequence of commands so that according to your role model, the end state of the system will satisfy an objectives that you fix.

cues.zh: 自计算机问世以来，火箭轨迹就是这么规划的，基本上从60年代初就开始了。
cues.en: This is the way rocket trajectories have been planned since computers have been around, so since the early ’60s essentially.

cues.zh: 所以是的，对模型预测控制而言是这样，但人们也常谈到分层规划。
cues.en: So yes, for a model predictive control, but you also often talk about hierarchical planning.

cues.zh: 分层规划能以某种方式从中涌现出来吗？
cues.en: Can hierarchical planning emerge from this somehow?

cues.zh: 所以不行，你得构建特定的架构来支持分层规划。
cues.en: Well, so no, you will have to build a specific architecture to allow for hierarchical planning.

cues.zh: 所以如果你想规划复杂的行动，分层规划绝对是必要的。
cues.en: So hierarchical planning is absolutely necessary if you want to plan complex actions.

cues.zh: 比如我想从纽约去巴黎——这是我常用的例子——我坐在NYU的办公室里，需要最小化的目标就是我到巴黎的距离。
cues.en: If I want to go from, let’s say from New York to Paris, it’s the example I use all the time, and I’m sitting in my office at NYU, my objective that I need to minimize is my distance to Paris.

cues.zh: 在高层面上，用非常抽象的方式表示我的位置，我得把这个分解成两个子目标。
cues.en: At a high level, a very abstract representation of my location, I would have to decompose this into two sub goals.

cues.zh: 第一个是去机场，第二个是搭飞机去巴黎。
cues.en: First one is go to the airport, second one is catch a plane to Paris.

cues.zh: 好，那我的子目标现在就是去机场。
cues.en: Okay, so my sub goal is now going to the airport.

cues.zh: 我的目标函数就是到机场的距离。
cues.en: My objective function is my distance to the airport.

cues.zh: 我怎么去机场呢？我得走到街上拦出租车，这在纽约是可以做到的。
cues.en: How do I go to the airport where I have to go in the street and hail a taxi, which you can do in New York.

cues.zh: 好，现在我有了另一个子目标：走到街上。
cues.en: Okay, now I have another sub goal go down on the street.

cues.zh: 这意味着要走向电梯、乘电梯下去、走出街道。
cues.en: Well that means going to the elevator, going down the elevator, walk out the street.

cues.zh: 我怎么走到电梯那儿？
cues.en: How do I go to the elevator?

cues.zh: 我得从椅子上站起来，打开办公室的门，走到电梯，按下按钮。
cues.en: I have to stand up from my chair, open the door in my office, go to the elevator, push the button.

cues.zh: 我怎么从椅子上站起来？
cues.en: How do I get up for my chair?

cues.zh: 你可以想象一路向下分解，直到基本上等同于毫秒级的肌肉控制。
cues.en: You can imagine going down, all the way down, to basically what amounts to millisecond by millisecond muscle control.

cues.zh: 显然，你不会用毫秒级的肌肉控制来规划从纽约到巴黎的整个行程。
cues.en: And obviously you’re not going plan your entire trip from New York to Paris in terms of millisecond by millisecond muscle control.

cues.zh: 首先，那会极其昂贵，而且完全不可能，因为你不知道所有将要发生的情况，比如打出租车或去机场路上堵车要花多长时间。
cues.en: First, that would be incredibly expensive, but it will also be completely impossible because you don’t know all the conditions of what’s going to happen, how long it’s going to take to catch a taxi or to go to the airport with traffic.

cues.zh: 我是说，你得精确掌握所有事物的状态才能做这种规划，而你并没有这些信息。
cues.en: I mean, you would have to know exactly the condition of everything to be able to do this planning and you don’t have the information.

cues.zh: 所以你得做这种分层规划，先开始行动，然后在过程中不断重新规划。
cues.en: So you have to do this hierarchical planning so that you can start acting and then sort of replanning as you go.

cues.zh: 而在AI领域，没人真正知道怎么做这件事。
cues.en: And nobody really knows how to do this in AI.

cues.zh: 没人知道如何训练一个系统去学习合适的多层次表征，从而让分层规划奏效。
cues.en: Nobody knows how to train a system to learn the appropriate multiple levels of representation so that hierarchical planning works.

cues.zh: 类似的东西已经涌现出来了吗？
cues.en: Does something like that already emerge?

cues.zh: 那么，你能用LLM、最先进的LLM，通过刚才那种详细的连环提问，把你从纽约带到巴黎吗？也就是：你能给我列出从纽约到巴黎所需的10个步骤吗？
cues.en: So can you use an LLM, state-of-the-art LLM, to get you from New York to Paris by doing exactly the kind of detailed set of questions that you just did, which is, can you give me a list of 10 steps I need to do, to get from New York to Paris?

cues.zh: 然后对于每一个步骤，你能给我列出10个步骤吗，我怎样才能让那个步骤发生？
cues.en: And then for each of those steps, can you give me a list of 10 steps, how I make that step happen?

cues.zh: 对于每一个步骤，你能给我列出10个步骤来实现每一个步骤，直到你移动你的每一块肌肉，也许不是，不管你能用自己的头脑实际控制什么。
cues.en: And for each of those steps, can you give me a list of 10 steps to make each one of those, until you’re moving your individual muscles, maybe not, whatever you can actually act upon using your own mind.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 所以这里也隐含了很多问题，对吧？
cues.en: So there’s a lot of questions that are also implied by this, right?

cues.zh: 所以第一件事是，LLM将能够把其中一些问题回答到某种抽象层次，前提是它们在训练集中接受过类似场景的训练。
cues.en: So the first thing is LLMs will be able to answer some of those questions down to some level of abstraction, under the condition that they’ve been trained with similar scenarios in their training set.

cues.zh: 它们能够回答所有这些问题，但其中一些可能是幻觉，也就是不符合事实。
cues.en: They would be able to answer all of those questions, but some of them may be hallucinated meaning non-factual.

cues.zh: 是的，没错。
cues.en: Yeah, true.

cues.zh: 我是说它们可能会给出一些答案，只不过它们无法真正给出你从椅子上站起来时逐毫秒的肌肉控制。
cues.en: I mean they’ll probably produce some answer except they’re not going to be able to really produce millisecond by millisecond muscle control of how you stand up from your chair.

cues.zh: 但到了某种抽象层面，你能用语言描述事物，它们或许能给你一个计划，但前提是它们受过训练，能产出这类计划。
cues.en: But down to some level of abstraction where you can describe things by words, they might be able to give you a plan, but only under the condition that they’ve been trained to produce those kinds of plans.

cues.zh: 它们没法为从未遇到过的情况做计划。
cues.en: They’re not going to be able to plan for situations where that they never encountered before.

cues.zh: 它们基本上只能照搬训练过的模板。
cues.en: They basically are going to have to regurgitate the template that they’ve been trained on.

cues.zh: 就拿纽约到巴黎这个例子来说，它会开始出问题吗？
cues.en: Just for the example of New York to Paris, is it going to start getting into trouble?

cues.zh: 你觉得会从哪个抽象层面开始？
cues.en: Which layer of abstraction do you think you’ll start?

cues.zh: 我能想象几乎每一个环节，LLM都能给出大致准确的回答，尤其是涉及纽约和巴黎这种大城市时。
cues.en: I can imagine almost every single part of that, an LLM would be able to answer somewhat accurately, especially when you’re talking about New York and Paris, major cities.

cues.zh: 我是说，如果你针对这个问题微调LLM，它肯定能解决。
cues.en: I mean certainly LLM would be able to solve that problem if you fine tune it for it.

cues.zh: 所以我不能说 LLM 做不到这一点，只要针对它训练，它就能做到，毫无疑问，在一定程度上，有些事情是可以用词语来表达的。
cues.en: And so I can’t say that an LLM cannot do this, it can do this if you train it for it, there’s no question down to a certain level where things can be formulated in terms of words.

cues.zh: 但如果你想用词语来描述如何下楼梯，或者如何从椅子上站起来，那是做不到的。
cues.en: But if you want to go down to how you climb down the stairs or just stand up from your chair in terms of words, you can’t do it.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么你需要对物理世界的体验，它的带宽远高于你能用词语、用人类语言表达的内容。
cues.en: That’s one of the reasons you need experience of the physical world, which is much higher bandwidth than what you can express in words, in human language.

cues.zh: 所以我们一直在讨论的联合嵌入空间，有没有可能这正是我们在机器人领域与物理现实互动所需要的东西，而 LLM 只是坐落在其上的东西，用于更高层次的推理，比如我需要订一张机票，我需要知道如何访问网站等等。
cues.en: So everything we’ve been talking about on the joint embedding space, is it possible that that’s what we need for the interaction with physical reality on the robotics front, and then just the LLMs are the thing that sits on top of it for the bigger reasoning, about the fact that I need to book a plane ticket and I need to know how to go to the websites and so on.

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 人们熟知的许多计划层次相对较高，实际上都是学来的。
cues.en: And a lot of plans that people know about that are relatively high level are actually learned.

cues.zh: 大多数人并不会自己发明计划。
cues.en: Most people don’t invent the plans by themselves.

cues.zh: 当然，我们确实有一定能力做到这一点，但人们使用的大多数计划都是经过训练的，他们见过别人使用这些计划，或者被告知该怎么做，对吧？
cues.en: We have some ability to do this of course, obviously, but most plans that people use are plans that have been trained on, they’ve seen other people use those plans or they’ve been told how to do things, right?

cues.zh: 你没法凭空发明——比如让一个从没听说过飞机的人，告诉他怎么从纽约到巴黎？
cues.en: That you can’t invent how you take a person who’s never heard of airplanes and tell them how do you go from New York to Paris?

cues.zh: 除非他以前见过类似的例子，否则他很可能无法拆解出整个计划。
cues.en: And they’re probably not going to be able to deconstruct the whole plan unless they’ve seen examples of that before.

cues.zh: 所以LLM当然能做到这一点，但如何把它与低层动作连接起来，就需要借助JEPA之类的东西，它基本上提升了表示的抽象层次，而不试图重建情境的细节，这正是我们需要JEPA的原因。
cues.en: So certainly LLMs are going to be able to do this, but then how you link this from the low level of actions, that needs to be done with things like JEPA that basically lift the abstraction level of the representation without attempting to reconstruct the detail of the situation, that’s why we need JEPAs for.

cues.zh: 我很想深入聊聊你对自回归LLM的怀疑。
cues.en: I would love to sort of linger on your skepticism around auto regressive LLMs.

cues.zh: 我想检验这种怀疑的一个方法是，你说的都很有道理，但如果把你今天说的以及一般性的观点套用到，我不知道，10年前，也许稍微短一点，不，就说三年前，我无法预测LLM的成功。
cues.en: So one way I would like to test that skepticism is everything you say makes a lot of sense, but if I apply everything you said today and in general to I don’t know, 10 years ago, maybe a little bit less, no, let’s say three years ago, I wouldn’t be able to predict the success of LLMs.

cues.zh: 所以你觉得自回归LLM能这么厉害，这合理吗？
cues.en: So does it make sense to you that autoregressive LLMs are able to be so damn good?

cues.zh: 合理。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 能解释一下你的直觉吗？
cues.en: Can you explain your intuition?

cues.zh: 因为如果我按字面接受你的智慧和直觉，我会说自回归LLM一次一个token，绝不可能做到它们现在做的事。
cues.en: Because if I were to take your wisdom and intuition at face value, I would say there’s no way autoregressive LLMs, one token at a time, would be able to do the kind of things they’re doing.

cues.zh: 不，有一点是自回归LLM，或者说一般意义上的LLM，不只是自回归的，也包括BERT风格的双向模型，正在利用的，那就是自监督学习，而我多年来一直是自监督学习的非常非常坚定的倡导者。
cues.en: No, there’s one thing that autoregressive LLMs or that LLMs in general, not just the autoregressive one, but including the bird style bidirectional ones, are exploiting and its self supervised running, and I’ve been a very, very strong advocate of self supervised running for many years.

cues.zh: 这些成果极其有力地证明了自监督运行确实有效。
cues.en: So those things are a incredibly impressive demonstration that self supervised running actually works.

cues.zh: 这个想法并非始于 BERT，但 BERT 确实很好地展示了它。
cues.en: The idea that started, it didn’t start with BERT, but it was really kind of good demonstration with this.

cues.zh: 思路是：取一段文本，把它破坏掉，然后训练一个巨大的神经网络去重建缺失的部分。
cues.en: So the idea that you take a piece of text, you corrupt it, and then you train some gigantic neural net to reconstruct the parts that are missing.

cues.zh: 这带来了巨大的收益。
cues.en: That has produced an enormous amount of benefits.

cues.zh: 它让我们能够构建理解语言的系统、能在数百种语言之间任意方向翻译的系统、以及多语言系统——也就是单个系统，可以训练它理解数百种语言、任意方向翻译，还能生成摘要、回答问题、生成文本。
cues.en: It allowed us to create systems that understand language, systems that can translate hundreds of languages in any direction, systems that are multilingual, so it’s a single system that can be trained to understand hundreds of languages and translate in any direction, and produce summaries and then answer questions and produce text.

cues.zh: 然后它有个特例，就是自回归技巧，你约束系统不能通过看整个文本来构建文本表示，而只能根据前面出现的词来预测下一个词。
cues.en: And then there’s a special case of it, which is the auto regressive trick where you constrain the system to not elaborate a representation of the text from looking at the entire text, but only predicting a word from the words that are come before.

cues.zh: 你通过约束网络架构来实现这一点，这就是构建自回归LLM的方法。
cues.en: And you do this by constraining the architecture of the network, and that’s what you can build an auto aggressive LLM from.

cues.zh: 所以多年前出现了一个惊喜，就是所谓的仅解码器LLM。
cues.en: So there was a surprise many years ago with what’s called decoder only LLM.

cues.zh: 所以这类系统只是试图从上一个词生成下一个词，而当你扩大规模时，它们往往会真正更多地理解语言。
cues.en: So since systems of this type that are just trying to produce words from the previous one and the fact that when you scale them up, they tend to really understand more about language.

cues.zh: 当你用大量数据训练它们，让它们变得非常大。
cues.en: When you train them on lots of data, you make them really big.

cues.zh: 那是一个惊喜，而且这个惊喜很久以前就出现了，来自Google、Meta、OpenAI等的工作，可以追溯到GPT类的工作，即通用预训练Transformer。
cues.en: That was a surprise and that surprise occurred quite a while back, with work from Google, Meta, OpenAI, et cetera, going back to the GPT kind of work, general pre-trained transformers.

cues.zh: 你是说像 GPT2 那样？
cues.en: You mean like GPT2?

cues.zh: 有一个特定的阶段，你会开始意识到，扩展规模也许真的会持续带来涌现性的收益。
cues.en: There’s a certain place where you start to realize scaling might actually keep giving us an emergent benefit.

cues.zh: 是的，我是说各地都有相关工作，但如果放到 GPT 的时间线上，那大概就是 GPT2 前后，没错。
cues.en: Yeah, I mean there were work from various places, but if you want to place it in the GPT timeline, that would be around GPT2, yeah.

cues.zh: 嗯，因为你讲得那么有感染力，说了那么多话，但其实就是自监督学习，是的。
cues.en: Well, because you said it so charismatic and you said so many words, but self supervised learning, yes.

cues.zh: 但同样的，你用来论证自回归 LLM 无法深入理解世界的那个直觉。
cues.en: But again, the same intuition you’re applying to saying that auto aggressive LLMs cannot have a deep understanding of the world.

cues.zh: 如果我们直接套用同样的直觉，你觉得它们能在世界中形成足够充分的表征，从而极具说服力，基本上以优异成绩通过最初的图灵测试，这说得通吗？
cues.en: If we just apply that, same intuition, does it make sense to you that they’re able to form enough of a representation in the world to be damn convincing, essentially passing the original touring test with flying colors?

cues.zh: 我们被它们的流畅性骗了，对吧？
cues.en: Well, we’re fooled by their fluency, right?

cues.zh: 我们想当然地认为，如果一个系统能流利地处理语言，那它就具备人类智能的所有特征，但这种印象是错误的。
cues.en: We just assume that if a system is fluent in manipulating language, then it has all the characteristics of human intelligence, but that impression is false.

cues.zh: 我们真的被它骗了。
cues.en: We’re really fooled by it.

cues.zh: 你觉得Alan Turing会怎么说？什么都不理解，只是跟它闲逛？
cues.en: What do you think Alan Turing would say, without understanding anything, just hanging out with it?

cues.zh: Alan Turing会认定图灵测试是个很糟糕的测试，对吧？
cues.en: Alan Turing would decide that a Turing test is a really bad test, okay?

cues.zh: 这就是AI界多年前就已认定图灵测试是个很糟糕的智能测试的原因。
cues.en: This is what the AI community has decided many years ago that the Turing test was a really bad test of intelligence.

cues.zh: Hans Marvek会怎么评价更大的语言模型？
cues.en: What would Hans Marvek say about the larger language models?

cues.zh: Hans Marvek会说Marvek悖论依然成立。
cues.en: Hans Marvek would say that Marvek Paradox still applies.

cues.zh: 好吧，我们可以通过——
cues.en: Okay, we can pass-

cues.zh: 你不觉得他会印象深刻吗？
cues.en: You don’t think he would be really impressed?

cues.zh: 不，当然所有人都会印象深刻。
cues.en: No, of course everybody would be impressed.

cues.zh: 但问题不在于是否让人印象深刻，而在于要知道这些系统的能力极限在哪里。
cues.en: But it’s not a question of being impressed or not, it’s the question of knowing what the limit of those systems can do.

cues.zh: 再说一次，它们确实很厉害。
cues.en: Again, they are impressive.

cues.zh: 它们能做很多有用的事。
cues.en: They can do a lot of useful things.

cues.zh: 围绕它们正在形成一个完整的产业。
cues.en: There’s a whole industry that is being built around them.

cues.zh: 它们会不断进步，但有很多事它们做不了，我们必须认清它们做不到什么，然后想办法怎么达到那一步。
cues.en: They’re going to make progress, but there is a lot of things they cannot do, and we have to realize what they cannot do and then figure out how we get there.

cues.zh: 我从大约10年的自监督运行研究中看到了这一点，其实这可以追溯到十多年前，就是自监督运行这个想法。
cues.en: And I’m seeing this from basically 10 years of research on the idea of self supervised running, actually that’s going back more than 10 years, but the idea of self supervised running.

cues.zh: 基本上就是捕捉一组输入的内部结构，而不针对任何特定任务训练系统，去学习表征。
cues.en: So basically capturing the internal structure of a piece of a set of inputs without training the system for any particular task, to learning representations.

cues.zh: 我14年前联合创办的会议叫国际学习表征会议。
cues.en: The conference I co-founded 14 years ago is called International Conference on Learning Representations.

cues.zh: 这正是深度学习要处理的核心问题，也是我近40年来一直痴迷的方向。
cues.en: That’s the entire issue that deep learning is dealing with, and it’s been my obsession for almost 40 years now.

cues.zh: 所以学习表征才是关键所在。
cues.en: So learning representation is really the thing.

cues.zh: 很长一段时间里，我们只能靠监督学习来做这件事，后来我们开始研究过去称为无监督学习的方法，并在2000年代初与[听不清 00:56:58]和Jeff Hinton一起复兴了无监督训练的思路。
cues.en: For the longest time, we could only do this with supervised learning, and then we started working on what we used to call unsupervised learning and revived the idea of unsupervised running in the early 2000s with your [inaudible 00:56:58] and Jeff Hinton.

cues.zh: 然后发现，只要能收集到足够的数据，监督训练其实效果相当不错。
cues.en: Then discovered that supervised running actually works pretty well if you can collect enough data.

cues.zh: 于是无监督、自监督训练的整体思路一度退居次要位置，后来我从2014年开始大力尝试复兴它，基本上就是在我们创办FAIR的时候，真正推动为文本、图像、视频和音频寻找自监督训练的新方法。
cues.en: And so the whole idea of unsupervised, self supervised running kind of took a backseat for a bit, and then I tried to revive it in a big way starting in 2014, basically when we started FAIR and really pushing for finding new methods to do self supervised running both for text and for images and for video and audio.

cues.zh: 其中一些工作取得了极其成功的结果。
cues.en: And some of that work has been incredibly successful.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，我们之所以有多语言翻译系统，比如在 Meta、在 Facebook 上做多语言的内容审核，能判断一段文本是不是仇恨言论之类的，正是因为自监督学习在 NLP 上的进展，再结合 Transformer 架构等等。
cues.en: I mean, the reason why we have multilingual translation system, things to do, content moderation on Meta, for example, on Facebook, that are multilingual, that understand whether a piece of text is hate speech not or something, is due to that progress using self supervised running for NLP, combining this with transformer architectures and blah, blah, blah.

cues.zh: 但这就是自监督学习的一大成功。
cues.en: But that’s the big success of self supervised running.

cues.zh: 我们在语音识别上也取得了类似的成功，有个叫 WAVE2VEC 的系统，顺便说一句，它也是一种联合嵌入架构，用对比学习训练出来的。
cues.en: We had similar success in speech recognition, a system called WAVE2VEC, which is also a joint embedding architecture, by the way, trained with contrastive running.

cues.zh: 这个系统还能构建多语言语音识别系统，主要用无标注数据，只需要几分钟的有标注数据就能真正做语音识别，太惊人了。
cues.en: And that system also can produce speech recognition systems that are multilingual with mostly unlabeled data and only need a few minutes of labeled data to actually do speech recognition, that’s amazing.

cues.zh: 现在我们有基于这些理念组合的系统，能够实现数百种语言之间的实时语音到语音翻译。
cues.en: We have systems now based on those combination of ideas that can do real time translation of hundreds of languages into each other, speech to speech.

cues.zh: 语音到语音，甚至包括那些没有书面形式的语言，这非常令人着迷。
cues.en: Speech to speech, even including, which is fascinating, languages that don’t have written forms.

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: That’s right.

cues.zh: 只有口语形式。
cues.en: Just spoken only.

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: That’s right.

cues.zh: 我们不经过文本，而是直接通过一种离散的语音单元内部表示实现语音到语音转换，这被称为Textless NLP。
cues.en: We don’t go through text, it goes directly from speech to speech using an internal representation of speech units that are discrete, but it’s called Textless NLP.

cues.zh: 我们以前是这么叫的。
cues.en: We used to call it this way.

cues.zh: 但没错，这方面取得了巨大成功。
cues.en: But yeah, so I mean incredible success there.

cues.zh: 然后有十年时间，我们尝试把这个思路应用到图像表示学习上，通过训练系统预测视频，通过训练系统预测视频中将发生什么来学习直觉物理。
cues.en: And then for 10 years, we tried to apply this idea to learning representations of images by training a system to predict videos, learning intuitive physics by training a system to predict what’s going to happen in the video.

cues.zh: 我们试了又试，失败了又失败，用生成模型，用预测像素的模型。
cues.en: And tried and tried and failed and failed, with generative models, with models that predict pixels.

cues.zh: 我们没法让它们学到图像的优质表征。
cues.en: We could not get them to learn good representations of images.

cues.zh: 我们没法让它们学到视频的优质表征。
cues.en: We could not get them to learn good representations of videos.

cues.zh: 我们试了很多次，发表了很多论文，它们勉强算能用，但效果并不好。
cues.en: And we tried many times, we published lots of papers on it, where they kind of sort of work, but not really great.

cues.zh: 它们开始奏效了，我们放弃了预测每个像素的想法，基本上只做联合嵌入，在表征空间里做预测，这就行了。
cues.en: They started working, we abandoned this idea of predicting every pixel and basically just doing the joint embedding and predicting and representation space, that works.

cues.zh: 所以有充分证据表明，用生成模型无法学到真实世界的优质表征。
cues.en: So there’s ample evidence that we’re not going to be able to learn good representations of the real world using generative model.

cues.zh: 所以我一直在告诉大家，现在人人都在谈论生成式AI。
cues.en: So I’m telling people, everybody’s talking about generative AI.

cues.zh: 如果你真的对类人AI感兴趣，就放弃生成式AI这个思路。
cues.en: If you’re really interested in human level AI, abandon the idea of generative AI.

cues.zh: 好，但你真的认为联合嵌入表示能走得很远吗？
cues.en: Okay, but you really think it’s possible to get far with the joint embedding representation.

cues.zh: 有常识推理，还有高层推理。
cues.en: So there’s common sense reasoning, and then there’s high level reasoning.

cues.zh: 我觉得这是两种……LLM能做的那种推理，好吧，我不用“推理”这个词了，但LLM能做的那些事，似乎和我们用来在世界上导航的常识推理有本质不同。
cues.en: I feel like those are two… The kind of reasoning that LLMs are able to do, okay, let me not use the word reasoning, but the kind of stuff that LLMs are able to do, seems fundamentally different than the common sense reasoning we use to navigate the world.

cues.zh: 看起来我们两者都需要。
cues.en: It seems like we’re going to need both.

cues.zh: 用联合嵌入，也就是JEPA类方法，看视频，你能学到，比如说，怎么从纽约到巴黎，或者怎么理解当今世界的政治局势吗？
cues.en: Would you be able to get, with the joint embedding, which is JEPA type of approach, looking at video, would you be able to learn, let’s see, well, how to get from New York to Paris or how to understand the state of politics in the world today.

cues.zh: 这些是各种人类在语言领域生成大量语言和观点的事物，但并没有以任何清晰可压缩的方式在视觉上表现出来。
cues.en: These are things where various humans generate a lot of language and opinions on, in the space of language, but don’t visually represent that in any clearly compressible way.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 嗯，有很多情况对于纯基于语言的系统来说可能很难了解。
cues.en: Well, there’s a lot of situations that might be difficult to, for a purely language based system to know.

cues.zh: 好吧，你也许可以通过阅读文本学到，世界上所有公开可用的文本都表明，我不可能打个响指就从纽约到巴黎。
cues.en: Okay, you can probably learn from reading texts, the entirety of the publicly available texts in the world that I cannot get from New York to Paris by snapping my fingers.

cues.zh: 那行不通，对吧？
cues.en: That’s not going to work, right?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 但这类情况中可能有更复杂的场景，LLM 可能从未遇到过，也可能无法判断它是否可能。
cues.en: But there’s probably more complex scenarios of this type, which an LLM may never have encountered and may not be able to determine whether it’s possible or not.

cues.zh: 所以从低层到高层的那个链接，问题在于语言所表达的高层是基于低层的共同经验，而 LLM 目前没有这种经验。
cues.en: So that link from the low level to the high level, the thing is that the high level that language expresses is based on the common experience of the low level, which LLMs currently do not have.

cues.zh: 我们彼此交流时，都知道我们对世界有共同的体验。
cues.en: When we talk to each other, we know we have a common experience of the world.

cues.zh: 其中很多是相似的，而LLM没有这种共同体验。
cues.en: A lot of it is similar, and LLMs don’t have that.

cues.zh: 但你看，它其实是存在的。
cues.en: But see, it’s present.

cues.zh: 你和我对世界有共同的体验，比如重力如何运作这类事情，而这种对世界的共同认知，我觉得就存在于语言之中。
cues.en: You and I have a common experience of the world in terms of the physics of how gravity works and stuff like this, and that common knowledge of the world, I feel like is there, in the language.

cues.zh: 我们不会明确表达出来，但如果你有海量的文本，你就能得到这些字里行间的信息。
cues.en: We don’t explicitly express it, but if you have a huge amount of text, you’re going to get this stuff that’s between the lines.

cues.zh: 为了形成一个一致的世界模型，你就必须理解重力如何运作，即使你没有关于重力的明确解释。
cues.en: In order to form a consistent world model, you’re going to have to understand how gravity works, even if you don’t have an explicit explanation of gravity.

cues.zh: 所以，尽管在重力这个例子里，维基百科上确实有关于重力的明确解释。
cues.en: So even though in the case of gravity, there is explicit explanations of gravity in Wikipedia.

cues.zh: 但我认为，要正确生成语言，就必须搞懂我们视为常识推理的那些东西。
cues.en: But the stuff that we think of as common sense reasoning, I feel like to generate language correctly, you’re going to have to figure that out.

cues.zh: 你之前说过，文本量不够……抱歉，好吧，所以你不这么认为？
cues.en: Now, you could say as you have, there’s not enough text… Sorry, okay, so you don’t think so?

cues.zh: 不，我同意你刚才说的，也就是要具备高层次的常识，你得先有低层次的常识作为基础。
cues.en: No, I agree with what you just said, which is that to be able to do high level common sense, to have high level common sense, you need to have the low level common sense to build on top of.

cues.zh: 但那个基础并不存在。
cues.en: But that’s not there.

cues.zh: 而在大语言模型里，这个基础也不存在。
cues.en: And that’s not there in the LLMs.

cues.zh: 大语言模型完全是用文本训练的。
cues.en: LLMs are purely trained from text.

cues.zh: 所以你刚才的另一个说法我不认同，即世界上所有语言都隐含了底层现实——其实有大量底层现实并没有在语言中表达出来。
cues.en: So then the other statement you made, I would not agree with, the fact that implicit in all languages in the world is the underlying reality, is a lot of underlying reality, which is not expressed in language.

cues.zh: 这对你来说显而易见吗？
cues.en: Is that obvious to you?

cues.zh: 是的，完全。
cues.en: Yeah, totally.

cues.zh: 我们所有的对话……好吧，有暗网，意思是那些私密对话，比如私信之类的，它可能比现有可获取的、LLMs训练所用的数据要大得多得多。
