cues.en: So all the conversations we had… Okay, there’s the dark web, meaning whatever, the private conversations like DMs and stuff like this, which is much, much larger probably than what’s available, what LLMs are trained on.

cues.zh: 你不需要交流那些常见的东西，对吧？
cues.en: You don’t need to communicate the stuff that is common, right?

cues.zh: 但幽默，所有的，不，你需要，你不需要，但它会自然流露出来。
cues.en: But the humor, all of it, no, you do, you don’t need to, but it comes through.

cues.zh: 如果我不小心把这个打翻了，你可能会拿我开玩笑，而你开玩笑的内容会是对杯子会掉落、重力如此运作这一事实的解释。
cues.en: If I accidentally knock this over, you’ll probably make fun of me in the content of the you making fun of me will be explanation of the fact that cups fall, and then gravity works in this way.

cues.zh: 然后你会得到一些非常模糊的信息，关于什么东西撞到地面会爆炸。
cues.en: And then you’ll have some very vague information about what kind of things explode when they hit the ground.

cues.zh: 然后也许你会开个关于熵之类的玩笑，那我们就再也无法重建这个了。
cues.en: And then maybe you’ll make a joke about entropy or something like this, then we’ll never be able to reconstruct this again.

cues.zh: 你讲这么个小笑话，就会有无数个其他笑话。
cues.en: You’ll make a little joke like this and there’ll be a trillion of other jokes.

cues.zh: 从这些笑话里，你能拼凑出重力起作用、杯子会摔碎之类的事实。
cues.en: And from the jokes, you can piece together the fact that gravity works and mugs can break and all this kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 你不需要亲眼看到，那样会非常低效。
cues.en: You don’t need to see, it’ll be very inefficient.

cues.zh: 把东西弄倒更容易，但我觉得只要有足够的数据，那种信息也会存在。
cues.en: It’s easier to knock the thing over, but I feel like it would be there if you have enough of that data.

cues.zh: 我只是觉得，我们在婴儿时期积累的这类信息，基本上在任何文本、任何描述里都不存在。
cues.en: I just think that most of the information of this type that we have accumulated when we were babies, it’s just not present in text, in any description, essentially.

cues.zh: 而感官数据是获得那种理解的丰富得多的来源。
cues.en: And the sensory data is a much richer source for getting that kind of understanding.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，一个4岁孩子有16000小时的清醒时间，倾向于通过视觉处理大约15次注视，仅视觉就有类似的触觉带宽，音频稍少一些。
cues.en: I mean, there’s 16,000 hours of wake time of a 4-year-old and tend to do 15 bites going through vision, just vision, there is a similar bandwidth of touch and a little less through audio.

cues.zh: 然后，语言要到出生一年后才出现。
cues.en: And then text, language doesn’t come in until a year in life.

cues.zh: 到九岁时，你已经了解了重力，知道了惯性，懂得了重力、稳定性，也知道了有生命物体和无生命物体的区别。
cues.en: And by the time you are nine years old, you’ve learned about gravity, you know about inertia, you know about gravity, the stability, you know about the distinction between animate and inanimate objects.

cues.zh: 你知道，到18个月大时，你就明白人们为什么想做事情，并且如果他们做不到，你会帮助他们。
cues.en: You know by 18 months, you know about why people want to do things and you help them if they can’t.

cues.zh: 我是说，有很多东西你主要是通过观察学到的，甚至不是通过互动。
cues.en: I mean, there’s a lot of things that you learn mostly by observation, really not even through interaction.

cues.zh: 在生命的最初几个月里，婴儿对世界其实没有任何影响力，他们只能观察。
cues.en: In the first few months of life, babies don’t really have any influence on the world, they can only observe.

cues.zh: 你就这样积累了大量的知识。
cues.en: And you accumulate a gigantic amount of knowledge just from that.

cues.zh: 所以这就是当前AI系统所缺失的。
cues.en: So that’s what we’re missing from current AI systems.

cues.zh: 我想在你的一个幻灯片中，有一个很好的图表，这是你展示LLMs有限的方式之一。
cues.en: I think in one of your slides, you have this nice plot that is one of the ways you show that LLMs are limited.

cues.zh: 我想请你从你的角度谈谈幻觉，为什么大语言模型会产生幻觉，以及这在多大程度上是大语言模型的根本缺陷？
cues.en: I wonder if you could talk about hallucinations from your perspectives, the why hallucinations happen from large language models and to what degree is that a fundamental flaw of large language models?

cues.zh: 对，因为自回归预测，每次生成一个 token 或一个词时，这个词都有一定概率把你带出合理答案的集合。
cues.en: Right, so because of the autoregressive prediction, every time an produces a token or a word, there is some level of probability for that word to take you out of the set of reasonable answers.

cues.zh: 如果你假设——这是个很强的假设——这种错误的概率是，这些错误在生成的 token 序列之间是独立的。
cues.en: And if you assume, which is a very strong assumption, that the probability of such error is that those errors are independent across a sequence of tokens being produced.

cues.zh: 这意味着，每生成一个 token，你留在正确答案集合内的概率就会下降，而且是指数级下降。
cues.en: What that means is that every time you produce a token, the probability that you stay within the set of correct answer decreases and it decreases exponentially.

cues.zh: 所以正如你所说，这里有一个很强的假设：如果犯错存在非零概率——看起来确实如此——那就会出现某种漂移。
cues.en: So there’s a strong, like you said, assumption there that if there’s a non-zero probability of making a mistake, which there appears to be, then there’s going to be a kind of drift.

cues.zh: 是的，而且这种漂移是指数级的。
cues.en: Yeah, and that drift is exponential.

cues.zh: 就像错误会累积一样。
cues.en: It’s like errors accumulate.

cues.zh: 所以一个答案变得毫无意义的概率，会随着 token 数量的增加而指数级上升。
cues.en: So the probability that an answer would be nonsensical increases exponentially with the number of tokens.

cues.zh: 顺便问一下，这对你来说显而易见吗？
cues.en: Is that obvious to you, by the way?

cues.zh: 嗯，从数学上讲也许是的，但难道不存在一种朝向真相的引力吗？
cues.en: Well, mathematically speaking maybe, but isn’t there a kind of gravitational pull towards the truth?

cues.zh: 因为平均而言，希望真相在训练集中得到了很好的体现？
cues.en: Because on average, hopefully, the truth is well represented in the training set?

cues.zh: 不，这基本上是一场对抗维度灾难的斗争。
cues.en: No, it’s basically a struggle against the curse of dimensionality.

cues.zh: 所以你可以纠正这一点的方法是，通过让系统为人们可能提出的各种问题生成答案，来对它进行微调。
cues.en: So the way you can correct for this is that you fine tune the system by having it produce answers for all kinds of questions that people might come up with.

cues.zh: 让它能为人们可能提出的各种问题给出答案。
cues.en: Having it produce answers for all kinds of questions that people might come up with.

cues.zh: 而人就是人，所以他们提出的很多问题彼此非常相似，所以你大概能覆盖人们会问的80%左右的问题，方法是收集数据，然后微调系统，让它对所有这些都能给出好答案，而且它大概能学会，因为它有很大的学习容量。
cues.en: And people are people, so a lot of the questions that they have are very similar to each other, so you can probably cover 80% or whatever of questions that people will ask by collecting data and then you fine tune the system to produce good answers for all of those things, and it’s probably going to be able to learn that because it’s got a lot of capacity to learn.

cues.zh: 但还有一大类提示词是你在训练中没有覆盖到的，而且那个集合极其庞大，比如在所有可能的提示词集合中，用于训练的提示词比例绝对微乎其微，它只是所有可能提示词中一个极小、极小、极小的子集。
cues.en: But then there is the enormous set of prompts that you have not covered during training, and that set is enormous, like within the set of all possible prompts, the proportion of prompts that have been used for training is absolutely tiny, it’s a tiny, tiny, tiny subset of all possible prompts.

cues.zh: 因此，系统在那些经过训练、预训练或微调的提示上会表现正常，但存在一个巨大的空间，是它不可能被训练到的，因为数量太庞大了。
cues.en: And so the system will behave properly on the prompts that has been either trained, pre-trained, or fine-tuned, but then there is an entire space of things that it cannot possibly have been trained on because the number is gigantic.

cues.zh: 所以，无论系统接受了何种训练以产生合适的答案，你都可以通过找到一个超出训练集范围的提示，或者类似的东西来打破它，然后它就会胡言乱语。
cues.en: So whatever training the system has been subject to produce appropriate answers, you can break it by finding out a prompt that will be outside of the set of prompts that’s been trained on, or things that are similar, and then it will just spew complete nonsense.

cues.zh: 当你说提示时，你是指那个确切的提示，还是指一个在许多部分都非常不同的提示？
cues.en: When you say prompt, do you mean that exact prompt or do you mean a prompt that’s in many parts, very different than?

cues.zh: 问一个问题或说一件以前在互联网上没被说过的事情，真的那么容易吗？
cues.en: Is it that easy to ask a question or to say a thing that hasn’t been said before on the internet?

cues.zh: 有人想出这样的办法：在提示里放入一串基本随机的字符，就足以让系统进入某种模式，给出与没有这些字符时完全不同的回答。
cues.en: People have come up with things where you put essentially a random sequence of characters in the prompt and that’s enough to throw the system into a mode where it is going to answer something completely different than it would have answered without this.

cues.zh: 这就是一种越狱系统的方式，基本上是跳出它的条件设定。
cues.en: So that’s a way to jailbreak the system, basically go outside of its conditioning.

cues.zh: 这是一个非常清楚的演示，但当然，这超出了它被设计来做的事情，对吧？
cues.en: That’s a very clear demonstration of it, but of course, that goes outside of what is designed to do, right?

cues.zh: 如果你实际上拼接出语法还算合理的句子，还那么容易攻破它吗？
cues.en: If you actually stitch together reasonably grammatical sentences, is it that easy to break it?

cues.zh: 是的，有人做过这样的事：你用英语写一句话或问一个问题，它给出一个完全正常的回答，然后你只是把几个词替换成另一种语言里的同一个词，突然间回答就完全不知所云了。
cues.en: Yeah, some people have done things like, you write a sentence in English or you ask a question in English and it produces a perfectly fine answer and then you just substitute a few words by the same word in another language and all of a sudden the answer is complete nonsense.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，人类可能生成的提示词中，有多大比例会导致系统崩溃？
cues.en: What I’m saying is, which fraction of prompts that humans are likely to generate are going to break the system?

cues.zh: 问题在于存在长尾，这是很多人在社交网络之类的地方已经意识到的问题，也就是人们会问的东西有一个非常非常长的长尾，而你可以针对大多数人会问的那80%左右的内容来微调系统。
cues.en: The problem is that there is a long tail, this is an issue that a lot of people have realized in social networks and stuff like that, which is there’s a very, very long tail of things that people will ask and you can fine tune the system for the 80% or whatever of the things that most people will ask.

cues.zh: 而这个长尾太大了，你没法针对所有情况来微调系统。
cues.en: And then this long tail is so large that you’re not going to be able to fine tune the system for all the conditions.

cues.zh: 最终，系统基本上就变成了一个巨大的查找表，而这并不是你真正想要的，你想要的是能够推理、当然也能规划的系统。
cues.en: And in the end, the system ends up being a giant lookup table essentially, which is not really what you want, you want systems that can reason, certainly that can plan.

cues.zh: LLM中进行的推理类型非常非常原始，你能看出它原始的原因在于，每生成一个token所花费的计算量是恒定的。
cues.en: The type of reasoning that takes place in LLM is very, very primitive, and the reason you can tell is primitive is because the amount of computation that is spent per token produced is constant.

cues.zh: 所以如果你提出一个问题，而这个问题在给定数量的 token 内有答案，那么用于计算该答案的计算量是可以精确估算的。
cues.en: So if you ask a question and that question has an answer in a given number of token, the amount of computation devoted to computing that answer can be exactly estimated.

cues.zh: 就是预测网络的规模，36 层也好，92 层也好，不管多少层，乘以 token 数量，就这么简单。
cues.en: It’s the size of the prediction network with its 36 layers or 92 layers or whatever it is multiply by number of tokens, that’s it.

cues.zh: 所以本质上，无论所问的问题是简单、复杂，还是因为不可判定之类的原因而无法回答，都无所谓，系统能够投入到答案上的计算量是恒定的，或者与答案中生成的 token 数量成正比。
cues.en: And so essentially, it doesn’t matter if the question being asked is simple to answer, complicated to answer, impossible to answer because it’s a decidable or something, the amount of computation the system will be able to devote to the answer is constant or is proportional to number of token produced in the answer.

cues.zh: 我们不是这样工作的，我们的推理方式是，当面对复杂的问题或复杂的疑问时，我们会花更多时间去尝试解决和回答，因为它更难。
cues.en: This is not the way we work, the way we reason is that when we’re faced with a complex problem or a complex question, we spend more time trying to solve it and answer it because it’s more difficult.

cues.zh: 这里面有预测成分，有迭代成分，通过反复不断地调整对事物的理解，还有分层成分。
cues.en: There’s a prediction element, there’s an iterative element where you’re adjusting your understanding of a thing by going over and over and over, there’s a hierarchical elements on.

cues.zh: 这是否意味着这是大语言模型的根本缺陷，还是说——
cues.en: Does this mean it’s a fundamental flaw of LLMs or does it mean that-

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: ……这个问题还有更多部分，你现在就像大语言模型一样，立刻就回答了。
cues.en: … There’s more part to that question, now you’re just behaving like an LLM, immediately answering.

cues.zh: 不，这只是底层的世界模型，在此基础上我们可以构建一些这类机制，比如你说的持久长期记忆或推理等等。
cues.en: No, that it’s just the low level world model on top of which we can then build some of these kinds of mechanisms, like you said, persistent long-term memory or reasoning, so on.

cues.zh: 但我们需要那个来自语言的世界模型。
cues.en: But we need that world model that comes from language.

cues.zh: 也许在构建良好的世界模型之上构建这种推理系统并不那么困难。
cues.en: Maybe it is not so difficult to build this kind of reasoning system on top of a well constructed world model.

cues.zh: 难不难，不久的将来会给出答案，因为很多人正在研究对话系统的推理和规划能力。
cues.en: Whether it’s difficult or not, the near future will say because a lot of people are working on reasoning and planning abilities for dialogue systems.

cues.zh: 即便我们只谈语言，仅仅具备在回答之前规划答案的能力，而且这种规划所用的形式不一定与你最终用来生成答案的语言挂钩，也就是说，这种心智模型让你在开口之前就能规划好要说什么，这一点非常重要。
cues.en: Even if we restrict ourselves to language, just having the ability to plan your answer before you answer in terms that are not necessarily linked with the language you’re going to use to produce the answer, so this idea of this mental model that allows you to plan what you’re going to say before you say it, that is very important.

cues.zh: 我认为未来几年会出现很多具备这种能力的系统，但这些系统的蓝图将与自回归式 LLM 截然不同。
cues.en: I think there’s going to be a lot of systems over the next few years that are going to have this capability, but the blueprint of those systems will be extremely different from auto aggressive LLMs.

cues.zh: 这与心理学家所说的人类“系统一”和“系统二”之间的区别是一样的。系统一是指那些你不需要刻意有意识地思考怎么做就能完成的任务，你就是直接去做，因为你已经做过足够多次，可以下意识地完成，而不需要去想它们。
cues.en: It’s the same difference as the difference between what psychologists call system one and system two in humans, so system one is the type of task that you can accomplish without deliberately consciously think about how you do them, you just do them, you’ve done them enough that you can just do it subconsciously without thinking about them.

cues.zh: 如果你是经验丰富的司机，开车时几乎不用思考，还能同时跟人聊天或听收音机。
cues.en: If you’re an experienced driver, you can drive without really thinking about it and you can talk to someone at the same time or listen to the radio.

cues.zh: 如果你是非常有经验的棋手，跟没经验的棋手对弈时也几乎不用思考，只需识别模式然后落子。
cues.en: If you are a very experienced chess player, you can play against a non- experienced chess player without really thinking either, you just recognize the pattern and you play.

cues.zh: 这就是系统一，也就是所有你凭本能去做、不需要刻意计划和思考的事情。
cues.en: That’s system one, so all the things that you do instinctively without really having to deliberately plan and think about it.

cues.zh: 然后还有一类任务需要你规划，比如你棋艺不算太精，或者你是老手但对上另一个老手，你会考虑各种选项，想上一会儿，如果有时间思考，你会比在限时快棋中表现好得多。
cues.en: And then there is all the tasks where you need to plan, so if you are a not too experienced chess player or you are experienced where you play against another experienced chess player, you think about all kinds of options, you think about it for a while and you are much better if you have time to think about it than you are if you play blitz with limited time.

cues.zh: 这种有意识的规划，用到了你内部的世界模型，这就是系统二，也是LMS目前做不到的。
cues.en: So this type of deliberate planning, which uses your internal world model, that’s system two, this is what LMS currently cannot do.

cues.zh: 我们怎么让它们做到这一点？
cues.en: How do we get them to do this?

cues.zh: 我们怎么构建一个系统，能进行这种规划或推理，对复杂问题投入比简单问题更多的资源？
cues.en: How do we build a system that can do this kind of planning or reasoning that devotes more resources to complex problems than to simple problems?

cues.zh: 它不会是对token的回归式预测，而更接近于对小型变量的推断，也就是过去所谓的概率模型或图模型之类的东西。
cues.en: And it’s not going to be a regressive prediction of tokens, it’s going to be more something akin to inference of little variables in what used to be called probabilistic models or graphical models and things of that type.

cues.zh: 原理基本上是这样的：提示就像观测变量，而模型所做的，基本上就是衡量一个答案在多大程度上是提示的好答案。
cues.en: Basically, the principle is like this, the prompt is like observed variables, and what the model does, is that basically, it can measure to what extent an answer is a good answer for a prompt.

cues.zh: 可以把它想象成一个巨大的神经网络，但它只有一个输出，这个输出是一个标量数值，比如说，如果答案是对问题的好答案，它就是零；如果答案不是好答案，它就是一个大数。
cues.en: So think of it as some gigantic neural net, but it’s got only one output, and that output is a scaler number, which is, let’s say, zero, if the answer is a good answer for the question and a large number, if the answer is not a good answer for the question.

cues.zh: 想象你有这个模型，如果你有这样的模型，你就可以用它来生成好答案，做法是给出提示，然后在可能的答案空间里搜索，找到能让那个数值最小的答案，这就叫基于能量的模型。
cues.en: Imagine you had this model, if you had such a model, you could use it to produce good answers, the way you would do is, produce the prompt and then search through the space of possible answers for one that minimizes that number, that’s called an energy based model.

cues.zh: 但这个基于能量的模型需要由 LLM 构建的模型吗？
cues.en: But that energy based model would need the model constructed by the LLM?

cues.zh: 其实你真正需要做的，不是去搜索能最小化那个能量的可能文本串。
cues.en: Well, so really what you need to do would be to not search over possible strings of text that minimize that energy.

cues.zh: 但你要做的是，我们在抽象表示空间里做这件事，也就是在抽象思维的空间里，你会通过最小化模型输出的过程来展开一个想法，而模型输出只是一个标量，这是一个优化过程。
cues.en: But what you would do, we do this in abstract representation space, so in the space of abstract thoughts, you would elaborate a thought using this process of minimizing the output of your model, which is just a scaler, it’s an optimization process.

cues.zh: 所以现在系统产生其传感器的方式，基本上就是通过最小化一个目标函数来进行优化。
cues.en: So now the way the system produces its sensor is through optimization by minimizing an objective function basically.

cues.zh: 我们说的是推理，不是训练，系统已经训练好了。
cues.en: And we’re talking about inference, we’re not talking about training, the system has been trained already.

cues.zh: 现在我们有了答案想法的抽象表示，也就是答案的表示，我们把它喂给一个基本的自回归解码器，这个解码器可以非常简单，它把这个表示转换成表达这个想法的文本。
cues.en: Now we have an abstract representation of the thought of the answer, representation of the answer, we feed that to basically an autoregressive decoder, which can be very simple, that turns this into a text that expresses this thought.

cues.zh: 所以在我看来，这就是未来数据系统的蓝图，它们会先思考答案，在转化为文本之前通过优化来规划答案，而这是图灵完备的。
cues.en: So that, in my opinion, is the blueprint of future data systems, they will think about their answer, plan their answer by optimization before turning it into text, and that is turning complete.

cues.zh: 你能具体解释一下那里的优化问题是什么吗？
cues.en: Can you explain exactly what the optimization problem there is?

cues.zh: 目标函数是什么？
cues.en: What’s the objective function?

cues.zh: 再仔细讲讲，你简要描述过，但你是在什么空间上进行优化的？
cues.en: Just linger on it, you briefly described it, but over what space are you optimizing?

cues.zh: 表示空间。
cues.en: The space of representations.

cues.zh: 是抽象表示吗？
cues.en: It goes abstract representation?

cues.zh: 系统内部有一个抽象表示，你有一个提示，提示经过编码器，产生一个表示，也许经过一个预测器，预测出合适答案的表示。
cues.en: You have an abstract representation inside the system, you have a prompt, the prompt goes through an encoder, produces a representation, perhaps goes through a predictor that predicts a representation of the proper answer.

cues.zh: 但这个表示可能不是好答案，因为可能需要做一些复杂的推理，所以还有另一个过程，它接收答案的表示并对其进行修改，以最小化一个代价函数，该函数衡量答案在多大程度上是问题的好答案。
cues.en: But that representation may not be a good answer because there might be some complicated reasoning you need to do, so then you have another process that takes the representation of the answers and modifies it so as to minimize a cost function that measures to what extent the answer is a good answer for the question.

cues.zh: 现在我们暂时忽略如何训练这个系统来衡量答案是否足够好的问题。
cues.en: Now we ignore the issue for a moment of how you train that system to measure whether an answer is a good answer for a fraction.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 假设这样的系统能够被创造出来，那么这个搜索过程是什么样的？
cues.en: Suppose such a system could be created, but what’s this search like process?

cues.zh: 这是一个优化过程。
cues.en: It’s an optimization process.

cues.zh: 如果整个系统都是可微的，你就可以做到这一点，那个标量输出就是运行答案表示经过某个神经网络的结果。
cues.en: You can do this if the entire system is differentiable, that scaler output is the result of running the representation of the answers to some neural net.

cues.zh: 然后通过梯度下降，通过反向传播梯度，你可以找出如何修改答案的表示以最小化那个值。
cues.en: Then by gradient descent, by back propagating gradients, you can figure out how to modify the representation of the answers so as to minimize that.

cues.zh: 这仍然是基于梯度的吗？
cues.en: That’s still a gradient based?

cues.zh: 这是基于梯度的推理。
cues.en: It’s gradient based inference.

cues.zh: 所以现在你在抽象空间中有了答案的表示，现在你可以把它转换成文本。
cues.en: So now you have a representation of the answer in abstract space, now you can turn it into text.

cues.zh: 这很酷的一点是，这个表示现在可以通过梯度下降进行优化，同时也独立于你用来表达答案的语言。
cues.en: And the cool thing about this is that the representation now can be optimized through gradient descent, but also is independent of the language in which you’re going to express the answer.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 所以你是在减法表示中运作的。
cues.en: So you’re operating in the subtract representation.

cues.zh: 这要追溯到联合嵌入，最好在那个空间里工作，我也不确定，或者把这个概念浪漫化一点，叫概念空间与具体感官信息空间。
cues.en: This goes back to the joint embedding, that it’s better to work in the space of, I don’t know, or to romanticize the notion like space of concepts versus the space of concrete sensory information.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 但这个东西能做类似推理的事情吗，也就是我们正在讨论的？
cues.en: But can this do something like reasoning, which is what we’re talking about?

cues.zh: 嗯，不太能，只能以非常简单的方式。
cues.en: Well, not really, only in a very simple way.

cues.zh: 基本上，你可以把这些东西看作是在做我提到的优化，只不过它们是在离散空间中优化，也就是可能的 token 序列空间。
cues.en: Basically, you can think of those things as doing the optimization I was talking about, except they optimize in the discrete space, which is the space of possible sequences of tokens.

cues.zh: 而且它们做这种优化的方式极其低效，就是生成大量假设，然后选出最好的。
cues.en: And they do this optimization in a horribly inefficient way, which is generate a lot of hypothesis and then select the best ones.

cues.zh: 这在算力竞争上极其浪费，因为你基本上得为每一个可能的生成序列都跑一遍 LLM，这极其浪费。
cues.en: And that’s incredibly wasteful in terms of competition because you basically have to run your LLM for every possible generative sequence and it’s incredibly wasteful.

cues.zh: 所以在连续空间里做优化要好得多，你可以做梯度和下降，而不是生成一大堆东西再挑最好的，你只需迭代地改进答案，朝最优解靠近，这样效率高得多。
cues.en: So it’s much better to do an optimization in continuous space where you can do gradient and descent as opposed to generate tons of things and then select the best, you just iteratively refine your answer to go towards the best, that’s much more efficient.

cues.zh: 但你只能在连续空间里、用可微函数来做这件事。
cues.en: But you can only do this in continuous spaces with differentiable functions.

cues.zh: 你说的是深度思考或深度推理的能力，那你怎么知道基于深度推理，哪个答案更好、哪个更差？
cues.en: You’re talking about the ability to think deeply or to reason deeply, how do you know what is an answer that’s better or worse based on deep reasoning?

cues.zh: 那我们就得问一个概念性的问题：怎么训练一个基于能量的模型？
cues.en: Then we are asking the question of, conceptually, how do you train an energy based model?

cues.zh: 基于能量的模型是一个输出标量的函数，就是一个数，你给它两个输入 X 和 Y，它告诉你 Y 是否与 X 相容。
cues.en: Energy based model is a function with a scaler output, just a number, you give it two inputs, X and Y, and it tells you whether Y is compatible with X or not.

cues.zh: X，你观察到，比如说它是一个提示、一张图像、一段视频，随便什么，而 Y 是一个候选答案、视频的延续，随便什么，它会告诉你 Y 是否与 X 相容。
cues.en: X, you observe, let’s say it’s a prompt, an image, a video, whatever, and Y is a proposal for an answer, a continuation of video, whatever and it tells you whether Y is compatible with X.

cues.zh: 它告诉你 Y 与 X 相容的方式是，如果 Y 与 X 相容，该函数的输出为零；如果 Y 与 X 不相容，输出为一个正数、非零。
cues.en: And the way it tells you that Y is compatible with X is that the output of that function would be zero if Y is compatible with X and would be a positive number, non-zero, if Y is not compatible with X.

cues.zh: 如何在一个完全通用的层面上训练这样的系统，就是给它展示相容的 X 和 Y 对，一个问题及对应的答案，然后训练内部大型神经网络的参数使其输出零。
cues.en: How do you train a system like this at a completely general level, is you show it pairs of X and Ys that are compatible, a question and the corresponding answer, and you train the parameters of the big neural net inside to produce zero.

cues.zh: 但这并不完全奏效，因为系统可能会决定，好吧，我就对一切都说零，所以现在你必须有一个流程来确保对于错误的 Y，能量会大于零。
cues.en: Now that doesn’t completely work because the system might decide, well, I’m just going to say zero for everything, so now you have to have a process to make sure that for a wrong Y, the energy would be larger than zero.

cues.zh: 这里你有两个选择，一个是对比方法，对比方法就是，你展示一个X和一个糟糕的Y，然后告诉系统，给这个高的能量，推高能量，改变神经网络中让能量混乱的权重，使能量上升。
cues.en: And there you have two options, one is contrastive method, so contrastive method is, you show an X and a bad Y and you tell the system, well, give a high energy to this, push up the energy, change the weights in the neural net that confuse the energy so that it goes up.

cues.zh: 这就是对比方法。
cues.en: So that’s contrasting methods.

cues.zh: 问题在于，如果Y的空间很大，需要展示的对比样本数量将会非常庞大。
cues.en: The problem with this is, if the space of Y is large, the number of such contrasting samples are going to have to show is gigantic.

cues.zh: 但人们确实这么做，训练RLHF系统时就是这么做的，基本上你训练的是一个所谓的奖励模型，它本质上是一个目标函数，告诉你一个答案是好是坏，而这基本上就是对比方法。
cues.en: But people do this, they do this when you train a system with RLHF, basically what you’re training is what’s called a reward model, which is basically an objective function that tells you whether an answer is good or bad, and that’s basically exactly what this is.

cues.zh: 所以我们已经在某种程度上这么做了，只是没有用于推理，只是用于训练。
cues.en: So we already do this to some extent, we’re just not using it for inference, we’re just using it for training.

cues.zh: 还有另一类方法是非对比式的，我更喜欢这些方法。这些非对比式方法的基本思路是：能量函数需要在来自训练集的、相互兼容的 XY 对上具有低能量。
cues.en: There is another set of methods which are non-contrastive, and I prefer those, and those non-contrastive methods basically say, the energy function needs to have low energy on pairs of XYs that are compatible that come from your training set.

cues.zh: 你如何确保在其他所有地方能量都会更高？
cues.en: How do you make sure that the energy is going to be higher everywhere else?

cues.zh: 做法是引入一个正则化项，也就是代价函数中的一个准则、一个项，它基本上会最小化能取低能量的空间体积。
cues.en: And the way you do this is by having a regularizer, a criterion, a term in your cost function that basically minimizes the volume of space that can take low energy.

cues.zh: 具体实现方式因架构而异，有各种不同的具体做法，但这就是基本原理。
cues.en: And the precise way to do this is all kinds of different specific ways to do this depending on the architecture, but that’s the basic principle.

cues.zh: 这样一来，如果你把 XY 空间中特定区域的能量函数压低，其他地方的能​​量就会自动升高，因为根据系统的构造或正则化函数，能取低能量的空间体积是有限的。
cues.en: So that if you push down the energy function for particular regions in the XY space, it will automatically go up in other places because there’s only a limited volume of space that can take low energy by the construction of the system or by the regularizing function.

cues.zh: 我们一直在很笼统地讨论，但什么是好的X和好的Y？
cues.en: We’ve been talking very generally, but what is a good X and a good Y?

cues.zh: X和Y的良好表示是什么？
cues.en: What is a good representation of X and Y?

cues.zh: 因为我们一直在讨论语言，如果你直接拿语言来用，那大概不行，所以必须要有某种对思想的抽象表示。
cues.en: Because we’ve been talking about language and if you just take language directly that presumably is not good, so there has to be some kind of abstract representation of ideas.

cues.zh: 你可以直接用语言来做，就是X是一段文本，Y是这段文本的延续。
cues.en: You can do this with language directly by just, X is a text and Y is a continuation of that text.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 或者X是一个问题，Y是答案。
cues.en: Or X is a question, Y is the answer.

cues.zh: 但你说那样不行，那只会做LLM正在做的事。
cues.en: But you’re saying that’s not going to take it, that’s going to do what LLMs are doing.

cues.zh: 不，这取决于系统的内部结构是如何构建的。
cues.en: Well, no, it depends on how the internal structure of the system is built.

cues.zh: 如果系统的内部结构是这样构建的：系统内部有一个潜在变量，我们称之为Z，你可以操纵它来最小化输出能量，那么Z就可以被视为一个好答案的表示，你可以把它翻译成一个好答案Y。
cues.en: If the internal structure of the system is built in such a way that inside of the system there is a latent variable, let’s call it Z, that you can manipulate so as to minimize the output energy, then that Z can be viewed as a representation of a good answer that you can translate into a Y that is a good answer.

cues.zh: 这个系统能用非常相似的方式训练吗？
cues.en: This system could be trained in a very similar way?

cues.zh: 方式非常相似，但必须用这种方法防止崩溃，确保对没有训练过的东西保持高能量。
cues.en: Very similar way, but you have to have this way preventing collapse of ensuring that there is high energy for things you don’t train it on.

cues.zh: 目前这在LLM中非常隐式，实现方式让人意识不到，但确实在做。
cues.en: And currently, it’s very implicit in LLM, it’s done in a way that people don’t realize it’s being done, but it is being done.

cues.zh: 这是因为当你给一个词高概率时，自动就会给其他词低概率，因为你能分配的概率总量有限，必须加起来等于一。
cues.en: It is due to the fact that when you give a high probability to a word, automatically, you give low probability to other words because you only have a finite amount of probability to go around right there to sum to one.

cues.zh: 所以当你最小化交叉熵之类的指标，训练LLM预测下一个词时，你是在提高系统给正确词的概率，但同时也在降低给错误词的概率。
cues.en: So when you minimize the cross entropy or whatever, when you train your LLM to predict the next word, you are increasing the probability your system will give to the correct word, but you’re also decreasing the probability it will give to the incorrect words.

cues.zh: 间接来说，这会给好的词序列高概率、给坏的词序列低概率，但这个机制非常间接。
cues.en: Now, indirectly, that gives a high probability to sequences of words that are good and low probability to sequences of words that are bad, but it’s very indirect.

cues.zh: 而且它为什么能奏效并不显然，因为你并不是在所有符号的联合概率上做这件事，而是把那个概率按连续 token 的条件概率分解了。
cues.en: And it’s not obvious why this actually works at all because you’re not doing it on the joint probability of all the symbols in a sequence, you factorize that probability in terms of conditional probabilities over successive tokens.

cues.zh: 那对视觉数据你怎么做这件事？
cues.en: How do you do this for visual data?

cues.zh: 我们一直用 I-JEPA 架构做这件事，基本上——
cues.en: We’ve been doing this with I-JEPA architectures, basically-

cues.zh: 联合嵌入。
cues.en: The joint embedding.

cues.zh: ……I-JEPA。
cues.en: … I-JEPA.

cues.zh: 所以那里两样东西之间的兼容性是，这里是一张图像或一段视频，这里是那张图像或视频的损坏、偏移或变换版本，或者被掩码的版本。
cues.en: So there the compatibility between two things is, here’s an image or a video, here is a corrupted, shifted or transformed version of that image or video or masked.

cues.zh: 然后系统的能量，就是“好东西”的预测表示与实际表示之间的预测误差。
cues.en: And then the energy of the system is the prediction error of the predicted representation of the good thing versus the actual representation of the good thing.

cues.zh: 你把损坏的图像输入系统，预测未损坏的好输入的表示，然后计算预测误差，这就是系统的能量。
cues.en: So you run the corrupted image to the system, predict the representation of the good input uncorrupted, and then compute the prediction error, that’s the energy of the system.

cues.zh: 所以这个系统会告诉你，如果这是一张好图像，而这是它的损坏版本，当这两者实际上一个是另一个的损坏版本时，它会给出零能量；如果两张图像完全不同，它会给出高能量。
cues.en: So this system will tell you if this is a good image and this is a corrupted version, it will give you zero energy if those two things, effectively, one of them is a corrupted version of the other, it gives you a high energy if the two images are completely different.

cues.zh: 希望整个过程能为你提供视觉现实的一个非常好的压缩表示？
cues.en: And hopefully that whole process gives you a really nice compressed representation of a visual reality?

cues.zh: 我们知道它确实能做到，因为之后我们把那些表示作为分类系统的输入之类的东西，而且它有效。
cues.en: And we know it does because then we use those representations as input to a classification system or something and that it works.

cues.zh: 然后那个分类系统运行得非常好，对吧。
cues.en: And then that classification system works really nicely, okay.

cues.zh: 那么总结一下，你用 Yann LeCun 特有的犀利方式建议我们放弃生成模型，转而采用联合嵌入架构？
cues.en: Well, so to summarize, you recommend in a spicy way that only Yann LeCun can, you recommend that we abandon generative models in favor of joint embedding architectures?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 放弃自回归生成。
cues.en: Abandon autoregressive generation.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 这感觉像法庭证词，放弃概率模型，转而采用我们谈到的基于能量的模型，放弃对比方法，转而采用正则化方法。
cues.en: This feels like court testimony, abandon probabilistic models in favor of energy based models as we talked about, abandon contrastive methods in favor of regularized methods.

cues.zh: 让我问问你，你一直对强化学习持批评态度。
cues.en: And let me ask you about this, you’ve been for a while, a critic of reinforcement learning.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 最后一条建议是，放弃强化学习，转而采用你提到的模型预测控制，只在规划未能产生预期结果时才使用强化学习，用强化学习来调整世界模型或评判器。
cues.en: The last recommendation is that we abandon RL in favor of model predictive control, as you were talking about, and only use RL when planning doesn’t yield the predicted outcome, and we use RL in that case to adjust the world model or the critic.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 你提到了 RLHF，即基于人类反馈的强化学习，那你为什么还是不喜欢强化学习？
cues.en: You’ve mentioned RLHF, reinforcement learning with human feedback, why do you still hate reinforcement learning?

cues.zh: 我并不讨厌强化学习，而且我认为——
cues.en: I don’t hate reinforcement learning, and I think-

cues.zh: 那全是爱，是的。
cues.en: It’s all love, yes.

cues.zh: ……我认为它不应该被完全抛弃，但我认为它的使用应该被最小化，因为它在样本效率上极其低下。
cues.en: … I think it should not be abandoned completely, but I think it’s use should be minimized because it’s incredibly inefficient in terms of samples.

cues.zh: 因此，训练一个系统的正确方式是，首先让它主要从观察中，也许加上少量交互，学习到世界的良好表征和世界模型。
cues.en: And so the proper way to train a system is to first have it learn good representations of the world and world models from mostly observation, maybe a little bit of interactions.

cues.zh: 然后在此基础上进行引导，如果表征是好的，那么调整应该是最小的。
cues.en: And then steered based on that, if the representation is good, then the adjustments should be minimal.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 现在有两点，如果你已经学到了一个世界模型，你可以利用这个模型来规划一系列动作以达到特定目标，你不需要强化学习，除非你衡量成功的方式可能不精确。
cues.en: Now there’s two things, if you’ve learned a world model, you can use the world model to plan a sequence of actions to arrive at a particular objective, you don’t need RL unless the way you measure whether you succeed might be in exact.

cues.zh: 你觉得会不会从自行车上摔下来，这个判断可能是错的；或者你在跟人打MMA，以为对方要出这招，结果他出了别的招。
cues.en: Your idea of whether you are going to fall from your bike might be wrong, or whether the person you’re fighting with MMA who’s going to do something and they do something else.

cues.zh: 所以出错有两种方式：要么你的目标函数没有反映你真正想优化的实际目标，要么你的世界模型不准确，也就是你对世界接下来会发生什么的预测不准确。
cues.en: So there’s two ways you can be wrong, either your objective function does not reflect the actual objective function you want to optimize or your world model is inaccurate, so the prediction you were making about what was going to happen in the world is inaccurate.

cues.zh: 如果你想在身处世界中行动的同时调整你的世界模型或目标函数，这基本就属于强化学习的范畴，强化学习在某种程度上就是处理这个的，也就是调整你的世界模型。
cues.en: If you want to adjust your world model while you are operating in the world or your objective function, that is basically in the realm of RL, this is what RL deals with to some extent, so adjust your word model.

cues.zh: 而提前调整世界模型的办法，就是去探索那些你知道自己世界模型不准确的空间区域，这基本上就叫好奇心，或者叫玩耍。
cues.en: And the way to adjust your word model even in advance is to explore parts of the space where you know that your world model is inaccurate, that’s called curiosity basically, or play.

cues.zh: 当你玩耍时，你会探索空间中那些你不想真正去做的部分，因为可能有危险，但你基本上可以在不伤害自己的情况下调整你的世界模型。
cues.en: When you play, you explore parts of the space that you don’t want to do for real because it might be dangerous, but you can adjust your world model without killing yourself basically.

cues.zh: 所以这就是你想用强化学习的地方，当需要学习特定任务时，你已经有好的表征，你已经有世界模型，但你需要根据当前情况调整它，这时你就用强化学习。
cues.en: So that’s what you want to use RL for, when it comes time to learning a particular task, you already have all the good representations, you already have your world model, but you need to adjust it for the situation at hand, that’s when you use RL.

cues.zh: 你认为为什么基于人类反馈的强化学习效果这么好？
cues.en: Why do you think RLHF works so well?

cues.zh: 这种基于人类反馈的强化学习，为什么它对大型语言模型产生了如此变革性的影响？
cues.en: This enforcement learning with human feedback, why did it have such a transformational effect on large language models than before?

cues.zh: 产生变革性影响的是人类反馈，有很多方法可以使用它，其中一些纯粹是监督式的，实际上，并不是真正的强化学习。
cues.en: What’s had the transformational effect is human feedback, there is many ways to use it, and some of it is just purely supervised, actually, it’s not really reinforcement learning.

cues.zh: 是HF吗？
cues.en: It’s the HF?

cues.zh: 是HF，然后有多种利用人类反馈的方法。
cues.en: It’s the HF, and then there is various ways to use human feedback.

cues.zh: 你可以让人类对世界模型生成的多个答案进行评分，然后训练一个目标函数来预测这个评分，接着用这个目标函数预测答案的好坏，并通过反向传播梯度来微调你的系统，使其只生成高评分的答案。
cues.en: So you can ask humans to rate multiple answers that are produced by world model, and then what you do is you train an objective function to predict that rating, and then you can use that objective function to predict whether an answer is good and you can back propagate gradient to this to fine tune your system so that it only produces highly rated answers.

cues.zh: 这是一种方法，在强化学习中，这意味着训练所谓的奖励模型，基本上就是一个小型神经网络，用来估计答案有多好。
cues.en: That’s one way, so in RL, that means training what’s called a reward model, so something that basically is a small neural net that estimates to what extent an answer is good.

cues.zh: 这与我之前讨论的规划目标非常相似，只不过现在它不是用于规划，而是用于微调你的系统。
cues.en: It’s very similar to the objective I was talking about earlier for planning, except now it’s not used for planning, it’s used for fine-tuning your system.

cues.zh: 我认为用它来做规划会高效得多，但目前它被用来微调系统的参数。
cues.en: I think it would be much more efficient to use it for planning, but currently, it’s used to fine tune the parameters of the system.

cues.zh: 有几种方法可以做到这一点，其中一些是有监督的，你只需问一个人，比如，这个问题的好答案是什么？
cues.en: There’s several ways to do this, some of them are supervised, you just ask a human person like, what is a good answer for this?

cues.zh: 然后你就把答案打进去。
cues.en: Then you just type the answer.

cues.zh: 这些系统有很多种调整方式。
cues.en: There’s lots of ways that those systems are being adjusted.

cues.zh: 现在，很多人对最近发布的 Google Gemini 1.5 提出了严厉批评，用我的话来说，它可以说是超级“觉醒”，这里取这个词的贬义。
cues.en: Now, a lot of people have been very critical of the recently released Google’s Gemini 1.5 for essentially, in my words, I could say super woke in the negative connotation of that word.

cues.zh: 它做了一些几乎滑稽到荒谬的事情，比如它修改历史，生成黑人乔治·华盛顿的图像，或者更严重的是你在 Twitter 上评论过的事情，即拒绝评论或生成天安门广场或坦克人的图像甚至描述，而那是历史上最具传奇色彩的抗议图像之一。
cues.en: There is some almost hilariously absurd things that it does, like it modifies history like generating images of a black George Washington, or perhaps more seriously something that you commented on Twitter, which is refusing to comment on or generate images or even descriptions of Tiananmen Square or The Tank Man, one of the most legendary protest images in history.

cues.zh: 当然，这些图像被中国政府高度审查，因此，大家都开始质疑设计这些LLM的过程究竟是怎样的？
cues.en: Of course, these images are highly censored by the Chinese government and therefore, everybody started asking questions of what is the process of designing these LLMs?

cues.zh: 审查之类的东西扮演了什么角色？
cues.en: What is the role of censorship and all that kind of stuff?

cues.zh: 你在Twitter上评论说开源才是答案。
cues.en: So you commented on Twitter saying that open source is the answer.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 基本上是这样，你能解释一下吗？
cues.en: Essentially, so can you explain?

cues.zh: 我实际上在我能想到的几乎所有社交网络上发表了那条评论，而且我在各种论坛上多次提出过这个观点。
cues.en: I actually made that comment on just about every social network I can, and I’ve made that point multiple times in various forums.

cues.zh: 我的观点是这样的，人们可以抱怨AI系统存在偏见，而它们确实普遍会因为训练数据的分布而产生偏见，这些数据反映了社会中的偏见，这对某些人来说可能具有冒犯性，也可能不会。
cues.en: Here’s my point of view on this, people can complain that AI systems are biased and they generally are biased by the distribution of the training data that they’ve been trained on that reflects biases in society, and that is potentially offensive to some people or potentially not.

cues.zh: 而一些去偏技术随后会因历史不准确之类的问题，冒犯到某些人。
cues.en: And some techniques to de-bias then become offensive to some people because of historical incorrectness and things like that.

cues.zh: 所以你可以问两个问题，第一个问题是，有没有可能做出一个没有偏见的 AI 系统？
cues.en: And so you can ask two questions, the first question is, is it possible to produce an AI system that is not biased?

cues.zh: 答案是，绝对不可能。
cues.en: And the answer is, absolutely not.

cues.zh: 这不是因为技术挑战，尽管确实存在技术挑战，而是因为偏见存在于观者的眼中。
cues.en: And it’s not because of technological challenges, although they are technological challenges to that, it’s because bias is in the eye of the beholder.

cues.zh: 不同的人对很多事情什么算偏见可能有不同的看法，有些事实是无可争议的，但有很多观点或事情可以用不同方式表达。
cues.en: Different people may have different ideas about what constitutes bias for a lot of things, there are facts that are indisputable, but there are a lot of opinions or things that can be expressed in different ways.

cues.zh: 所以你不可能有一个没有偏见的系统，那根本不可能。
cues.en: And so you cannot have an unbiased system, that’s just an impossibility.

cues.zh: 那这个问题的答案是什么？
cues.en: And so what’s the answer to this?

cues.zh: 答案和我们在自由民主中对新闻界的答案一样：新闻界必须自由且多元。
cues.en: And the answer is the same answer that we found in liberal democracy about the press, the press needs to be free and diverse.

cues.zh: 我们之所以要有言论自由，是因为我们不希望所有信息都来自单一来源，因为那与民主、进步理念乃至科学的整体理念相悖。
cues.en: We have free speech for a good reason, is because we don’t want all of our information to come from a unique source because that’s opposite to the whole idea of democracy and progressive ideas and even science.

cues.zh: 在科学中，人们必须为不同观点争论，科学的进步正是在人们有分歧、提出答案并形成共识时发生的，全世界所有民主国家都是如此。
cues.en: In science, people have to argue for different opinions and science makes progress when people disagree and they come up with an answer and consensus forms, and it’s true in all democracies around the world.

cues.zh: 有一个正在发生的未来：我们与数字世界的每一次互动，都将由AI系统、AI助手来中介。
cues.en: There is a future which is already happening where every single one of our interaction with the digital world will be mediated by AI systems, AI assistance.

cues.zh: 智能眼镜即将普及，Meta已经有售，就是Ray-Ban Meta，你可以和它对话，它连接了大语言模型，任何问题都能得到答案。
cues.en: We’re going to have smart glasses, you can already buy them from Meta, the Ray-Ban Meta where you can talk to them and they are connected with an LLM and you can get answers on any question you have.

cues.zh: 或者你看着一座纪念碑，眼镜里有摄像头，你可以问它，这座建筑或纪念碑有什么故事？
cues.en: Or you can be looking at a monument and there is a camera in the glasses you can ask it like, what can you tell me about this building or this monument?

cues.zh: 你可以看着一份外语菜单，我相信它会帮你翻译，或者如果我们语言不同，还能做实时翻译。
cues.en: You can be looking at a menu in a foreign language, and I think we will translate it for you, or we can do real time translation if we speak different languages.

cues.zh: 所以在不久的将来，我们与数字世界的很多交互都将通过这些系统来完成。
cues.en: So a lot of our interactions with the digital world are going to be mediated by those systems in the near future.

cues.zh: 我们用的搜索引擎将越来越不再是搜索引擎，而是对话系统，我们只需提问，它就会回答，然后可能给你指向合适的参考资料。
cues.en: Increasingly, the search engines that we’re going to use are not going to be search engines, they’re going to be dialogue systems that we just ask a question and it will answer and then point you to perhaps appropriate reference for it.

cues.zh: 但问题在于，我们无法承受这些系统只由美国西海岸的少数几家公司提供，因为这些系统将构成全人类知识的宝库，我们不能让它被少数人控制。
cues.en: But here is the thing, we cannot afford those systems to come from a handful of companies on the west coast of the US because those systems will constitute the repository of all human knowledge, and we cannot have that be controlled by a small number of people.

cues.zh: 它必须是多元的，原因和新闻界必须多元一样。那么，我们如何获得多元化的AI助手呢？
cues.en: It has to be diverse for the same reason the press has to be diverse, so how do we get a diverse set of AI assistance?

cues.zh: 目前训练一个基础模型、一个基础LLM非常昂贵且困难。未来可能不是LLM，但眼下就是LLM。
cues.en: It’s very expensive and difficult to train a base model, a base LLM at the moment, in the future it might be something different, but at the moment, that’s an LLM.

cues.zh: 所以只有少数几家公司能做好这件事。
cues.en: So only a few companies can do this properly.

cues.zh: 如果其中一些顶尖系统是开源的，任何人都可以使用，任何人都可以微调。
cues.en: And if some of those top systems are open source, anybody can use them, anybody can fine tune them.

cues.zh: 如果我们建立一些机制，让任何群体——无论是公民个人、公民团体、政府组织、非政府组织、公司等等——都能拿这些开源AI系统，用自己的数据为自己的目的进行微调，那么我们就会拥有非常多样化、针对各种用途专门化的AI系统。
cues.en: If we put in place some systems that allows any group of people, whether they are individual citizens, groups of citizens, government organizations, NGOs, companies, whatever, to take those open source AI systems and fine tune them for their own purpose on their own data, then we’re going to have a very large diversity of different AI systems that are specialized for all of those things.

cues.zh: 我跟你说，我跟法国政府聊了不少，法国政府绝不会接受本国所有公民的数字饮食被美国西海岸的三家公司控制。
cues.en: I tell you, I talked to the French government quite a bit, and the French government will not accept that the digital diet of all their citizens be controlled by three companies on the west coast of the US.

cues.zh: 这绝对不可接受，不管这些公司多么善意，这都是对民主的威胁，也是对本地文化、价值观和语言的威胁。
cues.en: That’s just not acceptable, it’s a danger to democracy regardless of how well-intentioned those companies are, and it’s also a danger to local culture, to values, to language.

cues.zh: 我跟印度Infosys的创始人聊过，他在资助一个项目，微调Meta出的开源模型Llama 2，让Llama 2会说印度全部22种官方语言，这对印度人非常重要。
cues.en: I was talking with the founder of Infosys in India, he’s funding a project to fine tune Llama 2, the open source model produced by Meta, so that Llama 2 two speaks all 22 official languages in India, it is very important for people in India.

cues.zh: 我跟一位前同事Moustapha Cisse聊过，他以前是Fair的科学家，后来回到非洲，为Google在非洲创建了一个研究实验室，现在有了新创公司Co-Kera。
cues.en: I was talking to a former colleague of mine, Moustapha Cisse, who used to be a scientist at Fair and then moved back to Africa, created a research lab for Google in Africa and now has a new startup Co-Kera.

cues.zh: 他想做的是，基本上就是让LLM能说塞内加尔的本地语言，这样人们就能获取医疗信息，因为他们接触不到医生，塞内加尔人均医生数量非常少。
cues.en: And what he’s trying to do, is basically have LLM that speak the local languages in Senegal so that people can have access to medical information because they don’t have access to doctors, it’s a very small number of doctors per capita in Senegal.

cues.zh: 如果没有开源平台，这些都无从谈起，所以有了开源平台，你就能拥有不仅在政治观点之类方面多样化的人工智能系统——
cues.en: You can’t have any of this unless you have open source platforms, so with open source platforms, you can have AI systems that are not only diverse in terms of political opinions or things of that-

cues.zh: ……人工智能系统不仅在政治观点之类方面多样化，而且在语言、文化、价值体系、政治观点、各领域的技术能力方面也多样化，你还能拥有一个产业、一个由公司组成的生态系统，针对行业中的垂直应用对这些开源系统进行微调。
cues.en: … AI systems that are not only diverse in terms of political opinions or things of that type, but in terms of language, culture, value systems, political opinions, technical abilities in various domains, and you can have an industry, an ecosystem of companies that fine tune those open source systems for vertical applications in industry.

cues.zh: 我不知道，一家出版社有成千上万本书，他们想建一个系统，让客户能就他们任何一本书的内容提问，你就得用他们的专有数据来训练。
cues.en: I don’t know, a publisher has thousands of books and they want to build a system that allows a customer to just ask a question about the content of any of their books, you need to train on their proprietary data.

cues.zh: 你有一家公司，我们在Meta内部也有一个，叫Metamate，它基本上就是一个LLM，能回答关于公司内部事务的任何问题，非常有用。
cues.en: You have a company, we have one within Meta, it’s called Metamate, and it’s basically an LLM that can answer any question about internal stuff about the company, very useful.

cues.zh: 很多公司都想要这个。
cues.en: A lot of companies want this.

cues.zh: 很多公司想要这个，不仅是为了他们的员工，也是为了他们的客户，用来服务他们的客户。
cues.en: A lot of companies want this not just for their employees, but also for their customers, to take care of their customers.

cues.zh: 所以，你要想有一个AI产业，你要想有不是带有独特偏见的AI系统，唯一的办法就是有开源平台，任何群体都能在上面构建专门的系统。
cues.en: So the only way you’re going to have an AI industry, the only way you’re going to have AI systems that are not uniquely biased is if you have open source platforms on top of which any group can build specialized systems.

cues.zh: 历史不可避免的方向是，绝大多数AI系统都将构建在开源平台之上。
cues.en: So the direction of inevitable direction of history is that the vast majority of AI systems will be built on top of open source platforms.

cues.zh: 这真是个美好的愿景。
cues.en: So that’s a beautiful vision.

cues.zh: 也就是说，像Meta或Google这样的公司，在构建基础预训练模型之后，应该只采取最少的微调步骤，步骤越少越好。
cues.en: So meaning a company like Meta or Google or so on should take only minimal fine-tuning steps after building the foundation pre-trained model as few steps as possible.

cues.zh: 基本上是这样。
cues.en: Basically.

cues.zh: Meta承担得起这么做吗？
cues.en: Can Meta afford to do that?

cues.zh: 不行。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 我不知道你知不知道，但公司总得想办法赚钱，而开源就是在白送……我也不知道。
cues.en: So I don’t know if you know this, but companies are supposed to make money somehow and open source is giving away… I don’t know.

cues.zh: Mark发了个视频，Mark Zuckerberg，一个非常性感的视频，讲的是35万块Nvidia H100。
cues.en: Mark made a video, Mark Zuckerberg, very sexy video talking about 350,000 Nvidia H100s.
Yeah, [inaudible 01:44:12]

cues.zh: 算一下就知道，光GPU就是1000亿，再加上训练一切所需的基础设施。
cues.en: The math of that is just for the GPUs, that’s 100 billion plus the infrastructure for training everything.

cues.zh: 我不是生意人，但那要怎么赚钱呢？
cues.en: So I’m no business guy, but how do you make money on that?

cues.zh: 你描绘的这种划分非常有力量，但怎么可能赚到钱呢？
cues.en: So the division you paint is a really powerful one, but how is it possible to make money?

cues.zh: 好，所以你有几种商业模式，对吧？
cues.en: Okay, so you have several business models, right?

cues.zh: 嗯哼。
cues.en: Mm-hmm.

cues.zh: Meta 所依托的商业模式是，你提供一项服务，而这项服务的资金来源要么是广告，要么是企业客户。
cues.en: The business model that Meta is built around is you offer a service and the financing of that service is either through ads or through business customers.

cues.zh: 举个例子，如果你有一个 LLM，能通过 WhatsApp 和顾客对话，帮一家夫妻披萨店做生意，顾客可以直接点披萨，系统会问他们：“你要什么配料，多大尺寸，等等等等。”商家会为此付费，对吧？
cues.en: So for example, if you have an LLM that can help a mom-and-pop pizza place by talking to the customers through WhatsApp, and so the customers can just order a pizza and the system will just ask them, “What topping do you want or what size, blah, blah, blah.” The business will pay for that, okay?

cues.zh: 这是一种模式。
cues.en: That’s a model.

cues.zh: 否则，如果它是一个更偏向传统服务的系统，那就可以靠广告支持，或者还有好几种模式。
cues.en: Otherwise, if it’s a system that is on the more classical services, it can be ad supported or there’s several models.

cues.zh: 但关键是，如果你有足够大的潜在客户群，而且你本来就得为他们构建那套系统，那把它分发到开源里对你并无坏处。
cues.en: But the point is, if you have a big enough potential customer base and you need to build that system anyway for them, it doesn’t hurt you to actually distribute it to the open source.

cues.zh: 再说一次，我不是生意人，但如果你发布开源模型，那其他人也能做同样的任务并在此基础上竞争，基本上就是为企业提供微调模型。
cues.en: Again, I’m no business guy, but if you release the open source model, then other people can do the same kind of task and compete on it, basically provide fine-tuned models for businesses.

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我是这一切的超级粉丝，但Meta下的赌注是不是就像，“我们会做得更好”？
cues.en: By the way, I’m a huge fan of all this, but is the bet that Meta is making, it’s like, “We’ll do a better job of it?”

cues.zh: 嗯，不是。
cues.en: Well, no.

cues.zh: 这个赌注更像是，“我们已经有庞大的用户群和客户群——
cues.en: The bet is more, “We already have a huge user base and customer base-

cues.zh: 啊，对。
cues.en: Ah, right.

cues.zh: ……所以这对他们会有用。
cues.en: … so it’s going to be useful to them.

cues.zh: 我们提供给他们的任何东西都会有用，而且有办法从中获得收入。
cues.en: Whatever we offer them is going to be useful and there is a way to derive revenue from this.

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 我们提供这个系统或基础模型、开源的基础模型，让别人也能在上面构建应用，这也没什么坏处。
cues.en: It doesn’t hurt that we provide that system or the base model, the foundation model in open source for others to build applications on top of it too.

cues.zh: 如果这些应用对我们的客户有用，我们直接从他们那里买下来就行。
cues.en: If those applications turn out to be useful for our customers, we can just buy it from them.

cues.zh: 他们可能会改进这个平台。
cues.en: It could be that they will improve the platform.

cues.zh: 事实上，我们已经看到了这一点。
cues.en: In fact, we see this already.

cues.zh: LLaMA 2 的下载量 literally 有数百万次，还有数千人提供了如何让它更好的想法。
cues.en: There is literally millions of downloads of LLaMA 2 and thousands of people who have provided ideas about how to make it better.

cues.zh: 所以这显然加速了进展，让系统能够服务于广泛的社区，而且 literally 有数千家企业正在用它构建应用。
cues.en: So this clearly accelerates progress to make the system available to a wide community of people, and there’s literally thousands of businesses who are building applications with it.

cues.zh: 所以，Meta 从这项技术中获取收入的能力，并不会因为开源分发基础模型而受损。
cues.en: So Meta’s ability to derive revenue from this technology is not impaired by the distribution of base models in open source.

cues.zh: Gemini 受到的根本性批评是，正如你在西海岸指出的那样，澄清一下，我们现在在东海岸，我猜 Meta AI 总部应该在这里。
cues.en: The fundamental criticism that Gemini is getting is that as you point out on the West Coast, just to clarify, we’re currently on the East Coast where I would suppose Meta AI headquarters would be.

cues.zh: 所以对西海岸有很强烈的言论，但我想问题在于，我认为可以公平地说，大多数科技人士在政治立场上偏向左翼。
cues.en: So there are strong words about the West Coast, but I guess the issue that happens is I think it’s fair to say that most tech people have a political affiliation with the left wing.

cues.zh: 他们倾向左翼。
cues.en: They lean left.

cues.zh: 所以人们批评 Gemini 的问题在于，在你提到的去偏见过程中，他们的意识形态倾向变得显而易见。
cues.en: So the problem that people are criticizing Gemini with is that there’s in that de-biasing process that you mentioned, that their ideological lean becomes obvious.

cues.zh: 这是可以避免的吗？
cues.en: Is this something that could be escaped?

cues.zh: 你说开源是唯一的出路。
cues.en: You’re saying open source is the only way.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 你亲眼见过这种让工程变得困难的意识形态倾向吗？
cues.en: Have you witnessed this kind of ideological lean that makes engineering difficult?

cues.zh: 不，我认为问题并不在于设计这些系统的人的政治倾向。
cues.en: No, I don’t think the issue has to do with the political leaning of the people designing those systems.

cues.zh: 问题在于他们的客户群体或受众的接受度或政治倾向。
cues.en: It has to do with the acceptability or political leanings of their customer base or audience.

cues.zh: 所以大公司承受不起冒犯太多人，因此他们会确保推出的任何产品都是安全的，不管“安全”具体指什么。
cues.en: So a big company cannot afford to offend too many people, so they’re going to make sure that whatever product they put out is safe, whatever that means.

cues.zh: 很容易做得过头，而要为所有人做到恰到好处是不可能的。
cues.en: It’s very possible to overdo it, and it’s impossible to do it properly for everyone.

cues.zh: 你不可能让所有人都满意。
cues.en: You’re not going to satisfy everyone.

cues.zh: 所以就像我之前说的，你不可能有一个让所有人都认为没有偏见的系统。
cues.en: So that’s what I said before, you cannot have a system that is perceived as unbiased by everyone.

cues.zh: 你往一个方向推，一群人会觉得它有偏见；然后你往另一个方向推，另一群人又会觉得它有偏见。
cues.en: It’s going to be you push it in one way, one set of people are going to see it as biased, and then you push it the other way and another set of people is going to see it as biased.

cues.zh: 除此之外，还有这样一个问题：如果你把系统往某个方向推得稍微过头，它就会变得不符合事实。
cues.en: Then in addition to this, there’s the issue of if you push the system perhaps a little too far in one direction, it’s going to be non-factual.

cues.zh: 你会得到穿制服的“黑纳粹”士兵。
cues.en: You’re going to have Black Nazi soldiers in uniform.

cues.zh: 对，所以我们应该提一下“黑纳粹士兵”的图像生成，这在事实上是不准确的。
cues.en: Yeah, we so we should mention image generation of Black Nazi soldiers, which is not factually accurate.

cues.zh: 没错，而且对某些人来说也可能具有冒犯性。
cues.en: Right, and can be offensive for some people as well.

cues.zh: 所以，要做出对所有人都没有偏见的系统是不可能的。
cues.en: So it’s going to be impossible to produce systems that are unbiased for everyone.

cues.zh: 所以我看到的唯一解决方案就是多样性。
cues.en: So the only solution that I see is diversity.

cues.zh: 是这个词完整意义上的多样性，在一切可能维度上的多样性。
cues.en: Diversity in the full meaning of that word, diversity of in every possible way.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: Marc Andreessen 今天刚发了条推文。
cues.en: Marc Andreessen just tweeted today.

cues.zh: 我来做个 TL;DR。
cues.en: Let me do a TL;DR.

cues.zh: 结论是，只有初创公司和开源才能避免他所强调的、大科技公司存在的那个问题。
cues.en: The conclusion is only startups and open source can avoid the issue that he’s highlighting with big tech.

cues.zh: 他问的是：“大型科技公司真能推出生成式AI产品吗？”（1）内部激进分子、员工群体、疯狂的高管、破碎的董事会、压力团体、极端监管者、政府机构、媒体、所谓的“专家”以及一切干扰输出的因素，不断提出越来越高的要求。
cues.en: He’s asking, “Can Big Tech actually field generative AI products?” (1) Ever-escalating demands from internal activists, employee mobs, crazed executives, broken boards, pressure groups, extremist regulators, government agencies, the press, in quotes, “experts” and everything corrupting the output.

cues.zh: （2）始终存在生成糟糕答案、画出糟糕图片或渲染糟糕视频的风险，谁知道它下一刻会说什么或做什么。
cues.en: (2) Constant risk of generating a bad answer or drawing a bad picture or rendering a bad video who knows what is going to say or do at any moment.

cues.zh: （3）法律风险、产品责任、诽谤、选举法以及许多其他事项等等，任何会让国会恼火的东西。
cues.en: (3) Legal exposure, product liability, slander, election law, many other things and so on, anything that makes Congress mad.

cues.zh: （4）不断尝试收紧对可接受输出的控制，降低模型的质量，也就是它在可用性、易用性、有效性等方面的实际表现。
cues.en: (4) Continuous attempts to tighten grip on acceptable output, degrade the model, how good it actually is, in terms of usable and pleasant to use and effective and all that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: (5) 不良文本、图像、视频的公开传播，实际上就是把这些样本放进了下一版本的训练数据里，以此类推。
cues.en: (5) Publicity of bad text, images, video actual puts those examples into the training data for the next version and so on.

cues.zh: 所以他只是强调，这件事有多难——各方人士都会不满意。
cues.en: So he just highlights how difficult this is from all kinds of people being unhappy.

cues.zh: 他说，你不可能造出一个让所有人都满意的系统。
cues.en: He said you can’t create a system that makes everybody happy.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 所以如果你打算自己做微调、并且保持闭源，本质上问题就在于：你要尽量减少不满意的人数。
cues.en: So if you’re going to do the fine-tuning yourself and keep it close source, essentially, the problem there is then trying to minimize the number of people who are going to be unhappy.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yep.

cues.zh: 你是说这几乎不可能做到，而有更好的方式来做开源
cues.en: You’re saying that almost impossible to do, and there are better ways to do open source

cues.zh: 基本上是这样。
cues.en: Basically.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: Mark 说得对，你列出的那些事情确实让大公司感到害怕。
cues.en: Mark is right about a number of things that you list that indeed scare large companies.

cues.zh: 当然，国会调查就是其中之一，还有法律责任——做出会让人伤害自己或伤害他人的东西。
cues.en: Certainly, congressional investigations is one of them, legal liability, making things that get people to hurt themselves or hurt others.

cues.zh: 大公司非常谨慎，不制造这类东西，首先是不想伤害任何人，其次是想保住自己的生意。
cues.en: Big companies are really careful about not producing things of this type because they don’t want to hurt anyone, first of all, and then second, they want to preserve their business.

cues.zh: 所以像这样的系统基本上不可能做到，它们不可避免地会形成政治观点，以及对各种事物的看法，这些看法可能涉及政治，也可能不涉及，但人们可能会有分歧，涉及道德问题、宗教问题之类，或者不同群体的人本来就会有分歧的文化问题。
cues.en: So it’s essentially impossible for systems like this that can inevitably formulate political opinions, and opinions about various things that may be political or not, but that people may disagree about, about moral issues and questions about religion and things like that or cultural issues that people from different communities would disagree with in the first place.

cues.zh: 所以只有相对少数的事情是人们会一致认同为基本原则的，但除此之外，如果你想让这些系统有用，它们就必然不可避免地会冒犯一些人。
cues.en: So there’s only a relatively small number of things that people will agree on are basic principles, but beyond that, if you want those systems to be useful, they will necessarily have to offend a number of people inevitably.

cues.zh: 所以开源就是更好，然后你就能得到——
cues.en: So open source is just better and then you get-

cues.zh: 多样性更好，对吧？
cues.en: Diversity is better, right?

cues.zh: 而开源能促成多样性。
cues.en: And open source enables diversity.

cues.zh: 没错。
cues.en: That’s right.

cues.zh: 开源能促成多样性。
cues.en: Open source enables diversity.

cues.zh: 这可能是一个迷人的世界：如果开源世界真如所说，如果 Meta 带头打造出这个开源基础模型的世界，政府会拥有微调过的模型，然后可能左派和右派的人都会有自己的模型和偏好可供选择，这反而可能让我们更加分裂。
cues.en: This can be a fascinating world where if it’s true that the open source world, if Meta leads the way and creates this open source foundation model world, governments will have a fine- tuned model and then potentially, people that vote left and right will have their own model and preference to be able to choose and it will potentially divide us even more.

cues.zh: 但这取决于我们人类自己。
cues.en: But that’s on us humans.

cues.zh: 我们得想明白，基本上技术是让人类能更有效地做人，而人类提出的所有棘手的伦理问题，就只能靠我们自己去解决。
cues.en: We get to figure out basically the technology enables humans to human more effectively, and all the difficult ethical questions that humans raise will just leave it up to us to figure that out.

cues.zh: 是的，存在一些限制。
cues.en: Yeah, there are some limits.

cues.zh: 就像言论自由也有其限制一样。
cues.en: The same way there are limits to free speech.

cues.zh: 对于那些系统可能被授权生成的内容，必须有一些限制，一些护栏。
cues.en: There has to be some limit to the kind of stuff that those systems might be authorized to produce, some guardrails.

cues.zh: 所以这是我感兴趣的一点，也就是我们之前讨论的那种架构类型，系统的输出是为了满足某个目标而进行推理的结果，这个目标可以包含护栏，而且我们可以把护栏放进开源系统里。
cues.en: So that’s one thing I’d be interested in, which is in the type of architecture that we were discussing before where the output of the system is a result of an inference to satisfy an objective, that objective can include guardrails, and we can put guardrails in open source systems.

cues.zh: 如果我们最终有了按照这个蓝图构建的系统，我们就可以在这些系统里设置护栏，保证有一套最低限度的护栏，使系统不危险、无毒害等等，这些是所有人都会认同的基本事项。
cues.en: If we eventually have systems that are built with this blueprint, we can put guardrails in those systems that guarantee that there is a minimum set of guardrails that make the system non-dangerous and non-toxic, et cetera, basic things that everybody would agree on.

cues.zh: 然后人们会添加的微调，或者人们会添加的额外防护措施，都会迎合他们自己的社区，不管是什么社区。
cues.en: Then the fine-tuning that people will add or the additional guardrails that people will add will cater to their community, whatever it is.

cues.zh: 微调更多会针对一些灰色地带，比如什么算仇恨言论、什么算危险内容之类的，但关键是——
cues.en: The fine-tuning will be more about the gray areas of what is hate speech, what is dangerous and all that kind of stuff, but it’s the-

cues.zh: 或者不同的价值体系。
cues.en: Or different value systems.

cues.zh: 仍然是价值体系。
cues.en: Still value systems.

cues.zh: 但即便涉及如何制造生物武器这类目标，比如，我想你评论过一些东西，或者至少有一篇论文，一群研究人员正试图理解这些 LLM 的社会影响。
cues.en: But still even with the objectives of how to build a bioweapon, for example, I think something you’ve commented on, or at least there’s a paper where a collection of researchers is trying to understand the social impacts of these LLMs.

cues.zh: 我觉得一个不错的标准是：LLM 是否让这件事比搜索——比如谷歌搜索——更容易了？
cues.en: I guess one threshold that’s nice is, does the LLM make it any easier than a search would, like a Google search would?

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 所以这方面越来越多的研究似乎都指向一个事实：它并没有帮助。
cues.en: So the increasing number of studies on this seems to point to the fact that it doesn’t help.

cues.zh: 所以，即便你已经有搜索引擎和图书馆，LLM 也帮不了你设计或制造生物武器或化学武器。
cues.en: So having an LLM doesn’t help you design or build a bioweapon or a chemical weapon if you already have access to a search engine and their library.

cues.zh: 所以你获得的更多信息，或者获取信息的便利性，其实帮不上什么忙。
cues.en: So the increased information you get or the ease with which you get it doesn’t really help you.

cues.zh: 这是第一点。
cues.en: That’s the first thing.

cues.zh: 第二点是，有一份制造化学武器、比如生物武器的操作指南是一回事。
cues.en: The second thing is, it’s one thing to have a list of instructions of how to make a chemical weapon, for example, a bioweapon.

cues.zh: 真正把它造出来是另一回事，而且比你想象的难得多，LLM 在这方面帮不了你。
cues.en: It’s another thing to actually build it, and it’s much harder than you might think, and then LLM will not help you with that.

cues.zh: 事实上，世界上没有人、甚至没有哪个国家使用过生物武器，因为大多数时候他们根本不知道怎么保护自己的人民免受其害。
cues.en: In fact, nobody in the world, not even countries used bioweapons because most of the time they have no idea how to protect their own populations against it.

cues.zh: 所以它实际上太危险了，根本不能用，而且事实上它也被国际条约所禁止。
cues.en: So it’s too dangerous, actually, to ever use, and it’s, in fact, banned by international treaties.

cues.zh: 化学武器就不一样了。
cues.en: Chemical weapons is different.

cues.zh: 它同样被条约禁止，但问题是一样的。
cues.en: It’s also banned by treaties, but it’s the same problem.

cues.zh: 很难在不伤及施害者自身的情况下使用，不过我们可以问问Elon Musk。
cues.en: It’s difficult to use in situations that doesn’t turn against the perpetrators, but we could ask Elon Musk.

cues.zh: 我可以给你一份非常精确的指令清单，告诉你如何造火箭发动机。
cues.en: I can give you a very precise list of instructions of how you build a rocket engine.

cues.zh: 即使你有一支50名经验丰富的工程师组成的团队来造它，你还是得炸掉十几个，才能得到一个能用的。
cues.en: Even if you have a team of 50 engineers that are really experienced building it, you’re still going to have to blow up a dozen of them before you get one that works.

cues.zh: 化学武器、生物武器之类的东西也是一样，它需要现实世界中的专业知识，而LLM帮不上忙。
cues.en: It’s the same with chemical weapons or bioweapons or things like this, it requires expertise in the real world that the LLM is not going to help you with.

cues.zh: 它甚至需要我们一直在谈的常识性专业知识，也就是如何把基于语言的指令在物理世界中实现出来，这需要大量不在指令之中的知识。
cues.en: It requires even the common sense expertise that we’ve been talking about, which is how to take language-based instructions and materialize them in the physical world requires a lot of knowledge that’s not in the instructions.

cues.zh: 是的，正是如此。
cues.en: Yeah, exactly.

cues.zh: 实际上，很多生物学家针对这些言论发表了看法，回应说：“你们知道实际做实验室工作有多难吗？”就像在说，“不，这可不是小事一桩。”
cues.en: A lot of biologists have posted on this actually, in response to those things saying, “Do you realize how hard it is to actually do the lab work?” Like, “No, this is not trivial.”

cues.zh: 是的，汉斯·莫拉维克再次成为焦点。
cues.en: Yeah, and Hans Moravec comes to light once again.

cues.zh: 继续聊聊LLaMA，马克宣布LLaMA 3终将问世。
cues.en: Just to linger on LLaMA, Marc announced that LLaMA 3 is coming out eventually.

cues.zh: 我认为还没有确定的发布日期，但你最期待的是什么？
cues.en: I don’t think there’s a release date, but what are you most excited about?

cues.zh: 首先，已经推出的LLaMA 2，或许未来的LLaMA 3、4、5、6、10，就是Meta旗下开源项目的未来？
cues.en: First of all, LLaMA 2 that’s already out there and maybe the future a LLaMA 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, just the future of the open source under Meta?

cues.zh: 嗯，有很多方面。
cues.en: Well, a number of things.

cues.zh: 所以会有各种版本的LLaMA，它们是前代LLaMA的改进版，更大、更好、多模态等等。
cues.en: So there’s going to be various versions of LLaMA that are improvements of previous LLaMAs, bigger, better, multimodal, things like that.

cues.zh: 然后在未来的世代中，能够规划的系统，真正理解世界如何运作，可能是通过视频训练的，因此它们拥有一些世界模型，也许能进行我之前谈到的推理和规划类型。
cues.en: Then in future generations, systems that are capable of planning that really understand how the world works, maybe are trained from video, so they have some world model maybe capable of the type of reasoning and planning I was talking about earlier.

cues.zh: 那要花多长时间？
cues.en: How long is that going to take?

cues.zh: 如果你们想把那个方向的研究成果引入 LLaMA 的产品线，大概什么时候能落地？
cues.en: When is the research that is going in that direction going to feed into the product line if you want of LLaMA?

cues.zh: 我不知道。
cues.en: I don’t know.

cues.zh: 我没法告诉你。
cues.en: I can’t tell you.

cues.zh: 在达到那一步之前，我们基本上还得经历几项突破，但你们可以跟踪我们的进展，因为我们会公开研究成果。
cues.en: There’s a few breakthroughs that we have to basically go through before we can get there, but you’ll be able to monitor our progress because we publish our research.

cues.zh: 比如上周我们发布了 V-JEPA 的工作，这是迈向视频训练系统的第一步。
cues.en: So last week we published the V-JEPA work, which is a first step towards training systems for video.

cues.zh: 下一步就是基于这类思路、从视频中训练的世界模型。
cues.en: Then the next step is going to be world models based on this type of idea training from video.

cues.zh: DeepMind 也有类似的工作，还有 UC Berkeley 也在做世界模型和视频方面的研究。
cues.en: There’s similar work at DeepMind also and taking place people, and also at UC Berkeley on world models and video.

cues.zh: 很多人在做这件事。
cues.en: A lot of people are working on this.

cues.zh: 我觉得很多好点子正在涌现。
cues.en: I think a lot of good ideas are appearing.

cues.zh: 我打赌那些系统会是轻量级JEPA，不会是生成模型，未来会告诉我们答案。
cues.en: My bet is that those systems are going to be JEPA light, they’re not going to be generative models, and we’ll see what the future will tell.

cues.zh: 有一些非常出色的工作，一位叫Danijar Hafner的先生现在在DeepMind，他研究的就是这类模型——先学习表征，然后通过强化训练将其用于规划或学习任务；Berkeley那边Pieter Abbeel、Sergey Levine等许多人做了大量工作，我实际上正以NYU的身份、通过一些资助项目与他们合作。
cues.en: There’s really good work, a gentleman called Danijar Hafner who is now DeepMind, who’s worked on models of this type that learn representations and then use them for planning or learning tasks by reinforcement training and a lot of work at Berkeley by Pieter Abbeel, Sergey Levine, a bunch of other people of that type I’m collaborating with actually in the context of some grants with my NYU hat.

cues.zh: 合作也通过Meta进行，因为Berkeley的实验室在某种程度上与Meta有关联，所以是和FAIR合作。
cues.en: Then collaboration is also through Meta ’cause the lab at Berkeley is associated with Meta in some way, so with fair.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得这非常令人兴奋。
cues.en: So I think it is very exciting.

cues.zh: 自从10年前FAIR成立以来，我还没有对机器学习和AI的方向这么兴奋过。
cues.en: I haven’t been that excited about the direction of machine learning and AI since 10 years ago when Fairway was started.

cues.zh: 在此之前，30年前，我们当时在做，哦抱歉，是35年前，研究组合网络和神经网络的早期阶段。
cues.en: Before that, 30 years ago, we were working, oh, sorry, 35 on combination nets and the early days of neural nets.

cues.zh: 所以我非常兴奋，因为我看到了一条通往潜在人类水平智能的路径，这些系统能够理解世界、记忆、规划、推理。
cues.en: So I’m super excited because I see a path towards potentially human-level intelligence with systems that can understand the world, remember, plan, reason.

cues.zh: 有一些想法可以在这方面取得进展，可能有机会奏效，我对此非常兴奋。
cues.en: There is some set of ideas to make progress there that might have a chance of working, and I’m really excited about this.

cues.zh: 我喜欢的是，我们多少能走上一个好的方向，或许能在我的大脑变成白酱之前，或者在我需要退休之前取得成功。
cues.en: What I like is that somewhat we get on to a good direction and perhaps succeed before my brain turns to a white sauce or before I need to retire.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 对你来说，仅仅是涉及的GPU数量、在这么多算力上的整个训练过程就很美吗？就是拉远视角，看着地球和人类一起建造了这些计算设备，能够训练出这一个大脑，然后我们开源，就像诞生了这个在巨大算力系统上训练的开源大脑，还有如何在那上面训练的细节、如何构建基础设施和硬件、冷却，所有这些类似的东西，还是说你大部分兴奋点仍然在理论层面，也就是软件方面？
cues.en: Is it beautiful to you just the amount of GPUs involved, the whole training process on this much compute, just zooming out, just looking at earth and humans together have built these computing devices and are able to train this one brain, then we then open source, like giving birth to this open source brain trained on this gigantic compute system, there’s just the details of how to train on that, how to build the infrastructure and the hardware, the cooling, all of this kind of stuff, or are you just still that most of your excitement is in the theory aspect of it, meaning the software?

cues.zh: 很多年前，我是个搞硬件的。
cues.en: I used to be a hardware guy many years ago.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 是的，没错。
cues.en: Yes, that’s right.

cues.zh: 几十年前了。
cues.en: Decades ago.

cues.zh: 硬件确实进步了一点。
cues.en: Hardware has improved a little bit.

cues.zh: 变了——
cues.en: Changed-

cues.zh: 一点点。
cues.en: A little bit.

cues.zh: ……确实进步了一点。
cues.en: … a little bit, yeah.

cues.zh: 当然，规模是必要的，但并不充分。
cues.en: Certainly, scale is necessary but not sufficient.

cues.zh: 绝对如此。
cues.en: Absolutely.

cues.zh: 所以我们确实需要竞争。
cues.en: So we certainly need competition.

cues.zh: 就计算能力而言，我们距离匹配人脑的计算能力还差得很远。
cues.en: We’re still far in terms of compute power from what we would need to match the compute power of the human brain.

cues.zh: 这或许会在未来几十年内实现，但我们还有很长的路要走。
cues.en: This may occur in the next couple of decades, but we’re still some ways away.

cues.zh: 当然，在能效方面，我们差得还很远，所以硬件上还有很多进步空间。
cues.en: Certainly, in terms of power efficiency, we’re really far, so there’s a lot of progress to make in hardware.

cues.zh: 目前，很多进步一部分来自硅技术，但很大一部分来自架构创新，还有相当一部分来自更高效地实现那些已经流行起来的架构，基本上是Transformer和卷积网络的结合，所以在我们达到饱和之前，还有一段路要走。
cues.en: Right now, a lot of the progress is, there’s a bit coming from silicon technology, but a lot of it coming from architectural innovation and quite a bit coming from more efficient ways of implementing the architectures that have become popular, basically combination of transformers and com nets, and so there’s still some ways to go until we are going to saturate.

cues.zh: 我们得想出新原理、新制造技术、新的基础组件，也许要基于不同的原理，还有经典数字[听不清 02:03:41]
cues.en: We’re going to have to come up with new principles, new fabrication technology, new basic components perhaps based on different principles and classical digital [inaudible 02:03:41]

cues.zh: 有意思。
cues.en: Interesting.

cues.zh: 所以你认为，要构建 AMI，我们可能也需要一些硬件层面的创新。
cues.en: So you think in order to build AMI, we potentially might need some hardware innovation too.

cues.zh: 嗯，如果想让它普及，那当然，因为我们必须降低功耗。
cues.en: Well, if we want to make it ubiquitous, yeah, certainly, ’cause we’re going to have to reduce the power consumption.

cues.zh: 如今一块 GPU 是五百瓦到一千瓦。
cues.en: A GPU today is half a kilowatt to a kilowatt.

cues.zh: 人脑大约 25 瓦，而 GPU 的算力远低于人脑。
cues.en: Human brain is about 25 watts, and a GPU is way below the power of the human brain.

cues.zh: 你需要大约十万到一百万块才能与之匹敌，所以我们在这里差了巨大的倍数。
cues.en: You need something like 100,000 or a million to match it, so we are off by a huge factor here.

cues.zh: 你常说 GI 不会很快到来，意思是今年不会，未来几年也不会，可能还更遥远。
cues.en: You often say that a GI is not coming soon, meaning not this year, not the next few years, potentially farther away.

cues.zh: 你对此的基本直觉是什么？
cues.en: What’s your basic intuition behind that?

cues.zh: 首先，它不会是一个事件。
cues.en: So first of all, it’s not going to be an event.

cues.zh: 这种想法被科幻小说和好莱坞推广开来，认为有人会发现AGI或人类水平AI或AMI（随你怎么叫）的秘密，然后打开机器，我们就有了AGI，这根本不会发生。
cues.en: The idea somehow, which is popularized by science fiction and Hollywood, that somehow somebody is going to discover the secret to AGI or human-level AI or AMI, whatever you want to call it, and then turn on a machine and then we have AGI, that’s just not going to happen.

cues.zh: 它不会是一个事件。
cues.en: It’s not going to be an event.

cues.zh: 它会是一个渐进的过程。
cues.en: It’s going to be gradual progress.

cues.zh: 我们会有能从视频中学习世界如何运作并学到良好表征的系统吗？
cues.en: Are we going to have systems that can learn from video how the world works and learn good representations?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 在让它们达到我们在人类身上观察到的规模和性能之前，还需要相当长的时间。
cues.en: Before we get them to the scale and performance that we observe in humans it’s going to take quite a while.

cues.zh: 它不会在一天之内发生。
cues.en: It’s not going to happen in one day.

cues.zh: 我们会有拥有大量关联记忆、能记住东西的系统吗？
cues.en: Are we going to get systems that can have large amount of associated memory so they can remember stuff?

cues.zh: 是，但同样，这不会明天就实现。
cues.en: Yeah, but same, it’s not going to happen tomorrow.

cues.zh: 还需要开发一些基础技术。
cues.en: There is some basic techniques that need to be developed.

cues.zh: 我们有很多这样的技术，但要让它们与完整系统协同工作，就是另一回事了。
cues.en: We have a lot of them, but to get this to work together with a full system is another story.

cues.zh: 我们会不会拥有能够推理和规划的系统，也许沿着我之前描述的目标驱动AI架构的思路？
cues.en: Are we going to have systems that can reason and plan perhaps along the lines of objective-driven AI architectures that I described before?

cues.zh: 是的，但在这一切正常运作之前，还需要一段时间。
cues.en: Yeah, but before we get this to work properly, it’s going to take a while.

cues.zh: 在我们让所有这些东西协同工作，并在此基础上拥有能够学习分层规划、分层表征的系统，能够像人脑那样针对手头许多不同情况进行配置的系统之前，所有这些至少需要十年，很可能还要长得多，因为有很多问题我们现在还看不到、尚未遇到，所以我们不知道在这个框架内是否有简单的解决方案。
cues.en: Before we get all those things to work together, and then on top of this, have systems that can learn hierarchical planning, hierarchical representations, systems that can be configured for a lot of different situation at hand, the way the human brain can, all of this is going to take at least a decade and probably much more because there are a lot of problems that we’re not seeing right now that we have not encountered, so we don’t know if there is an easy solution within this framework.

cues.zh: 所以它并不是即将到来。
cues.en: So it’s not just around the corner.

cues.zh: 过去12、15年里，我一直听到有人声称AGI即将到来，而且他们总是错。
cues.en: I’ve been hearing people for the last 12, 15 years claiming that AGI is just around the corner and being systematically wrong.

cues.zh: 他们说这话的时候，我就知道他们错了。
cues.en: I knew they were wrong when they were saying it.

cues.zh: 我直接戳穿了他们的胡扯。
cues.en: I called their bullshit.

cues.zh: 首先，从“人工智能”这个词诞生之日起，就存在一种永恒的乐观主义，这或许与其他技术不同。
cues.en: First of all, from the birth of the term artificial intelligence, there has been a eternal optimism that’s perhaps unlike other technologies.

cues.zh: 这是莫拉维克悖论吗？是人们为何对AGI如此乐观的解释吗？
cues.en: Is it a Moravec’s paradox, the explanation for why people are so optimistic about AGI?

cues.zh: 别以为这只是莫拉维克悖论。
cues.en: Don’t think it’s just Moravec’s paradox.

cues.zh: 莫拉维克悖论是认识到世界并不像我们想的那么容易的一个结果。
cues.en: Moravec’s paradox is a consequence of realizing that the world is not as easy as we think.

cues.zh: 首先，智能不是线性的东西，不能用秤或单一数字来衡量。
cues.en: So first of all, intelligence is not a linear thing that you can measure with a scale or with a single number.

cues.zh: 你能说人类比红毛猩猩更聪明吗？
cues.en: Can you say that humans are smarter than orangutans?

cues.zh: 在某些方面，是的，但在很多方面，红毛猩猩在不少领域比人类更聪明，比如这让它们能在森林里生存下来。
cues.en: In some ways, yes, but in some ways, orangutans are smarter than humans in a lot of domains that allows them to survive in the forest, for example.

cues.zh: 所以IQ是一种非常有限的智力衡量标准。
cues.en: So IQ is a very limited measure of intelligence.

cues.zh: 人类的智力比IQ所衡量的范围要大。
cues.en: Human intelligence is bigger than what IQ, for example, measures.

cues.zh: 嗯，IQ大致能衡量人类的一些东西，但这是因为人类的形态相对统一，对吧？
cues.en: Well, IQ can measure approximately something for humans, but because humans come in relatively uniform form, right?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 但它只衡量一种能力，这种能力可能对某些任务有用，对其他任务则不然。
cues.en: But it only measures one type of ability that maybe relevant for some tasks but not others.

cues.zh: 但如果你谈论的是其他智能实体，它们觉得简单的基本事情却非常不同，那IQ就说明不了什么了。
cues.en: But then if you were talking about other intelligent entities for which the basic things that are easy to them is very different, then it doesn’t mean anything.

cues.zh: 所以智力是一组技能的集合，以及高效获取新技能的能力。
cues.en: So intelligence is a collection of skills and an ability to acquire new skills efficiently.

cues.zh: 某个智能实体拥有或能快速学会的技能集合，与另一个实体的技能集合是不同的。
cues.en: The collection of skills that a particular intelligent entity possess or is capable of learning quickly is different from the collection of skills of another one.

cues.zh: 因为这是多维的，技能集合是一个高维空间，你无法衡量，也无法比较两者谁更智能。
cues.en: Because it’s a multidimensional thing, the set of skills is a high dimensional space, you can’t measure, you cannot compare two things as to whether one is more intelligent than the other.

cues.zh: 它是多维的。
cues.en: It’s multidimensional.

cues.zh: 所以你经常反驳所谓的AI末日论者。
cues.en: So you push back against what are called AI doomers a lot.

cues.zh: 你能解释一下他们的观点，以及你为什么认为他们错了吗？
cues.en: Can you explain their perspective and why you think they’re wrong?

cues.zh: 好，AI末日论者设想了各种灾难场景，比如AI如何逃脱或控制一切，基本上就是杀光我们所有人，而这依赖于一大堆大多是错误的假设。
cues.en: Okay, so AI doomers imagine all kinds of catastrophe scenarios of how AI could escape or control and basically kill us all, and that relies on a whole bunch of assumptions that are mostly false.

cues.zh: 第一个假设是，超级智能的出现将是一个事件，某个时刻我们会搞清秘密，然后启动一台超级智能机器，因为以前从没做过，它就会接管世界并杀光我们所有人。
cues.en: So the first assumption is that the emergence of super intelligence is going to be an event, that at some point we’re going to figure out the secret and we’ll turn on a machine that is super intelligent, and because we’d never done it before, it’s going to take over the world and kill us all.

cues.zh: 那是错的。
cues.en: That is false.

cues.zh: 它不会是某个单一事件。
cues.en: It’s not going to be an event.

cues.zh: 我们将拥有和猫一样聪明的系统，具备人类水平智能的所有特征，但它们的智能水平可能像猫、鹦鹉之类的。
cues.en: We’re going to have systems that are as smart as a cat, have all the characteristics of human-level intelligence, but their level of intelligence would be like a cat or a parrot maybe or something.

cues.zh: 然后我们会逐步推进，让这些东西变得更智能。
cues.en: Then we’re going to work our way up to make those things more intelligent.

cues.zh: 在让它们变得更智能的同时，我们也会给它们加上一些护栏，并学会如何设置护栏，让它们行为得当。
cues.en: As we make them more intelligent, we’re also going to put some guardrails in them and learn how to put some guardrails so they behave properly.

cues.zh: 这不会是一次性的努力，而是会有很多不同的人来做这件事，其中一些人会成功造出可控、安全、有正确护栏的智能系统。
cues.en: It’s not going to be one effort, that it’s going to be lots of different people doing this, and some of them are going to succeed at making intelligent systems that are controllable and safe and have the right guardrails.

cues.zh: 如果某些系统失控了，我们可以用好的那些去对付失控的那些。
cues.en: If some other goes rogue, then we can use the good ones to go against the rogue ones.

cues.zh: 所以这将是我的智能 AI 警察对抗你的失控 AI。
cues.en: So it’s going to be my smart AI police against your rogue AI.
