cues.zh: 所以这不会是那种我们将面对一个单一的失控 AI 把我们都杀掉的情形。
cues.en: So it’s not going to be like we’re going to be exposed to a single rogue AI that’s going to kill us all.

cues.zh: 那根本不会发生。
cues.en: That’s just not happening.

cues.zh: 现在，还有另一个谬误，就是认为因为系统很智能，它就必然想接管一切。
cues.en: Now, there is another fallacy, which is the fact that because the system is intelligent, it necessarily wants to take over.

cues.zh: 有几个论点让人们对此感到恐惧，而我认为这些论点同样完全错误。
cues.en: There is several arguments that make people scared of this, which I think are completely false as well.

cues.zh: 其中一个来自自然界，似乎越是智能的物种最终会支配其他物种，甚至有时是刻意、有时是意外地消灭其他物种。
cues.en: So one of them is in nature, it seems to be that the more intelligent species otherwise end up dominating the other and even distinguishing the others sometimes by design, sometimes just by mistake.

cues.zh: 于是就有这样一种想法：“既然 AI 系统比我们更智能，那它们肯定会消灭我们，即使不是刻意为之，也仅仅因为它们不在乎我们。”这种说法由于多种原因是荒谬的。
cues.en: So there is thinking by which you say, “Well, if AI systems are more intelligent than us, surely they’re going to eliminate us, if not by design, simply because they don’t care about us,” and that’s just preposterous for a number of reasons.

cues.zh: 第一个原因是它们不会成为一个物种。
cues.en: First reason is they’re not going to be a species.

cues.zh: 它们不会成为与我们竞争的物种。
cues.en: They’re not going to be a species that competes with us.

cues.zh: 它们不会有支配的欲望，因为支配欲必须被硬编码进智能系统中。
cues.en: They’re not going to have the desire to dominate because the desire to dominate is something that has to be hardwired into an intelligent system.

cues.zh: 它被硬编码在人类身上。
cues.en: It is hardwired in humans.

cues.zh: 它被硬编码在狒狒、黑猩猩、狼身上，但不在红毛猩猩身上。
cues.en: It is hardwired in baboons, in chimpanzees, in wolves, not in orangutans.

cues.zh: 这种支配欲或臣服欲，或以其他方式获取地位的欲望，是社会性物种特有的。
cues.en: The species in which this desire to dominate or submit or attain status in other ways is specific to social species.

cues.zh: 像红毛猩猩这样的非社会性物种没有这种欲望，而它们几乎和我们一样聪明，对吧？
cues.en: Non-social species like orangutans don’t have it, and they are as smart as we are, almost, right?

cues.zh: 对你来说，人类没有显著动机把这一点编码进AI系统，而即便他们这么做了，也会有其他AI因此惩罚他们，我会在这个问题上与他们竞争。
cues.en: To you, there’s not significant incentive for humans to encode that into the AI systems, and to the degree they do, there’ll be other AIs that punish them for it, I’ll compete them over it.

cues.zh: 让AI系统服从人类，有各种各样的激励因素。
cues.en: Well, there’s all kinds of incentive to make AI systems submissive to humans.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: Right?

cues.zh: 我们就是要这样构建它们。
cues.en: This is the way we’re going to build them.

cues.zh: 然后人们就说：“哦，但看看LLM。
cues.en: So then people say, “Oh, but look at LLMs.

cues.zh: LLM是不可控的，”他们说对了。
cues.en: LLMs are not controllable,” and they’re right.

cues.zh: LLM确实不可控。
cues.en: LLMs are not controllable.

cues.zh: 但目标驱动的AI，也就是通过优化目标来得出答案的系统，意味着它们必须优化这个目标，而这个目标可以包含护栏。
cues.en: But objectively-driven AI, so systems that derive their answers by optimization of an objective means they have to optimize this objective, and that objective can include guardrails.

cues.zh: 一个护栏是：服从人类。
cues.en: One guardrail is, obey humans.

cues.zh: 另一个护栏是：在限定范围内，如果服从人类会伤害其他人，就不要服从。
cues.en: Another guardrail is, don’t obey humans if it’s hurting other humans within limits.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 我在哪儿听过这个，我不记得了——
cues.en: I’ve heard that before somewhere, I don’t remember-

cues.zh: 是的，也许在某本书里。
cues.en: Yes, maybe in a book.

cues.zh: 是啊，但说到那本书，这一切是否也可能带来意想不到的后果？
cues.en: Yeah, but speaking of that book, could there be unintended consequences also from all of this?

cues.zh: 不，当然不是。
cues.en: No, of course.

cues.zh: 所以这不是一个简单的问题。
cues.en: So this is not a simple problem.

cues.zh: 设计这些护栏、让系统行为得当，并不是一个简单的问题，不存在什么银弹，能让你用数学证明系统是安全的。
cues.en: Designing those guardrails so that the system behaves properly is not going to be a simple issue for which there is a silver bullet for which you have a mathematical proof that the system can be safe.

cues.zh: 这将是一个非常渐进、迭代的设计过程，我们通过设置这些护栏，让系统行为得当。
cues.en: It’s going to be a very progressive, iterative design system where we put those guardrails in such a way that the system behave properly.

cues.zh: 有时它们会做出意料之外的事，因为护栏没设对，我们就去纠正，让它们做对。
cues.en: Sometimes they’re going to do something that was unexpected because the guardrail wasn’t right and we’re dd correct them so that they do it right.

cues.zh: 那种认为我们不能出一点小错、因为一出小错就会死的想法，是荒谬的。
cues.en: The idea somehow that we can’t get it slightly wrong because if we get it slightly wrong, we’ll die is ridiculous.

cues.zh: 我们就是要逐步推进。
cues.en: We are just going to go progressively.

cues.zh: 这就像——我多次用过的类比——涡轮喷气发动机的设计。
cues.en: It is just going to be, the analogy I’ve used many times is turbojet design.

cues.zh: 我们是怎么让涡轮喷气发动机变得如此难以置信地可靠的？
cues.en: How did we figure out how to make turbojet so unbelievably reliable?

cues.zh: 那些是极其复杂的硬件，有时要在极高的温度下连续运行20个小时，而我们能乘坐双引擎客机以接近音速的速度飞越半个地球。
cues.en: Those are incredibly complex pieces of hardware that run at really high temperatures for 20 hours at a time sometimes, and we can fly halfway around the world on a two-engine jetliner at near the speed of sound.

cues.zh: 这有多不可思议？
cues.en: Like how incredible is this?

cues.zh: 简直难以置信。
cues.en: It’s just unbelievable.

cues.zh: 我们能做到这一点，是因为发明了一条让涡轮喷气发动机安全的通用原则吗？
cues.en: Did we do this because we invented a general principle of how to make turbojets safe?

cues.zh: 不，是花了几十年时间精细调整这些系统的设计，才让它们变得安全。
cues.en: No, it took decades to fine tune the design of those systems so that they were safe.

cues.zh: 通用电气或斯奈克玛之类的公司里，有没有一个专门负责涡轮喷气发动机安全的独立团队？
cues.en: Is there a separate group within General Electric or Snecma or whatever that is specialized in turbojet safety?

cues.zh: 没有。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 设计本身就关乎安全，因为更好的涡轮喷气发动机也是更安全的涡轮喷气发动机，也就是更可靠的那一种。
cues.en: The design is all about safety, because a better turbojet is also a safer turbojet, so a more reliable one.

cues.zh: AI 也是一样。
cues.en: It’s the same for AI.

cues.zh: 你需要专门的规定来保障 AI 安全吗？
cues.en: Do you need specific provisions to make AI safe?

cues.zh: 不需要，你需要打造更好的 AI 系统，它们自然会安全，因为设计上就是为了更有用、更可控。
cues.en: No, you need to make better AI systems, and they will be safe because they are designed to be more useful and more controllable.

cues.zh: 那我们来设想一个系统，一个能极具说服力、能让你相信任何事的 AI 系统。
cues.en: So let’s imagine a system, AI system that’s able to be incredibly convincing and can convince you of anything.

cues.zh: 至少我能想象出这样的系统，也能看出它会像武器一样，因为它能操控人的思想。
cues.en: I can at least imagine such a system, and I can see such a system be weapon like because it can control people’s minds.

cues.zh: 我们很容易轻信。
cues.en: We’re pretty gullible.

cues.zh: 我们总想相信某件事，而你可以有一个 AI 系统来控制这一点，你也能看到政府把它当武器用。
cues.en: We want to believe a thing, and you can have an AI system that controls it and you could see governments using that as a weapon.

cues.zh: 那么你觉得，如果设想出这样的系统，它和核武器之类的东西有相似之处吗？
cues.en: So do you think if you imagine such a system, there’s any parallel to something like nuclear weapons?

cues.zh: 没有。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 为什么这项技术不一样？
cues.en: Why is that technology different?

cues.zh: 所以你是说会逐步发展？
cues.en: So you’re saying there’s going to be gradual development?

cues.zh: 逐步发展会是，可能很快，但会是迭代式的，然后我们就能做出响应等等。
cues.en: Gradual development is going to be, it might be rapid, but there’ll be iterative and then we’ll be able to respond and so on.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 可能会——
cues.en: It might be-

cues.zh: 所以那个由普京或他手下设计的AI系统，会去跟每个美国人交谈，试图说服他们投票给——
cues.en: So that AI system designed by Vladimir Putin or whatever, or his minions is going to be talking to, trying to talk to every American to convince them to vote for-

cues.zh: 随便谁。
cues.en: Whoever.

cues.zh: ……随便哪个能让普京满意的人。
cues.en: … Whoever pleases Putin.

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 或者随便什么，或者像他们一直试图做的那样，煽动人们互相对立。
cues.en: Or whatever, or rile people up against each other as they’ve been trying to do.

cues.zh: 它们不会直接跟你对话，而是会跟你的AI助手对话，而你的AI助手会和它们的AI助手一样聪明。
cues.en: They’re not going to be talking to you, they’re going to be talking to your AI assistant, which is going to be as smart as theirs.

cues.zh: 因为正如我所说，未来你跟数字世界的每一次互动，都会由你的AI助手来中介。
cues.en: Because as I said, in the future, every single one of your interaction with the digital world will be mediated by your AI assistant.

cues.zh: 所以你首先会问，这是个骗局吗？
cues.en: So the first thing you’re going to ask, is this a scam?

cues.zh: 这东西跟我说的是真话吗？
cues.en: Is this thing telling me the truth?

cues.zh: 它甚至都接触不到你，因为它只会跟你的AI系统对话，或者跟你的AI系统对话。
cues.en: It’s not even going to be able to get to you because it’s only going to talk to your AI system or your AI system.

cues.zh: 它会像垃圾邮件过滤器一样。
cues.en: It’s going to be like a spam filter.

cues.zh: 你甚至根本看不到那封邮件，那封垃圾邮件。
cues.en: You’re not even seeing the email, the spam email.

cues.zh: 它会被自动放进一个你永远看不到的文件夹里。
cues.en: It’s automatically put in a folder that you never see.

cues.zh: 情况会是一样的。
cues.en: It’s going to be the same thing.

cues.zh: 那个试图说服你相信某件事的AI系统，会去跟AI助手对话，而那个助手至少和它一样聪明，它会说：“这是垃圾信息。”它甚至都不会引起你的注意。
cues.en: That AI system that tries to convince you of something is going to be talking to AI assistant, which is going to be at least as smart as it, and it’s going to say, “This is spam.” It’s not even going to bring it to your attention.

cues.zh: 所以对你来说，任何一个AI系统都很难实现如此大的跨越，以至于能说服其他AI系统。
cues.en: So to you, it’s very difficult for any one AI system to take such a big leap ahead to where it can convince even the other AI systems.

cues.zh: 总会有这种竞争，没人能远远领先。
cues.en: There’s always going to be this kind of race where nobody’s way ahead.

cues.zh: 这就是世界的历史。
cues.en: That’s the history of the world.

cues.zh: 世界历史就是，哪里有了进步，就会有反制措施，这是一场猫鼠游戏。
cues.en: History of the world is whenever there is a progress someplace, there is a countermeasure and it’s a cat and mouse game.

cues.zh: 大多数情况下是这样，但这就是核武器如此有趣的原因，因为它是一种如此强大的武器，谁先得到它至关重要。
cues.en: Mostly yes, but this is why nuclear weapons are so interesting because that was such a powerful weapon that it mattered who got it first.

cues.zh: 你可以想象希特勒、斯大林、毛泽东先得到这种武器，那对美国先得到武器的影响会有所不同。
cues.en: That you could imagine Hitler, Stalin, Mao getting the weapon first, and that having a different kind of impact on the world than the United States getting the weapon first.

cues.zh: 但对你来说，核武器，你不觉得会有突破性发现，然后像曼哈顿计划那样为AI付出努力吗？
cues.en: But to you, nuclear weapons, you don’t imagine a breakthrough discovery and then Manhattan Project-like effort for AI?

cues.zh: 不。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 不，正如我所说，这不会是一个事件。
cues.en: No, as I said, it’s not going to be an event.

cues.zh: 这将是持续不断的进展。
cues.en: It’s going to be continuous progress.

cues.zh: 而一旦出现突破，就会非常迅速地广泛传播。
cues.en: And whenever one breakthrough occurs, it’s going to be widely disseminated really quickly.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 可能首先是在行业内。
cues.en: Probably first within industry.

cues.zh: 这不是一个政府或军事机构特别有创新性的领域，事实上他们远远落后。
cues.en: This is not a domain where government or military organizations are particularly innovative and they’re in fact way behind.

cues.zh: 所以这会来自行业，这类信息传播得极快。
cues.en: And so this is going to come from industry and this kind of information disseminates extremely quickly.

cues.zh: 过去几年我们已经看到了这一点，出现了一个新的……就拿AlphaGo来说，即使没有特别详细的信息，它也在三个月内被复现了，对吧？
cues.en: We’ve seen this over the last few years where you have a new … Even take AlphaGo, this was reproduced within three months even without particularly detailed information, right?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 这是一个不擅长保密的行业。
cues.en: This is an industry that’s not good at secrecy.
But people [inaudible 02:19:22]-

cues.zh: 不。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 但即使有，仅仅是你知道某件事是可能的，这一点就足以让你意识到值得投入时间去真正做它。
cues.en: But even if there is, just the fact that you know that something is possible makes you realize that it’s worth investing the time to actually do it.

cues.zh: 你可能是第二个做这件事的人，但你会做到的。
cues.en: You may be the second person to do it, but you’ll do it.

cues.zh: Transformer 中自监督的所有创新、仅解码器架构、大语言模型，都是如此。
cues.en: And same for all the innovations of self supervision in transformers, decoder only architectures, LLMS.

cues.zh: 这些东西，你不需要确切了解它们的工作原理细节，就能知道它是可行的，因为它已经部署了，然后正在被复现。
cues.en: Those things, you don’t need to know exactly the details of how they work to know that it’s possible because it’s deployed and then it’s getting reproduced.

cues.zh: 然后那些公司的人会流动。
cues.en: And then people who work for those companies move.

cues.zh: 他们从一家公司跳到另一家公司，信息就传播开了。
cues.en: They go from one company to another and the information disseminates.

cues.zh: 美国科技产业、尤其是硅谷的成功，恰恰就在于此，因为信息流通得非常非常快，传播得非常快。
cues.en: What makes the success of the US tech industry and Silicon Valley in particular is exactly that, is because the information circulates really, really quickly and disseminates very quickly.

cues.zh: 所以整个地区因为这种信息流通而领先。
cues.en: And so the whole region is ahead because of that circulation of information.

cues.zh: 也许就顺着 AI 末日论者的心理多聊几句，你用经典的 Yann LeCun 风格给出了一个很好的例子，说明当一项新技术出现时，你说工程师会说：“我发明了这个新东西。
cues.en: Maybe just to linger on the psychology of AI doomers, you give, in the classic Yann LeCun way, a pretty good example of just when a new technology comes to be, you say engineer says, “I invented this new thing.

cues.zh: 我把它叫做圆珠笔。”然后推特上就炸了：“天哪，人们可以用它写下可怕的东西，比如虚假信息、宣传、仇恨言论。
cues.en: I call it a ball pen.” And then the Twitter sphere responds, “OMG people could write horrible things with it, like misinformation, propaganda, hate speech.

cues.zh: 现在就禁了它。”接着写作末日论者登场，跟AI末日论者如出一辙：“想象一下，人人都能拿到一支圆珠笔。
cues.en: Ban it now.” Then writing doomers come in, akin to the AI doomers, “Imagine if everyone can get a ball pen.

cues.zh: 这会毁掉社会。
cues.en: This could destroy society.

cues.zh: 应该立法禁止用圆珠笔写仇恨言论，现在就监管圆珠笔。”然后铅笔行业的巨头说：“没错，圆珠笔非常危险。
cues.en: There should be a law against using ball pen to write hate speech, regulate ball pens now.” And then the pencil industry mogul says, “Yeah, ball pens are very dangerous.

cues.zh: 铅笔写的字能擦掉，圆珠笔写的字却永远留在那里。
cues.en: Unlike pencil writing, which is erasable, ball pen writing stays forever.

cues.zh: 政府应该要求圆珠笔制造商持证经营。”面对新技术时，这似乎确实是人类心理的一部分。
cues.en: Government should require a license for a pen manufacturer.” This does seem to be part of human psychology when it comes up against new technology.

cues.zh: 对此你能谈谈什么深刻的见解吗？
cues.en: What deep insights can you speak to about this?

cues.zh: 嗯，人们对新技术及其可能对社会产生的影响有一种天然的恐惧。
cues.en: Well, there is a natural fear of new technology and the impact it can have in society.

cues.zh: 对于自己所熟悉的世界受到重大变革威胁，人们会本能地做出反应，这些变革要么是文化现象，要么是技术革命。
cues.en: And people have instinctive reaction to the world they know being threatened by major transformations that are either cultural phenomena or technological revolutions.

cues.zh: 他们担心自己的文化，担心自己的工作，担心孩子的未来和生活方式。
cues.en: And they fear for their culture, they fear for their job, they fear for the future of their children and their way of life.

cues.zh: 所以任何变化都令人恐惧。
cues.en: So any change is feared.

cues.zh: 纵观历史，你会发现，任何技术革命或文化现象总是伴随着一些群体或媒体的反弹，基本上把社会当前的所有问题都归咎于那项特定的变革。
cues.en: And you see this along history, any technological revolution or cultural phenomenon was always accompanied by groups or reaction in the media that basically attributed all the current problems of society to that particular change.

cues.zh: 电一度被认为迟早会害死所有人。
cues.en: Electricity was going to kill everyone at some point.

cues.zh: 火车曾被视为可怕的东西，因为时速超过50公里就没法呼吸了。
cues.en: The train was going to be a horrible thing because you can’t breathe past 50 kilometers an hour.

cues.zh: 有个很棒的网站叫“悲观主义者档案”。
cues.en: And so there’s a wonderful website called the Pessimist Archive.

cues.zh: 特别棒。
cues.en: It’s great.

cues.zh: 里面收录了各种报纸剪报，全是人们想象中因技术创新或文化现象而出现的可怕事情，比如爵士乐或漫画书被指责导致失业、年轻人不想工作之类的绝佳例子。
cues.en: Which has all those newspaper clips of all the horrible things people imagine would arrive because of either a technological innovation or a cultural phenomenon, just wonderful examples of jazz or comic books being blamed for unemployment or young people not wanting to work anymore and things like that.

cues.zh: 这种现象已经存在了几个世纪，都是些条件反射式的反应。
cues.en: And that has existed for centuries and it’s knee-jerk reactions.

cues.zh: 问题是，我们是拥抱变化还是抵制变化？
cues.en: The question is do we embrace change or do we resist it?

cues.zh: 真正的危险是什么，而不是想象中的危险？
cues.en: And what are the real dangers as opposed to the imagined ones?

cues.zh: 人们担心，我觉得他们对大型科技公司的一个担忧——这个话题我们反复讨论过，但我觉得值得再提一次——他们担心AI会变得多么强大，也担心它掌握在少数 centralized power 手中，由少数人集中控制。
cues.en: So people worry about, I think one thing they worry about with big tech, something we’ve been talking about over and over, but I think worth mentioning again, they worry about how powerful AI will be and they worry about it being in the hands of one centralized power of just a handful of central control.

cues.zh: 所以这就是对大科技公司的怀疑，这些公司能赚大钱、控制这项技术，借此占便宜、欺负社会中的小人物。
cues.en: And so that’s the skepticism with big tech you make, these companies can make a huge amount of money and control this technology, and by so doing take advantage, abuse the little guy in society.

cues.zh: 嗯，这正是我们需要开源平台的原因。
cues.en: Well, that’s exactly why we need open source platforms.

cues.zh: 对，我就是想把这一点反复强调清楚。
cues.en: Yeah, I just wanted to nail the point home more and more.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 那我来问你，就像我说的，你在网上确实有点锋芒。
cues.en: So let me ask you on your, like I said, you do get a little bit flavorful on the internet.

cues.zh: Joscha Bach 发了条推文，你看到后笑了，是关于 HAL 9,000 的。
cues.en: Joscha Bach tweeted something that you LOL’d at in reference to HAL 9,000.

cues.zh: 原话是：“我理解你的论点，也完全明白你的沮丧，但舱门该开还是该关，是个复杂而微妙的问题。”所以你是 Meta AI 的负责人。
cues.en: Quote, “I appreciate your argument and I fully understand your frustration, but whether the pod bay doors should be opened or closed is a complex and nuanced issue.” So you’re at the head of Meta AI.

cues.zh: 这正是我担心的，我们的 AI 霸主会用这种企业腔调居高临下地跟我们说话，而你用自己的方式在抵抗这一点。
cues.en: This is something that really worries me, that our AI overlords will speak down to us with corporate speak of this nature, and you resist that with your way of being.

cues.zh: 在大公司工作，你能就此发表一下看法吗？如何避免过度恐惧，我想，因过度谨慎而造成伤害？
cues.en: Is this something you can just comment on, working at a big company, how you can avoid the over fearing, I suppose, through caution create harm?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 同样，我认为答案在于开源平台，让广泛多元的人群构建AI助手，这些助手能体现全世界文化、观点、语言和价值体系的多样性，这样你就不会因为单一AI实体而被某种特定思维方式洗脑。
cues.en: Again, I think the answer to this is open source platforms and then enabling a widely diverse set of people to build AI assistance that represent the diversity of cultures, opinions, languages, and value systems across the world so that you’re not bound to just be brainwashed by a particular way of thinking because of a single AI entity.

cues.zh: 所以，我认为这对社会来说是一个非常非常重要的问题。
cues.en: So, I think it’s a really, really important question for society.

cues.zh: 我看到的问题正是如此，这也是为什么我一直如此直言不讳，有时还带点讽刺——
cues.en: And the problem I’m seeing is that, which is why I’ve been so vocal and sometimes a little sardonic about it-

cues.zh: 永远不要停。
cues.en: Never stop.

cues.zh: 永远不要停，Yann。
cues.en: Never stop, Yann.

cues.zh: 我们很喜欢。
cues.en: We love it.

cues.zh: …是因为我认为，通过专有 AI 系统造成的这种权力集中，其危险远大于其他一切。
cues.en: … is because I see the danger of this concentration of power through proprietary AI systems as a much bigger danger than everything else.

cues.zh: 如果我们真的想要 AI 系统有多元观点，那么在将来我们都通过 AI 系统交互的世界里，为了维护思想、信仰、政治观点等的多样性，以及维护民主，我们就需要这些系统是多元的。
cues.en: That if we really want diversity of opinion AI systems, that in the future where we’ll all be interacting through AI systems, we need those to be diverse for the preservation of diversity of ideas and creed and political opinions and whatever, and the preservation of democracy.

cues.zh: 而阻碍这一点的，是那些人——他们认为出于安全考虑，我们应该把 AI 系统锁起来严加看管，因为把它交到所有人手里太危险了，因为它可能被恐怖分子之类的人利用。
cues.en: And what works against this is people who think that for reasons of security, we should keep the AI systems under lock and key because it’s too dangerous to put it in the hands of everybody, because it could be used by terrorists or something.

cues.zh: 那可能导致一个非常糟糕的未来：我们所有的信息摄取都被少数几家公司通过专有系统所控制。
cues.en: That would lead to potentially a very bad future in which all of our information diet is controlled by a small number of companies through proprietary systems.

cues.zh: 所以你相信人类会用这项技术去构建整体上对人类有益的系统。
cues.en: So you trust humans with this technology to build systems that are on the whole good for humanity.

cues.zh: 这不正是民主和言论自由的意义所在吗？
cues.en: Isn’t that what democracy and free speech is all about?

cues.zh: 我想是的。
cues.en: I think so.

cues.zh: 你相信机构会做正确的事吗？
cues.en: Do you trust institutions to do the right thing?

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 你相信人们会做正确的事吗？
cues.en: Do you trust people to do the right thing?

cues.zh: 是的，确实会有坏人做坏事，但他们不会拥有比好人更先进的技术。
cues.en: And yeah, there’s bad people who are going to do bad things, but they’re not going to have superior technology to the good people.

cues.zh: 那么就会是我的好AI对抗你的坏AI，对吧？
cues.en: So then it’s going to be my good AI against your bad AI, right?

cues.zh: 就像我们刚才谈到的例子，也许某个流氓国家会构建某种AI系统，试图说服所有人陷入内战之类的，或者选出一个有利的统治者，但他们必须突破我们的AI系统。
cues.en: There’s the examples that we were just talking about of maybe some rogue country will build some AI system that’s going to try to convince everybody to go into a civil war or something or elect a favorable ruler, but then they will have to go past our AI systems.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 一个带有浓重俄罗斯口音的 AI 系统会试图说服我们——
cues.en: An AI system with a strong Russian accent will be trying to convince our-

cues.zh: 而且句子里不加任何冠词。
cues.en: And doesn’t put any articles in their sentences.

cues.zh: 嗯，那至少会荒谬得好笑。
cues.en: Well, it’ll be at the very least, absurdly comedic.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 既然我们谈到了物理现实，我很想问问你对机器人在这个物理现实中未来的愿景。
cues.en: So since we talked about the physical reality, I’d love to ask your vision of the future with robots in this physical reality.

cues.zh: 你一直在谈论的许多种智能，都会让机器人成为我们人类更高效的协作者。
cues.en: So many of the kinds of intelligence that you’ve been speaking about would empower robots to be more effective collaborators with us humans.

cues.zh: 既然 Tesla 的 Optimus 团队已经向我们展示了一些人形机器人的进展，我觉得这确实让整个行业重新焕发了活力，而我认为 Boston Dynamics 在这个领域已经领先了非常非常久。
cues.en: So since Tesla’s Optimus team has been showing us some progress on humanoid robots, I think it really reinvigorated the whole industry that I think Boston Dynamics has been leading for a very, very long time.

cues.zh: 所以现在有各种各样的公司，Figure AI，当然还有 Boston Dynamics。
cues.en: So now there’s all kinds of companies Figure AI, obviously Boston Dynamics.

cues.zh: Unitree。
cues.en: Unitree.

cues.zh: Unitree，但有很多台。
cues.en: Unitree, but there’s a lot of them.

cues.zh: 有那么几台。
cues.en: There’s a few of them.

cues.zh: 很棒。
cues.en: It’s great.

cues.zh: 很棒。
cues.en: It’s great.

cues.zh: 我很喜欢。
cues.en: I love it.

cues.zh: 那你觉得很快就会有数百万台人形机器人到处走动吗？
cues.en: So do you think there’ll be millions of humanoid robots walking around soon?

cues.zh: 不会很快，但终究会发生。
cues.en: Not soon, but it’s going to happen.

cues.zh: 我认为未来十年机器人领域会非常有意思，机器人产业的兴起已经等了10年、20年，除了预设行为和类似的东西之外，并没有真正兴起。
cues.en: The next decade I think is going to be really interesting in robots, the emergence of the robotics industry has been in the waiting for 10, 20 years without really emerging other than for pre-program behavior and stuff like that.

cues.zh: 主要问题还是莫拉维克悖论，我们如何让这些系统理解世界如何运作并规划行动？
cues.en: And the main issue is, again, the Moravec paradox, how do we get those systems to understand how the world works and plan actions?

cues.zh: 对于非常专门的任务，我们能做到。
cues.en: And so we can do it for really specialized tasks.

cues.zh: Boston Dynamics 的做法基本上是用大量手工打造的动力学模型和精心的预先规划，这是非常经典的机器人技术，有很多创新，也有一点感知，但仍然不行，他们造不出家用机器人。
cues.en: And the way Boston Dynamics goes about it is basically with a lot of handcrafted dynamical models and careful planning in advance, which is very classical robotics with a lot of innovation, a little bit of perception, but it’s still not, they can’t build a domestic robot.

cues.zh: 我们距离完全自动驾驶的L5级别还有一段距离，而且距离拥有一个能像17岁少年那样开20小时车就能自我训练的系统来实现L5级自动驾驶，那更是非常遥远。
cues.en: We’re still some distance away from completely autonomous level five driving, and we’re certainly very far away from having level five autonomous driving by a system that can train itself by driving 20 hours like any 17-year-old.

cues.zh: 所以，除非我们有了世界模型，也就是能够自我训练以理解世界运作方式的系统，否则我们在机器人技术领域不会取得重大进展。
cues.en: So until we have, again, world models, systems that can train themselves to understand how the world works, we’re not going to have significant progress in robotics.

cues.zh: 所以目前很多从事机器人硬件工作的人都在押注或寄希望于AI能在这方面取得足够的进展，
cues.en: So a lot of the people working on robotic hardware at the moment are betting or banking on the fact that AI is going to make sufficient progress towards that,

cues.zh: 他们也希望能从中发现一款产品。
cues.en: And they’re hoping to discover a product in it too.

cues.zh: 因为在拥有真正强大的世界模型之前，会先出现一个近乎强大的世界模型，而人们正试图在一台笨拙的机器人身上找到产品，我想，而不是一台完美高效的机器人。
cues.en: Because before you have a really strong world model, there’ll be an almost strong world model and people are trying to find a product in a clumsy robot, I suppose, not a perfectly efficient robot.

cues.zh: 所以有工厂场景，人形机器人可以帮忙自动化工厂的一些环节。
cues.en: So there’s the factory setting where humanoid robots can help automate some aspects of the factory.

cues.zh: 我觉得这任务难到离谱，因为安全要求太高，还有各种相关问题。
cues.en: I think that’s a crazy difficult task because of all the safety required and all this kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 我觉得家庭场景更有意思，但接着你会想，你刚才提到装洗碗机，对吧？
cues.en: I think in the home is more interesting, but then you start to think, I think you mentioned loading the dishwasher, right?

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我猜这是你们正在攻克的主要问题之一。
cues.en: I suppose that’s one of the main problems you’re working on.

cues.zh: 还有收拾整理、打扫房子、饭后清理餐桌。
cues.en: There’s cleaning up, cleaning the house, clearing up the table after a meal.

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 洗碗，所有这些任务，还有做饭。
cues.en: Washing the dishes, all those tasks, cooking.

cues.zh: 所有这些任务原则上都可以自动化，但实际上极其精密、非常复杂。
cues.en: All the tasks that in principle could be automated but are actually incredibly sophisticated, really complicated.

cues.zh: 但哪怕只是在充满不确定性的空间里做基本导航。
cues.en: But even just basic navigation around a space full of uncertainty.

cues.zh: 也行。
cues.en: That works.

cues.zh: 现在就可以做，导航没问题。
cues.en: You can do this now, navigation is fine.

cues.zh: 但要以对我们人类有吸引力的方式导航，就是另一回事了。
cues.en: Well, navigation in a way that’s compelling to us humans is a different thing.

cues.zh: 是啊，不一定非得……其实我们有演示，因为 fair 有个所谓的具身 AI 团队，他们没自己造机器人，而是用商用机器人。
cues.en: Yeah, it’s not going to be necessarily … We have demos actually, because there is a so-called embodied AI group at fair, and they’ve been not building their own robots, but using commercial robots.

cues.zh: 你可以让机器狗去冰箱那儿，它们真能打开冰箱，还能从里面拿一罐东西之类的，然后给你送过来。
cues.en: And you can tell the robot dog go to the fridge and they can actually open the fridge and they can probably pick up a can in the fridge and stuff like that and bring it to you.

cues.zh: 所以它能导航，能抓取物体——只要训练过识别这些物体，现在的视觉系统已经相当好用了——但它还不是那种完全通用的机器人，还没复杂到能收拾餐桌这种事。
cues.en: So it can navigate, it can grab objects as long as it’s been trained to recognize them, which vision systems work pretty well nowadays, but it’s not like a completely general robot that would be sophisticated enough to do things like clearing up the dinner table.

cues.zh: 对我来说，人形机器人、各种机器人越来越多地进入家庭，这是一个令人兴奋的未来，因为这能让人类在物理空间中真正直接地与AI系统互动。
cues.en: To me, that’s an exciting future of getting humanoid robots, robots in general in the home more and more, because it gets humans to really directly interact with AI systems in the physical space.

cues.zh: 这样一来，我们就能从哲学、心理学层面探索人与机器人的关系。
cues.en: And in so doing it allows us to philosophically, psychologically explore our relationships with robots.

cues.zh: 这会非常、非常、非常有意思。
cues.en: Going to be really, really, really interesting.

cues.zh: 所以我希望你们在JEPA这件事上能尽快取得进展。
cues.en: So I hope you make progress on the whole JEPA thing soon.

cues.zh: 嗯，我希望一切能按计划推进。
cues.en: Well, I hope things can work as planned.

cues.zh: 再说一次，我们研究从视频中自监督学习这个想法已经十年了，但真正取得重大进展只是最近两三年的事。
cues.en: Again, we’ve been working on this idea of self supervised running from video for 10 years, and only made significant progress in the last two or three.

cues.zh: 实际上你提到过，如果没有大量算力，会出现很多有意思的断裂问题。
cues.en: And actually you’ve mentioned that there’s a lot of interesting breakage that can happen without having access to a lot of compute.

cues.zh: 如果你想读这个方向的博士，还有很多可以做出创新的机会。
cues.en: So if you’re interested in doing a PhD in this kind of stuff, there’s a lot of possibilities still to do innovative work.

cues.zh: 你会给想读研、读博的本科生什么建议？
cues.en: So what advice would you give to an undergrad that’s looking to go to grad school and do a PhD?

cues.zh: 其实我已经列过了，就是如何通过观察来训练世界模型这个想法。
cues.en: Basically, I’ve listed them already, this idea of how do you train a world model by observation?

cues.zh: 而且你不一定非要在超大规模数据集上训练。
cues.en: And you don’t have to train necessarily on gigantic data sets.

cues.zh: 但要在像其他模型那样具备涌现能力，可能确实需要在大规模数据集上训练。
cues.en: It could turn out to be necessary, to actually train on large data sets, to have emergent properties like we have with other lamps.

cues.zh: 不过我觉得有很多好想法不一定非要靠扩大规模，比如如何用学到的世界模型来做规划？
cues.en: But I think there is a lot of good ideas that can be done without necessarily scaling up than there is how do you do planning with a learn world model?

cues.zh: 如果系统所处的世界不是物理世界，而是比如互联网，或者某种世界，其中动作是在搜索引擎里搜索、查询数据库、运行仿真、调用计算器或求解微分方程，那你怎么让系统真正规划出一系列动作来给出问题的解？
cues.en: If the world the system evolves in is not the physical world, but is the world of let’s say the internet or some sort of world where an action consists in doing a search in a search engine or interrogating a database or running a simulation or calling a calculator or solving a differential equation, how do you get a system to actually plan a sequence of actions to give the solution to a problem?

cues.zh: 所以规划问题不只是规划物理动作的问题。
cues.en: And so the question of planning is not just a question of planning physical actions.

cues.zh: 它可以是规划使用工具的动作，用于对话系统或任何类型的智能系统。
cues.en: It could be planning actions to use tools for a dialogue system or for any kind of intelligence system.

cues.zh: 这方面有一些研究，但数量不多。
cues.en: And there’s some work on this, but not a huge amount.

cues.zh: FAIR 有一些工作，其中一个叫 Toolformer，是几年前的了，还有一些更近期的规划研究，但我认为我们对这些都还没有好的解决方案。
cues.en: Some work at fair, one called Toolformer, which was a couple years ago and some more recent work on planning, but I don’t think we have a good solution for any of that.

cues.zh: 然后是分层规划的问题。
cues.en: Then there is the question of hierarchical planning.

cues.zh: 我提到的从纽约到巴黎的旅行规划例子就是分层的，但我们采取的几乎每个动作在某种意义上都涉及分层规划，而我们真的完全不知道怎么做。
cues.en: So the example I mentioned of planning a trip from New York to Paris, that’s hierarchical, but almost every action that we take involves hierarchical planning in some sense, and we really have absolutely no idea how to do this.

cues.zh: 在 AI 中还没有任何演示表明，分层规划所需的各种层次的表示已经被学习出来。
cues.en: There’s zero demonstration of hierarchical planning in AI where the various levels of representations that are necessary have been learned.

cues.zh: 我们设计这两个层级时，可以做两层分层规划。
cues.en: We can do two level hierarchical planning when we designed the two levels.

cues.zh: 比如，你有一只机器狗，你想让它从客厅走到厨房。
cues.en: So for example, you have a dog-like robot, you want it to go from the living room to the kitchen.

cues.zh: 你可以规划一条避开障碍物的路径，然后把它发给低层规划器，由后者算出如何移动腿来跟随这条轨迹。
cues.en: You can plan a path that avoids the obstacle, and then you can send this to a lower level planner that figures out how to move the legs to follow that trajectories.

cues.zh: 这样可行，但这种两层规划是手工设计的。
cues.en: So that works, but that two level planning is designed by hand.

cues.zh: 我们要指定合适的抽象层级，以及每个抽象层级上的表示形式。
cues.en: We specify what the proper levels of abstraction, the representation at each level of abstraction have to be.

cues.zh: 这要怎么学习呢？
cues.en: How do you learn this?

cues.zh: 如何学习动作计划的分层表示？
cues.en: How do you learn that hierarchical representation of action plans?

cues.zh: 借助[听不清 02:37:21]和深度学习，我们可以训练系统学习感知的分层表示。
cues.en: With [inaudible 02:37:21] and deep learning, we can train the system to learn hierarchical representations of percepts.

cues.zh: 那如果要表示的是行动计划，对应的又是什么？
cues.en: What is the equivalent when what you’re trying to represent are action plans?

cues.zh: 行动计划，对。
cues.en: For action plans, yeah.

cues.zh: 你想的基本就是一只机器狗或人形机器人，自己开机，从纽约一路跑到巴黎。
cues.en: So you want basically a robot dog or humanoid robot that turns on and travels from New York to Paris all by itself.

cues.zh: 举个例子。
cues.en: For example.

cues.zh: 它可能在TSA那儿会有点麻烦。
cues.en: It might have some trouble at the TSA.

cues.zh: 不，但即便是做相当简单的事，比如家务，像做饭之类的。
cues.en: No, but even doing something fairly simple like a household task, like cooking or something.

cues.zh: 是啊，涉及的东西很多。
cues.en: Yeah, there’s a lot involved.

cues.zh: 这是个超级复杂的任务，而且再一次，我们把它当成理所当然。
cues.en: It’s a super complex task and once again, we take it for granted.

cues.zh: 你对人类的未来抱有什么希望？
cues.en: What hope do you have for the future of humanity?

cues.zh: 我们谈到了那么多令人兴奋的技术，那么多令人兴奋的可能性。
cues.en: We’re talking about so many exciting technologies, so many exciting possibilities.

cues.zh: 展望未来10年、20年、50年、一百年，是什么让你抱有希望？
cues.en: What gives you hope when you look out over the next 10, 20, 50, a hundred years?

cues.zh: 如果你看社交媒体，有战争在发生，有分裂，有仇恨，所有这些也同样是人性的一部分。
cues.en: If you look at social media, there’s wars going on, there’s division, there’s hatred, all this kind of stuff that’s also part of humanity.

cues.zh: 但这一切之中，什么让你抱有希望？
cues.en: But amidst all that, what gives you hope?

cues.zh: 我喜欢这个问题。
cues.en: I love that question.

cues.zh: 我们可以用AI让人类变得更聪明。
cues.en: We can make humanity smarter with AI.

cues.zh: AI基本上会放大人类的智能。
cues.en: AI basically will amplify human intelligence.

cues.zh: 就好像我们每个人都会拥有一群聪明的AI助手。
cues.en: It’s as if every one of us will have a staff of smart AI assistants.

cues.zh: 它们可能比我们更聪明。
cues.en: They might be smarter than us.

cues.zh: 它们会听从我们的指令，也许能以比我们自己好得多的方式执行任务，因为它们比我们更聪明。
cues.en: They’ll do our bidding, perhaps execute a task in ways that are much better than we could do ourselves, because they’d be smarter than us.

cues.zh: 所以这就像每个人都会成为一群超级聪明的虚拟人的老板。
cues.en: And so it’s like everyone would be the boss of a staff of super smart virtual people.

cues.zh: 所以我们不应因此感到受威胁，就像我们不应因为管理一群人中有些人比我们更聪明而感到受威胁一样。
cues.en: So we shouldn’t feel threatened by this any more than we should feel threatened by being the manager of a group of people, some of whom are more intelligent than us.

cues.zh: 我当然有很多这方面的经验，就是有比我更聪明的人和我一起工作。
cues.en: I certainly have a lot of experience with this, of having people working with me who are smarter than me.

cues.zh: 这其实是件大好事。
cues.en: That’s actually a wonderful thing.

cues.zh: 所以，拥有比我们更聪明的机器，在所有任务和日常生活中协助我们，无论是工作还是个人生活，我觉得那绝对是件大好事。
cues.en: So having machines that are smarter than us, that assist us in all of our tasks, our daily lives, whether it’s professional or personal, I think would be an absolutely wonderful thing.

cues.zh: 因为智能是最被需要的商品。
cues.en: Because intelligence is the commodity that is most in demand.

cues.zh: 这就是我的意思。
cues.en: That’s really what I mean.

cues.zh: 人类犯的所有错误，其实都是因为缺乏智能，或者缺乏知识，而这两者是相关的。
cues.en: All the mistakes that humanity makes is because of lack of intelligence really, or lack of knowledge, which is related.

cues.zh: 所以让人变得更聪明，我们只会变得更好。
cues.en: So making people smarter, we just can only be better.

cues.zh: 同理，公共教育是好事，书籍是好事，互联网本质上也是好事，甚至社交网络只要运营得当也是好事。
cues.en: For the same reason that public education is a good thing and books are a good thing, and the internet is also a good thing, intrinsically and even social networks are a good thing if you run them properly.

cues.zh: 这很难，但你能做到。
cues.en: It’s difficult, but you can.

cues.zh: 因为它有助于信息和知识的交流以及知识的传播。
cues.en: Because it helps the communication of information and knowledge and the transmission of knowledge.

cues.zh: 所以 AI 会让人类变得更聪明。
cues.en: So AI is going to make humanity smarter.

cues.zh: 我一直用的类比是，人类历史上或许有一件与 AI 助手普及化可能带来的影响相当的事件，那就是印刷机的发明。
cues.en: And the analogy I’ve been using is the fact that perhaps an equivalent event in the history of humanity to what might be provided by generalization of AI assistant is the invention of the printing press.

cues.zh: 它让每个人都变得更聪明，因为人们能够接触到书籍。
cues.en: It made everybody smarter, the fact that people could have access to books.

cues.zh: 书籍比以前便宜得多，于是更多人有动力学习阅读，而在此之前并非如此。
cues.en: Books were a lot cheaper than they were before, and so a lot more people had an incentive to learn to read, which wasn’t the case before.

cues.zh: 人们因此变得更聪明。
cues.en: And people became smarter.

cues.zh: 它促成了启蒙运动。
cues.en: It enabled the enlightenment.

cues.zh: 没有印刷机就不会有启蒙运动。
cues.en: There wouldn’t be an enlightenment without the printing press.

cues.zh: 它促成了哲学、理性主义、摆脱宗教教条、民主和科学。
cues.en: It enabled philosophy, rationalism, escape from religious doctrine, democracy, science.

cues.zh: 毫无疑问，没有它，就不会有美国革命或法国大革命。
cues.en: And certainly without this, there wouldn’t have been the American Revolution or the French Revolution.

cues.zh: 那样的话，我们可能还处在封建制度之下。
cues.en: And so we would still be under a feudal regimes perhaps.

cues.zh: 它彻底改变了世界，因为人们变得更聪明，学到了各种知识。
cues.en: And so it completely transformed the world because people became smarter and learned about things.

cues.zh: 同时，它也在欧洲引发了长达200年的宗教冲突，因为人们最先读到的是《圣经》，并意识到对《圣经》或许存在与神父所讲不同的解读。
cues.en: Now, it also created 200 years of essentially religious conflicts in Europe because the first thing that people read was the Bible and realized that perhaps there was a different interpretation of the Bible than what the priests were telling them.

cues.zh: 于是这催生了新教运动，造成了分裂。
cues.en: And so that created the Protestant movement and created the rift.

cues.zh: 事实上，天主教会并不喜欢印刷机这个主意，但他们别无选择。
cues.en: And in fact, the Catholic Church didn’t like the idea of the printing press, but they had no choice.

cues.zh: 所以它既有坏影响，也有好影响。
cues.en: And so it had some bad effects and some good effects.

cues.zh: 我不认为今天会有人说印刷机的发明总体上带来了负面影响，尽管它在欧洲引发了200年的宗教冲突。
cues.en: I don’t think anyone today would say that the invention of the printing press had a overall negative effect despite the fact that it created 200 years of religious conflicts in Europe.

cues.zh: 现在，把这个对比一下——我本来很得意能想出这个类比，但后来发现之前已经有人提出过同样的想法——把这个和奥斯曼帝国的情况对比一下。
cues.en: Now, compare this, and I thought I was very proud of myself to come up with this analogy, but realized someone else came with the same idea before me, compare this with what happened in the Ottoman Empire.

cues.zh: 奥斯曼帝国禁止印刷机长达200年，而且不是禁止所有语言，只禁止阿拉伯语。
cues.en: The Ottoman Empire banned the printing press for 200 years, and he didn’t ban it for all languages, only for Arabic.

cues.zh: 在奥斯曼帝国，你其实可以印刷拉丁语、希伯来语或其他语言的书籍，只是不能用阿拉伯语。
cues.en: You could actually print books in Latin or Hebrew or whatever in the Ottoman Empire, just not in Arabic.

cues.zh: 我原以为这是因为统治者只想维持对民众的控制、宗教教条之类的东西。
cues.en: And I thought it was because the rulers just wanted to preserve the control over the population and the religious dogma and everything.

cues.zh: 但和UAE人工智能部长Omar Al Olama聊过之后，他告诉我不是的，还有另一个原因。
cues.en: But after talking with the UAE Minister of AI, Omar Al Olama, he told me no, there was another reason.

cues.zh: 另一个原因是为了保护书法家行会。
cues.en: And the other reason was that it was to preserve the corporation of calligraphers.

cues.zh: 有一种艺术形式，就是用这东西书写优美的阿拉伯诗歌或宗教文本之类的。
cues.en: There’s an art form, which is writing those beautiful Arabic poems or whatever, religious text in this thing.

cues.zh: 那本质上是一个非常强大的抄写员行会，掌控着帝国的很大一部分，我们没法让他们失业。
cues.en: And it was a very powerful corporation of scribes basically that run a big chunk of the empire, and we couldn’t put them out of business.

cues.zh: 所以他们禁止印刷机，部分原因就是为了保护那个行业。
cues.en: So they banned the printing press in part to protect that business.

cues.zh: 那么，今天AI的类比是什么？
cues.en: Now, what’s the analogy for AI today?

cues.zh: 我们禁止AI是在保护谁？
cues.en: Who are we protecting by banning AI?

cues.zh: 那些要求监管AI以保护自己工作的人，又是谁？
cues.en: Who are the people who are asking that AI be regulated to protect their jobs?

cues.zh: 当然，这确实是个真问题：像AI这样的技术变革会对就业市场和劳动力市场产生什么影响？
cues.en: And of course, it’s a real question of what is going to be the effect of a technological transformation like AI on the job market and the labor market?

cues.zh: 有些经济学家比我更懂这个问题，但我和他们聊时，他们告诉我们，我们不会没工作可做。
cues.en: And there are economists who are much more expert at this than I am, but when I talk to them, they tell us we’re not going to run out of the job.

cues.zh: 这不会导致大规模失业。
cues.en: This is not going to cause mass unemployment.

cues.zh: 这只会是不同职业的逐渐转变。
cues.en: This is just going to be gradual shift of different professions.

cues.zh: 10年或15年后会热门的职业，我们今天根本不知道会是什么。
cues.en: The professions that are going to be hot 10 or 15 years from now, we have no idea today what they’re going to be.

cues.zh: 同样，如果回到20年前，20年前谁能想到，甚至5年、10年前最热门的职业是移动应用开发者？
cues.en: The same way, if you go back 20 years in the past, who could have thought 20 years ago that the hottest job, even five, 10 years ago, was mobile app developer?

cues.zh: 那时智能手机还没发明。
cues.en: Smartphones weren’t invented.

cues.zh: 未来大多数工作可能在元宇宙里。
cues.en: Most of the jobs of the future might be in the Metaverse.

cues.zh: 嗯，有可能，是的。
cues.en: Well, it could be, yeah.

cues.zh: 但关键是，你根本无法预测。
cues.en: But the point is you can’t possibly predict.

cues.zh: 但你说得对。
cues.en: But you’re right.

cues.zh: 你提出了很多有力的观点。
cues.en: You made a lot of strong points.

cues.zh: 我相信人性本善。
cues.en: And I believe that people are fundamentally good.

cues.zh: 所以，如果AI，尤其是开源AI，能让人变得更聪明，那只会放大人类内心的善。
cues.en: And so if AI, especially open source AI, can make them smarter, it just empowers the goodness in humans.

cues.zh: 我也有同感，我认为人性本善。
cues.en: So I share that feeling, I think people are fundamentally good.

cues.zh: 事实上，很多末日论者之所以悲观，是因为他们不认为人性本善，他们要么不信任人，要么不信任机构能做出正确的事、让人行为得当。
cues.en: And in fact, a lot of doomers are doomers because they don’t think that people are fundamentally good, and they either don’t trust people or they don’t trust the institution to do the right thing so that people behave properly.

cues.zh: 我想你我都相信人类，我也代表很多人说一句：谢谢你推动开源运动，推动研究和AI开源，让大众能用上，也把模型本身开源。
cues.en: Well, I think both you and I believe in humanity, and I think I speak for a lot of people in saying thank you for pushing the open source movement, pushing to making both research and AI open source, making it available to people, and also the models themselves, making it open source.

cues.zh: 谢谢你。
cues.en: So thank you for that.

cues.zh: 也谢谢你在互联网上，用如此多彩而优美的方式，说出你的想法。
cues.en: And thank you for speaking your mind in such colorful and beautiful ways on the internet.

cues.zh: 希望你别停下来。
cues.en: I hope you never stop.

cues.zh: 你是我认识、也是我崇拜的人里，最有趣的人之一。
cues.en: You’re one of the most fun people I know and get to be a fan of.

cues.zh: Yann，谢谢你再次和我对话，也谢谢你做你自己。
cues.en: So Yann, thank you for speaking to me once again, and thank you for being you.

cues.zh: 谢谢你，Lex。
cues.en: Thank you, Lex.

cues.zh: 感谢收听这次与 Yann LeCun 的对话。
cues.en: Thanks for listening to this conversation with Yann LeCun.

cues.en: To support this podcast, please check out our sponsors in the description.

cues.zh: 现在，让我用 Arthur C. 的一句话来结束。
cues.en: And now, let me leave you with some words from Arthur C.

cues.zh: Clarke。
cues.en: Clarke.

cues.zh: 发现可能之极限的唯一方法，就是越过它们，进入不可能。
cues.en: The only way to discover the limits of the possible is to go beyond them, into the impossible.

cues.zh: 感谢收听，希望下次再见。
cues.en: Thank you for listening and hope to see you next time.
